**Accepted design (developer, 2026-11-21).** Tags: **[Spec]** settled by spec v1.0; **[ADR]** settled by ADR-011/ADR-012; **[Conv]** follows existing code; **[New]** approved in M04-T01.

*Review model* — Prisma `Review`, table `reviews`:

| Field / rule | Definition | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID primary key, `@default(dbgenerated("gen_random_uuid()")) @db.Uuid` | [ADR-011 / Conv] |
| `user_id` | `@db.Uuid`, FK → `users`, **ON DELETE RESTRICT** | [ADR-011 decision 7; Spec §2.2] |
| `landmark_id` | `@db.Uuid`, FK → `landmarks`, **ON DELETE RESTRICT**; internal landmark UUID, never `source_code` | [Spec §2.2, §2.5; ADR-011 decision 8 pattern] |
| `rating` | `INTEGER NOT NULL`; hand-written `reviews_rating_range_check CHECK ("rating" BETWEEN 1 AND 5)` | [Spec §3, §10.1.1]; constraint SQL [New] |
| `body` | `TEXT NULL`; hand-written `reviews_body_length_check CHECK ("body" IS NULL OR char_length("body") BETWEEN 1 AND 2000)` | [Spec §3, §10.1.2]; code-point unit [New, D4] |
| `created_at` | `TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`; never changes | [Conv; Spec §4.2] |
| `updated_at` | `TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL`, declared `@default(now()) @updatedAt` — a database default, unlike the earlier tables — and explicitly assigned `now()` by every successful PATCH | [New, A5 + clarification 2] |
| Uniqueness | Unique `(user_id, landmark_id)` | [Spec §3, §4.1; postgres-prisma skill] |
| Index | `(landmark_id, created_at DESC, id DESC)` | [Spec §5 ordering]; index [New] |
| Back-relations | `reviews Review[]` on `User` and `Landmark` (no columns) | [Conv] |
| Not present | Publication-status column, soft-delete column, stored aggregate columns | [Spec §10.1.4–5]; [New] for aggregates |

*Timestamp semantics (clarification 2).* Every successful PATCH assigns the database's current timestamp (`now()`, the transaction start time, `TIMESTAMP(3)`) to `updated_at`, including a PATCH whose values equal the stored ones. Strict monotonic increase is **not** guaranteed (same-millisecond edits, commit order differing from start order, clock adjustments), nor is `updated_at > created_at`. Nothing depends on it: ordering uses `created_at DESC, id DESC`, reviews have no optimistic concurrency, and clients must not use `updated_at` for ordering or conflict detection. Every raw `UPDATE` must set `updated_at = now()` explicitly, because Prisma's `@updatedAt` is applied only by the Prisma client; M04-T02 must prove this by test.

*Index: pagination vs. aggregate.* The list query (`WHERE landmark_id = $1 ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT … OFFSET …`) matches the index's equality column and order, so PostgreSQL walks the index in order and stops at the limit without a sort (`OFFSET` still walks skipped entries — acceptable here, as for favorites and landmarks). The aggregate (`COUNT(*)`, `AVG(rating)` for one landmark) uses the same index only to locate that landmark's rows; `rating` is not in the index, so every review row of the landmark is read — cost proportional to that landmark's review count. No covering index (`INCLUDE (rating)`) or stored counters are added (premature at this scale); computing on read keeps aggregates correct under concurrent create, edit, and delete (spec §6). The unique `(user_id, landmark_id)` index serves the own-review lookup and the duplicate check. The visibility check, aggregate, and page come from one SQL statement so they share a snapshot.

*Validation (server-side Zod strict objects; the frontend mirrors but is not authoritative).*
- `rating` — required on create; a JSON number that is an integer 1–5; strings (`"5"`), booleans, `null`, fractions, and out-of-range values rejected (JSON `5.0` parses to `5` and is accepted). [Spec §3, test #3]
- PATCH — at least one of `rating`, `body`; an omitted field is unchanged; `body: null` or whitespace-only clears it. [Spec §4.2]
- `body` (D4, A7) — absent or `null` → `null`; otherwise must be a string; reject U+0000 (NUL — PostgreSQL `text` cannot store it, so it would surface as a 500); reject strings that are not well formed (unpaired surrogates, via `String.prototype.isWellFormed()`, available under Node `>=22` — otherwise the driver silently substitutes U+FFFD); trim with `String.prototype.trim()`; empty → `null`; otherwise at most 2,000 **Unicode code points** (`[...body].length`). No NFC/NFKC normalization; internal line breaks preserved (`\r\n` counts as 2); other control characters allowed (rendering is inert). Anything the service accepts satisfies the database CHECK; the CHECK does not repeat the trim, because ECMAScript and PostgreSQL `btrim` whitespace definitions differ.
- Unexpected fields — rejected, including `user_id`, `author_id`, timestamps, `is_own_review`, and aggregate fields. [Spec §6; ADR-012 decision 5]
- IDs — the existing UUID syntax, lower-cased. Pagination — `page` ≥ 1 (default 1), `limit` 1–100 (default **20**, unlike favorites' 50). [Spec §6; Conv]
- Request size — bounded by `express.json()`'s 100 kB default (2,000 code points ≤ ~8 kB); explicit limits are M04-T04's. [Conv]

*Routes (D1 option B, D2 option B2).* `GET /api/v1/landmarks/:landmarkId/reviews` — public, one new GET-only allowlist entry, identical for every caller, never reads the session. Through `mountProtected(apiRouter, "/reviews", …)` only: `POST /api/v1/reviews` (`{ landmark_id, rating, body? }`), `GET /api/v1/reviews?landmark_id=<uuid>` (`{ "review": <safe representation> | null }`), `PATCH /api/v1/reviews/:reviewId`, `DELETE /api/v1/reviews/:reviewId`. Safe representation: `id`, `rating`, `body`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `author_label` (`Community Member`). Create → 201 with the representation; PATCH → 200 with the updated representation; DELETE → 200 `{ "success": true }`; a repeated DELETE → 404.

*Ownership and visibility.* Identity only from `authenticatedUserId`; owner-scoped SQL; missing and non-owned reviews give the same 404 (ADR-012 decisions 2–4). *Visible* = exists, `is_active`, and `sensitivity_status = 'PUBLIC'`.

| Operation | PUBLIC, active | SENSITIVE, active | UNREVIEWED, active | Retired | Missing (well-formed UUID) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Public list (any caller) | 200 reviews + aggregate | 404 | 404 | 404 | 404 |
| Create (signed in) | 201; 409 if already reviewed | 404 | 404 | 404 | 404 |
| Own-review lookup (signed in) | 200, review or `null` | 404 (A3) | 404 (A3) | 404 (A3) | 404 |
| PATCH own review | 200 | 404 (A2) | 404 (A2) | 404 (A2) | — |
| DELETE own review | 200 | 200 | 200 | 200 | — |
| PATCH/DELETE another user's review or a missing review ID | 404 | 404 | 404 | 404 | 404 |
| Any authenticated route without a session | 401 | 401 | 401 | 401 | 401 |

Create is a single statement (visible-landmark CTE → `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (user_id, landmark_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING …`), as favorites' `addFavorite`. DELETE is `DELETE … WHERE id = $review AND user_id = $user` and never joins `landmarks`, so nothing about the landmark can leak. Active non-`PUBLIC` landmarks already return a 200 minimal redacted profile from `GET /landmarks/:id`; their reviews must still return 404, so M04-T03 must not request reviews on a redacted profile or must treat the 404 as "reviews unavailable".

*Error mapping (D3, A1, A2, A4).* Malformed path or body ID → 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` (A1; landmark detail's 404-on-malformed is not followed); invalid review content, an empty PATCH, unexpected or identity fields → 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` (replacing the spec's 422); invalid pagination, missing or malformed lookup `landmark_id`, unexpected query parameters → 400 `INVALID_QUERY`; no or invalid session → 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`; untrusted origin → 403 `INVALID_ORIGIN` (403 never used for ownership); non-visible landmark, missing review, another user's review, or PATCH of one's own review on a non-visible landmark → 404 `NOT_FOUND`; duplicate create → 409 `REVIEW_ALREADY_EXISTS`, plain envelope, no review ID (A4); throttled → 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`; session infrastructure failure → 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`; unexpected protected-route failure → 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR`. Order: origin → session → rate limit → validation → service. Malformed JSON and bodies over 100 kB keep Express's default HTML 400/413 (existing app-wide follow-up).

*Moderation (spec §§1, 8, 10.1.4; A8).* Valid reviews publish immediately; no approval queue, moderator or administrator role, reporting workflow, automatic or AI moderation, or profanity filter; the interface must not imply human moderation. Protection is authentication, CSRF/origin checks, rate limits, validation and size limits, safe text rendering, and author deletion. M04-T04's "approved moderation approach" means exactly these protections. No in-app operator removal: removal by the operator would be a manual database action outside the application.

**Decisions approved by the developer (2026-11-21) and rationale:**
- **D1 — Option B, protected `/reviews` mount.** Spec v1.0's `POST /api/v1/landmarks/:landmarkId/reviews` cannot be protected under ADR-012 (`mountProtected` refuses parameterised paths and protects every method under its path; decision 9 permits only GET-only public entries and rejects route-level `requireSession`). Option B keeps every ADR-012 guarantee with no infrastructure change; it costs a spec §6 amendment. Rejected: A (extend `mountProtected` and the inspector — an ADR-012 amendment to security-reviewed code), C (another prefix — no advantage), D (route-level guard — prohibited).
- **D2 — Option B2, separate authenticated own-review lookup.** Keeps the public list identical and cacheable for all callers, adds no optional-authentication pattern to a public route, and answers "already reviewed?" regardless of pagination (spec §4.1's "Edit your review"). Cost: two requests for a signed-in profile view; spec §§3 and 6 amended. Rejected: B1 (`is_own_review` on the public list), B3 (both).
- **D3 — Align with existing conventions.** 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`/`INVALID_QUERY` replace 422; 404 replaces 403 for ownership; new 409 `REVIEW_ALREADY_EXISTS`. One error vocabulary across favorites and reviews; ownership stays non-disclosing.
- **D4 — Unicode code points, ECMAScript trim, NUL and unpaired-surrogate rejection, no normalization.** The only unit the application and PostgreSQL count identically; avoids a database error (NUL) and silent U+FFFD substitution (surrogates); preserves the user's text.
- **A1** 400 for malformed landmark IDs, including on the public list. **A2** 404 for PATCH of one's own review when the landmark is non-visible. **A3** 404 for the own-review lookup when the landmark is non-visible. **A4** plain 409 without a review ID (the client obtains it from the lookup). **A5** database default on `updated_at` plus explicit assignment on update. **A6** per-user, per-process rate limiting following the favorites pattern; exact limits deferred to M04-T02 for approval; the public list unthrottled like the public landmark routes. **A7** no Unicode normalization. **A8** no in-app operator removal workflow. **A9** M04-T02 owns the schema and migration.
- **Clarification 1** (non-visible review deletion) and **clarification 2** (`updated_at` semantics) — both recorded above and below.

**Accepted limitations:**
- **Non-visible review deletion (clarification 1).** When a landmark becomes retired, `SENSITIVE`, or `UNREVIEWED`, its reviews disappear from the public list and the own-review lookup returns 404, including for the author. The API still permits the author to delete by review ID (spec §§4.2, 7, 10.1.6), but the M04 interface exposes no way to discover that ID, so authors cannot find or delete such a review through the application. The row stays stored, hidden, and excluded from all aggregates. This is consistent with the spec, which requires deletion to be possible and a confirmation step wherever the interface offers deletion, but does not require an interface for non-visible landmarks.
- No in-app operator removal of reviews (A8).
- `updated_at` is not strictly monotonic (clarification 2).
- Review throttling is per process — not shared across instances; resets on restart (A6).
- Multi-code-point emoji count as several characters toward the 2,000 limit (D4).
- The public list inherits the open app-wide follow-up for non-JSON errors on public routes (malformed JSON, oversized bodies, unexpected errors).
- No real landmark is `PUBLIC` (classification policy unresolved and release-blocking), so nothing can be reviewed on real data; end-to-end verification will need guarded synthetic `PUBLIC` fixtures, as in M03-T06.

**Deferred improvements (outside M04's scope):**
- An authenticated, owner-scoped **"My reviews" page** listing the user's reviews, including those on non-visible landmarks — shown only with a generic "Landmark unavailable" label and no name, coordinates, or other metadata — with confirmed deletion. Requires its own specification amendment and approval.
- A covering index or stored aggregates, only if review volume ever makes on-read aggregates measurably slow.

**Carried to later M04 tasks:** M04-T02 — schema and migration (A9), the API, exact rate limits for approval (A6), confirming `server_encoding` is `UTF8` on `landmarks_test`, `landmarks_dev`, and (before release) Render, a test that raw `UPDATE`s set `updated_at`, and the public-list allowlist entry. M04-T03 — the code-point character counter (not `maxLength`, which counts UTF-16 units), "You"/"Your Review" via the lookup, and no review requests for redacted profiles. M04-T04 — explicit size limits and the abuse-protection tests above.

**Status:** **Complete — formally accepted by the developer 2026-11-22** with all increments accepted. Planning authorized 2026-11-22; the plan, its five-increment structure, and decisions R1–R9 approved 2026-11-22 (R5 after clarification); Increments 1a, 1b, 1c, 2, 3, 4, and 5 (documentation and final verification) each authorized and accepted 2026-11-22. **Backend only:** the reviews interface is M04-T03 (Proposed, not started) and the additional abuse, hostile-input, and stress verification is M04-T04 (Proposed, not started). **Git:** not yet committed — by the developer's 2026-11-22 workflow decision, Git checkpoints are now made once per completed milestone, so M04-T02's changes are committed with the M04 milestone checkpoint after M04-T01 through M04-T04 are complete and the milestone is approved. *(Done 2026-11-23: committed in the M04 milestone checkpoint `6006978`, pushed to `origin/main`, GitHub Actions run #28 success.)*

**Approved decisions (developer, 2026-11-22):**
- **R1** reviews limits: 20 mutations (POST, PATCH, DELETE combined) and 120 own-review lookups per user per 60-second fixed window, 10,000-key cap that refuses rather than evicts, 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`; approved as initial limits; the public list is not throttled (A6). **R2(a)** extract a generic per-user limiter, with no favorites behaviour change. **R3** the public list lives in `src/reviews/public-router.ts`, mounted with `apiRouter.use`; `landmarks/router.ts` untouched. **R4** timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds; UTC database configuration verified before implementation. **R5** `average_rating` is a JSON number or `null`, computed as `sum(rating)::float8 / count(*)` with no application rounding (no specification amendment). **R6** foreign keys `ON UPDATE CASCADE`, as favorites. **R7** mutations accept no query parameters; DELETE accepts only an absent or empty body; a repeated lookup parameter is 400 `INVALID_QUERY`. **R8** M04-T02 covers functional, ownership, visibility, CSRF, and non-disclosure testing; hostile inputs, explicit size limits, abuse scenarios, and limiter stress are M04-T04; spec #10 is split between the backend (here) and inert rendering (M04-T03). **R9** a non-normative spec §9 verification note is approved in principle; any specification edit needs separate authorization (not made).

**Final API contract (as implemented and tested):**

| Method and path | Access | Success | Refusals |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/landmarks/:landmarkId/reviews?page&limit` | Public (GET-only allowlist) | 200 `{ reviews, aggregate: { average_rating, rating_count }, page, limit, has_more }` | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` (malformed ID), 400 `INVALID_QUERY`, 404 `NOT_FOUND` |
| `POST /api/v1/reviews` | Session | 201 bare review object | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`/`INVALID_QUERY`, 404, 409 `REVIEW_ALREADY_EXISTS` |
| `GET /api/v1/reviews?landmark_id=` | Session | 200 `{ review }` or `{ review: null }` | 400 `INVALID_QUERY`, 404 |
| `PATCH /api/v1/reviews/:reviewId` | Owner, visible landmark | 200 bare review object | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`/`INVALID_QUERY`, 404 |
| `DELETE /api/v1/reviews/:reviewId` | Owner, any landmark state | 200 `{ "success": true }` | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`/`INVALID_QUERY`, 404 (including a repeat) |

- **Review object:** exactly `id`, `rating`, `body`, `created_at`, `updated_at` (ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds), `author_label` (`"Community Member"`). Never a user ID, email, or landmark data.
- **All authenticated routes:** 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`, 403 `INVALID_ORIGIN` (cookie-bearing writes without trusted origin), 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`, 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR`; every response carries `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. Order: origin → `noStore` → session → limiter → validation → service.
- **Public list:** identical for every caller, never reads the session, no `Cache-Control`, not throttled; newest first (`created_at DESC, id DESC`), `page` default 1, `limit` default 20 and maximum 100; the aggregate covers every review of the landmark; `average_rating` is `null` when `rating_count` is 0.
- **Visibility:** a landmark that is missing, retired, `SENSITIVE`, or `UNREVIEWED` gives the same 404 for the list, create, lookup, and PATCH; DELETE by the owner works whatever the landmark state.

**Accepted limitations and deferred follow-ups (also in §11):**
- **Public API errors outside production.** An unexpected error on a public route (the review list, like `/landmarks`) reaches Express's default handler; outside `NODE_ENV=production` its HTML shows the stack trace, file paths, and the database host and name (verified with an unreachable database; never the password). In production it shows only "Internal Server Error". The app-wide JSON handling of public-route errors remains a follow-up.

- **Bidirectional control characters** are stored exactly; M04-T03 must isolate review text when rendering (for example `dir="auto"` or `<bdi>`).

- **The M01-T04 metadata-only re-import defect** remains open.

**Status:** **Complete — final report accepted and closure approved by the developer 2026-11-22.** Planning authorized and the plan accepted 2026-11-22 with decisions Q1–Q12 (Q4 as amended: format the API's unrounded average to one decimal without reconstructing the rating sum). **Scope:**
- Display landmark ratings and reviews.
- Allow authenticated users to submit feedback.
- Provide validation and error states.
- Support authorized review management.

States: loading, ready, empty ("No reviews yet"), unavailable (the list's 404 — nothing about the landmark is shown), and error with "Try again". "Show more" (Q2) appends the next page, removes duplicates by ID, and moves focus to the first new review (or to the count line when nothing new arrived). **Accepted adjustment:** a failed "Show more" keeps the shown reviews and the button (so focus is not lost), shows an alert, and the same button retries. **Increment 3 (2026-11-22) — the user's own review and creation — ACCEPTED.** `useOwnReview.ts` (the server-derived own-review lookup, keyed to the landmark and signed-in user), `OwnReviewPanel.tsx`, `ReviewForm.tsx`, `testAuth.tsx`. Anonymous visitors get "Sign in to write a review" with a `returnTo` back to the page; a signed-in user without a review gets the "Write a review" form; the user's own entry in the public list is labelled "Your review" by matching the lookup's ID (the API stays identical for every caller). Nothing is shown as posted until the server confirms; the list is refreshed without being cleared. The section now requires the session context, so earlier profile tests were wrapped in providers, and `LandmarkProfilePage.test.tsx` stubs `ReviewsSection` (its own coverage is in `LandmarkProfilePage.reviews.test.tsx`). Frontend unit 1014/1014; Playwright 80/80.

(1) **UI correction:** a success announcement ("Your review was posted/updated/deleted.") is cleared when the session becomes anonymous; switching to another account already cleared it. Drafts and error messages are kept exactly as before (Q6), and authentication and ownership behaviour are unchanged. Three unit tests (sign-out clears it and signing back in does not restore it; an account switch clears it; a session that ends keeps the draft and its message) and one E2E assertion; the sign-out test was confirmed to fail with the fix disabled. (2) **`AccountNav.test.tsx` flake investigated** (not modified; finding under the limitations below). (3) This record, the README "Reviews interface" section, and the §11 status. (4) Requirements traceability below.

**Implemented interface (as delivered):**
- **Placement:** a "Reviews" region (`<section>` labelled by its `h3`) on the full profile of an active `PUBLIC` landmark: rating summary ("4.0 out of 5 · 1 review", or "No reviews yet"), the disclaimer "Reviews are personal opinions. They do not establish public access, legal entry, maintained trails, or safety.", the user's own-review panel, the public list (newest first, 20 per page), a count line, and "Show more reviews".
- **Display:** one-decimal half-up formatting of the API's unrounded average (`formatRating.ts`); each review shows its rating (stars hidden from assistive technology, plus "Rated N out of 5"), "Community Member" (or "You" in the user's own panel; "Your review" in the list), the creation date, and "Edited" when changed. Text is rendered as plain React text in `<p dir="auto">` with `white-space: pre-wrap`: HTML and script-like text is inert, line breaks are kept, and bidirectional text is isolated from the surrounding line.
- **Own review:** anonymous → a sign-in link back to the page; signed in without a review → the "Write a review" form (1–5 star radio group, optional text with a live "N of 2,000 characters" count, "Post review"); with a review → "Your review" with Edit and Delete (accessible names "Edit your review" / "Delete your review"), shown nowhere else.
- **Edit and delete:** edit is prefilled, sends only changed fields (`body: null` clears the text), and has Cancel; delete uses an inline confirmation group ("Delete your review? This can't be undone.") with "Delete review" and Cancel.
- **Failures:** 400 → the server's fixed message; 401 → "Your session has ended…", the session is re-checked, and the draft stays on the page with the sign-in link; 404 → a neutral notice (an edit's text becomes a new-review draft); 409 → the existing review is shown, the unsent text is kept read-only, and "Edit using the text you hadn't posted" carries it into an edit; 429 → the wait time from `Retry-After`; 5xx/network/malformed → a generic retry message. Nothing is shown as saved or deleted before the server confirms; nothing is removed optimistically.
- **Accounts:** a result arriving after a different account signed in is ignored; switching accounts clears every draft, message, and mode; signing out removes every ownership control and (Increment 6) the earlier success announcement, while a draft interrupted by an ended session is kept.

**Accessibility behaviour:** labelled form fields and a fieldset/legend radio group; client validation mirroring the server, with a focused error summary ("There's a problem with your review:") whose links move focus to the field; field errors tied by `aria-describedby`/`aria-invalid`; one polite status region for success announcements and `role="alert"` for failures; busy buttons use `aria-disabled`/`aria-busy` and ignore repeat activation instead of becoming disabled (focus is kept). Focus moves predictably: to the "Your review" heading after posting or saving; to the edit form's heading on Edit; back to Edit on Cancel; to the confirmation prompt on Delete and back to Delete on Cancel; to the "Reviews" heading after a deletion; to the first new review (or the count line) after "Show more". Everything is operable by keyboard (verified in a real browser).

### M04-T04: Implement Review Protection and Moderation

**Status:** **Complete — 2026-11-23** (final report accepted and closure approved by the developer). The read-only plan was accepted 2026-11-22 with decisions D1–D4; Increments 1–4 accepted 2026-11-22 (Increment 2 including one developer-approved CSS correction); Increment 5 (bounded concurrency and stress verification) accepted 2026-11-23, together with a developer-approved correction to the Increment 2 containment test; Increment 6 (final integrity verification, documentation, traceability, and closure preparation) accepted 2026-11-23. All six increments accepted. **Verification-first:** no production-code, schema, migration, API-contract, security-model, ADR, specification, or dependency change is authorized unless separately approved; any defect is reported with a proposed fix before implementation. Committed in the M04 milestone checkpoint `6006978` (2026-11-23; GitHub Actions run #28 success).

**Dependencies:** M04-T02

**Scope:**
- Apply the approved moderation approach.
- Protect against unauthorized modification.
- Test malicious and invalid inputs.
- Verify relevant abuse protections.

**Approved plan (2026-11-22):** six increments — (1) hostile input and request/response size; (2) Unicode edge cases with frontend/server validation parity and real-browser rendering checks; (3) authorization and information-disclosure regression matrix; (4) rate-limit and abuse scenarios; (5) bounded concurrency and stress; (6) integrity, documentation, and closure. The moderation approach is already settled by ADR-013 decision 9 (immediate publication; no queue, roles, reporting, filters, or in-app operator removal), so this task verifies rather than adds moderation. **Decisions:** **D1** zero-width-only text stays valid under the existing `trim()` contract — pinned by tests and documented, with no new rejection rule or warning; **D2** the application-wide 100 kB JSON parser limit is the explicit request-size limit; **D3** bounded, deterministic stress verification without latency thresholds, investigating PostgreSQL plan choices rather than requiring an unconditional index, and kept separately runnable if it materially slows the default suite; **D4** per-IP and multi-account abuse remain accepted limitations (per-user limits, R1/A6). **Guidance:** compare security-relevant response properties rather than dynamic headers.

**Increment 1 (2026-11-22) — hostile input and request/response size — ACCEPTED.** New `backend/tests/reviews-hostile.integration.test.ts` (23 tests; real application and real reviews limiter, rotating fresh accounts because the limiter counts before validation). No production change and no review-specific defect. Results: new file 23/23 in nine consecutive runs; backend integration 489/489 (31 files; route inventory 15/15, route guard 14/14, reviews security 31/31); backend unit 328/328; Playwright 93/93 (run separately); backend build and type checks, ESLint, a strict temporary type check of the reviews tests, and root Prettier clean; `landmarks_dev` unchanged; no fixture leftovers. **Accepted findings:**
- **Request boundaries:** the parser limit is exact — 102,400 bytes accepted (the review created), 102,401 refused with 413, for POST and PATCH and for chunked bodies without `Content-Length`; a 102,400-byte request with an over-long `body` gets the reviews 400 ("body must be at most 2,000 characters."), so parser acceptance and schema validation are distinct layers. gzip is accepted and limited by its DECOMPRESSED size (a 1 MB gzip bomb under 100 kB on the wire is 413); other encodings are 415.
- **Existing Express HTML error pages (app-wide follow-up, not a reviews defect):** parser-generated 400 (malformed JSON, strict-mode top-level values), 413, and 415 (charset or encoding), and Express's own URL-decoding failure (malformed `%`-encoding, 400) on the public list and on protected routes — where the M03-T04 protected-route error handler passes 4xx errors on by design, keeping `private, no-store`. Outside production the page includes the stack trace; in production only the status text (verified for 400, 413, 415).
- **UTF-7:** `charset=utf-7` is accepted by the current parser (body-parser accepts any decodable `utf-*` charset), so ASCII `+ADw-b+AD4-` arrives as `<b>`; validation (characters, length) applies to the DECODED text and storage and responses remain inert UTF-8 JSON — no bypass.
- **`__proto__` query keys** are dropped by Express's query parser before review validation (no pollution; `toString`-style keys are still refused) — a narrow discrepancy with R7's "no other query parameters".
- **Hostile corpus:** 50 inputs × 5 positions (text, `landmark_id`, `rating`, field name, path ID / `page`); every response is either the exact spec §4.1 outcome or a fixed message — never 5xx, never reflected, no internal detail. Malformed JSON, 40,000-level nesting, duplicate keys (last value wins), and numeric literals (`4.0`, `4e0`, `0.4e1`, `4.0000000000000001` accepted as 4; `1e400`, `-0`, `4.5`, `"4"`, and others refused) behave as defined; oversized and malformed IDs and queries keep the existing fixed 400s; Node itself answers 431 above its 16 KB request-line limit.
- **Response size:** 100 maximum-length reviews whose bodies are six-byte JSON escapes, at `limit=100`, measured **1,218,203 bytes** against a computed worst-case bound of **1,218,226 bytes** (envelope 127 + 100 × 12,180 + 99 separators; at most 6 bytes per code point in JSON); pagination, order, and data intact.
- **Cost:** the file adds about 28 seconds to the integration suite (mostly account creation for limiter rotation).

**Increment 2 (2026-11-22) — Unicode edge cases, validation parity, browser rendering — ACCEPTED.** One shared, ASCII-only corpus of 43 explicitly defined cases (`frontend/src/reviews/testdata/unicodeReviewCorpus.json`, code points written as `U+XXXX`; test data only) drives the frontend validator (`frontend/src/reviews/unicodeParity.test.ts`, 89 tests, including the fallback for browsers without `String.prototype.isWellFormed`), the server validator (`backend/tests/reviews-unicode.test.ts`, 45), and the real API and database (`backend/tests/reviews-unicode.integration.test.ts`, 3). Each side decodes the corpus independently and both pin the same fingerprint. Groups: zero-width only (kept — **D1 pinned**); characters removed by `trim()` (U+FEFF, U+00A0, U+3000, U+2028/2029, Zs spaces, tab/CR/LF/VT/FF) and kept by it (U+0085, U+180E); noncharacters and private use; combining marks and emoji sequences (no normalization); exactly 2,000 versus 2,001 code points (ASCII, astral, zero-width, combining; counted after trimming); line breaks; NUL and unpaired surrogates (rejected before trimming). **No frontend/server disagreement.** PostgreSQL stores exactly the expected text and its `char_length` equals the API's code-point count. Browser checks (`e2e/reviews.spec.ts`): zero-width-only text accepted end to end through the form and rendered inert; at 320 px, 2,000-code-point unbroken, URL-like, emoji, and combining-mark reviews cause no horizontal overflow and the review controls stay usable. **Defect found and fixed (developer-approved CSS correction):** valid text of stacked combining marks ("a" + 1,999 U+0301) painted about 5,400 px of glyph ink upward, over the disclaimers, map, heading, and site header (layout, overflow, and hit-testing were unaffected). `frontend/src/reviews/ReviewsSection.module.css` `.body` now has `overflow: hidden` with `padding-block: 0.25em` replacing the former 0.25rem top margin (same top spacing; 4 px more below), keeping `pre-wrap` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere`. A new browser test asserts containment deterministically (computed clipping and wrapping, nothing cut off, the stacked marks' measured ink far exceeding their box, ordinary accents fitting inside it, three-line text intact) and, as a supplement, byte-identical same-browser screenshots of the header, heading, map, and both disclaimers; it failed against the previous CSS on both checks. Results: frontend unit 1141/1141; backend unit 373/373; backend integration 492/492; Playwright 96/96; axe 36 scans, 0 violations; type checks, builds, ESLint, root Prettier clean; `landmarks_dev` unchanged; no fixture leftovers. **Accepted limitations:** pathological combining marks are visually clipped (the full text remains in the data, the editor, and the accessibility tree); cross-browser and cross-platform font measurements are deferred; marks may still overlap other lines of the same review; earlier M04 test files that contain literal invisible characters are left unchanged.

**Increment 3 (2026-11-22) — authorization and information-disclosure regression — ACCEPTED.** New `backend/tests/reviews-disclosure.integration.test.ts` (11 tests; test-only, no production change). A table-driven matrix of **164 cells** — the five review endpoints × anonymous, owner, other user, and the owner's EXPIRED session × PUBLIC, retired, SENSITIVE, UNREVIEWED, and missing landmarks × the caller's own, another user's, and a nonexistent review (36 cells per existing landmark, 20 for a missing one) — plus cross-cutting tests, comparing security-relevant properties (status, exact body bytes, a fixed header set) rather than dynamic headers. **No review-specific authorization or information-disclosure defect.** Verified: identical 401s for anonymous and expired callers; another user's review indistinguishable from a nonexistent one for edit and delete; hidden landmarks byte-identical to a missing one for list, lookup, create (404, never 409), and edit; owners can delete their own review in every landmark state (the documented exception) without landmark data, and a repeat equals a nonexistent ID; malformed input refused before lookup (400; 401 first for anonymous callers on protected routes); untrusted origins 403 identically for existing and unknown reviews; exact field allowlists (list envelope, six review fields, the `{ review }` wrapper); no landmark metadata, coordinates, emails, user IDs, other users' text, or internals in any response; `private, no-store` on every protected response (200, 401, 403, 404, 409, 429, 500); the public list byte-identical for six caller types and never setting a cookie; 429 identical for own, other, and unknown reviews. Captured logs contained no review text, emails, IDs, cookies, landmark data, stacks, or SQL; a forced failure logged only its event code and error class. Three temporary production faults (an extra identity field, no-store removed, a caller-varying public list) were each detected and restored byte-identical. Results: backend integration 503/503; backend unit 373/373; Playwright 96/96; builds, type checks, ESLint, root Prettier clean; `landmarks_dev` unchanged; no fixture leftovers. **Accepted observations:** Better Auth may clear an expired session cookie (empty value, `Max-Age=0`) while returning the same 401 body; public-list 500s use Express's default HTML page (existing app-wide follow-up); timing side channels were not measured; per-process limiting remains an accepted limitation.

**Increment 4 (2026-11-22) — rate-limit and abuse verification — ACCEPTED.** New `backend/tests/reviews-abuse.integration.test.ts` (8), `backend/tests/reviews-rate-limit-capacity.test.ts` (3, unit), and one real-limiter test in `e2e/reviews.spec.ts`; no production change — **the limiter conforms to R1.** Verified on the real routers and protected mount with an injected controlled clock at the approved limits: the window opens at the first allowed request; `Retry-After` = max(1, ceil(remaining seconds)) at every transition (30 → 29 at +31.000 s, 2 at +58.999 s, 1 from +59.000 s to +59.999 s); a new window opens at exactly +60.000 s with a full quota; blocked requests neither count nor extend the window; admitted requests count whatever their outcome (400, 404, 409), while 401 and 403 never reach the limiter; a 429 changes no row, timestamp, or list; mutation and lookup buckets, and users, are independent; the public list is never throttled; at the key cap a NEW key is refused fail-closed (`Retry-After` 60), live keys are never evicted, one event-code log line is written per fill, and keys are freed exactly when their windows expire — at the real 10,000-key default in a 0.25 s unit test (default suite). On the REAL application: 50 concurrent mutations by one user → exactly 20 admitted and 30 × 429, admitted ones receiving their normal outcomes (400, 404, 200, 201, at most one 201 then 409 for one landmark) with row counts matching exactly and no 5xx; 150 concurrent lookups → exactly 120 × 200 and 30 × 429. Real browser: after a dedicated account spends its real quota, posting shows "Too many requests. Please try again in N seconds." from the server's `Retry-After`, as an alert, with the draft and rating kept and nothing created. Results: backend unit 376/376; backend integration 511/511; Playwright 97/97; axe 0 violations; builds, type checks, ESLint, root Prettier clean; `landmarks_dev` unchanged; no fixture leftovers. **Noted (as designed):** capacity refusals always state `Retry-After: 60`; a capacity refusal can reach a user who has made no request; malformed requests consume quota.

**Increment 5 (2026-11-22; accepted 2026-11-23) — bounded concurrency and stress — ACCEPTED.** New `backend/tests/reviews-stress.integration.test.ts` (4 tests; test-only, no production, index, query, or schema change), in the default integration suite. It never truncates: every row it creates is tracked and deleted explicitly (reviews, favorites, sessions, accounts, users, landmarks), and `afterAll` asserts that the row counts of users, accounts, sessions, landmarks, reviews, favorites, and verifications equal their values before the file ran, so unrelated data in `landmarks_test` is untouched. Findings:
- **Pagination and aggregate:** 1,000 synthetic users and reviews with deterministic IDs on one landmark (every third review shares a timestamp, exercising the `id` tie-break); 11 pages at `limit=100` return exactly the 1,000 IDs in PostgreSQL's `created_at DESC, id DESC` order with no gap or duplicate; `has_more` true on pages 1–9 and false on page 10, page 11 empty; the aggregate identical on every page (`rating_count` 1000, `average_rating` 3, equal to PostgreSQL's `sum / count`).
- **Query plans (recorded, not asserted, per D3):** the composite index `reviews_landmark_id_created_at_id_idx (landmark_id, created_at DESC, id DESC)` exists. With all reviews on one landmark the planner chooses a sequential scan and sort (524 buffer hits, about 0.6 ms) — with sequential scans disabled it uses a bitmap scan of the unique `(user_id, landmark_id)` index (351 hits, 0.69 ms). With a selective distribution (10,000 reviews, 10% on the landmark; inserted inside a transaction that was rolled back) it uses a bitmap scan of the composite index for that landmark's 1,000 rows and then sorts (356 hits, about 0.6 ms). An experimental `WHERE landmark_id = $1` page (not production code) reads only 101 rows in index order (10 hits, 0.04 ms). A drift guard checks that the EXPLAIN SQL still matches `backend/src/reviews/repository.ts`; `ANALYZE reviews` was run (statistics only).
- **Accepted optimization follow-up (not a defect):** the production list query selects the page with `landmark_id IN (SELECT id FROM visible)`, so each page reads and sorts all of a landmark's reviews instead of reading only the requested page in index order; the aggregate needs every row anyway, so a rewrite could save at most the page half. Acceptable at the verified scale; any change needs its own approval (candidate for M07-T04).
- **Mixed concurrency:** 30 real accounts, 300 mutations in two concurrent phases (10 per user, within the limit of 20) with 100 concurrent public-list readers. Phase A: 120 creates plus 30 racing duplicates → exactly 120 × 201 and 30 × 409 (one 201 per user and landmark). Phase B: 90 edits and 60 deletes, each user's edit racing the delete of the same review → every delete 200, every other edit 200, and the racing edit 200 or 404 (one 404 observed in one run). No 5xx, no 429, no constraint violation. Afterwards exactly 60 rows remain, each the review that user's create returned carrying that user's edit; no duplicate `(user_id, landmark_id)` pair; every API aggregate equals PostgreSQL's recalculation; all 100 readers 200 and internally consistent.
- **Connection-pool pressure:** 100 concurrent list requests (pages 1–10 of the 1,000-review landmark) against the default pool of 10: all 200 and well-formed, identical pages byte-identical; latency recorded without thresholds (about 0.3 s total; min 135, median 225, p95 298, max 301 ms — queueing, no errors).
- **Runtime and placement:** about 10.3 s per file (1,000-row seed 0.3 s, pagination 0.09 s, 30 sign-ups 6.1 s, each phase about 0.7 s, pool 0.3 s, cleanup 0.2 s) — about 5–6% of the integration suite; kept in the default suite, and runnable on its own by path. Cleanup removed 1,060 reviews, 30 sessions, 30 accounts, 1,030 users, and 5 landmarks.
- **Results:** stress file 4/4 in six runs; backend unit 376/376; backend integration 515/515 (35 files); builds, type checks (including the strict reviews-tests check), ESLint, root Prettier clean; `landmarks_dev` unchanged; no fixture leftovers.

**Containment-test correction (developer-approved 2026-11-23, test-only).** The full Playwright suite failed 96/97 in both Increment 5 runs on the *supplementary* pixel comparison of the Leaflet map in the Increment 2 combining-mark containment test ("map is unchanged"; 10/10 when run alone): the map's rendering is not byte-stable between page loads under full-suite load. `e2e/reviews.spec.ts` now compares only the static regions — site header, page heading, access disclaimer, reviews disclaimer — with a comment explaining the exclusion; every deterministic containment assertion is unchanged. No production CSS or application code changed. **Negative control:** with `overflow: hidden` removed from `.body` and the frontend rebuilt (the Playwright server serves the built bundle), a temporary copy of the test with the overflow and pixel assertions made soft failed 3 of 3 runs, each of the four retained regions failing every time and the deterministic overflow checks failing for every review body; the CSS was then restored (identical SHA-256), the frontend rebuilt, and the temporary copy deleted. Results: focused test 10/10; full Playwright 97/97 in three consecutive runs; root Prettier, e2e ESLint, and the e2e type check clean; no fixture leftovers; `landmarks_dev` unchanged.

## Milestone 05: Trip Planning

**Objective:** Allow users to organize multiple landmarks into saved geographic itineraries.

**Related Requirements:** FR-06, FR-11, FR-12

### M05-T01: Define Trip Planning Behavior

**Status:** **Complete — 2026-11-23** (design task; closed by the developer after the final approval sequence). Planning authorized 2026-11-23; the planning review, decisions T1–T16, and seven clarifications (with a PostgreSQL probe) approved by the developer 2026-11-23; **Increment 1 (documentation)** drafted 2026-11-23, conditionally accepted subject to targeted corrections, corrected, and **accepted 2026-11-23**. The developer then, on 2026-11-23, **approved `specs/TRIP_PLANNING_SPEC.md` v1.1** (now the current approved specification; v1.0 superseded, its replaced text preserved in the spec's §11), **accepted ADR-014** (status Accepted), accepted the documented API response contracts, accepted the existing Markdown formatting conventions without a Prettier rewrite, and **closed M05-T01**. Design-only: no application code, Prisma schema, migration, test, or dependency change. Uncommitted — the Git checkpoint is deferred until Milestone 05 is complete (developer workflow decision of 2026-11-22).

**Dependencies:** M00-T01

**Scope:**
- Establish itinerary requirements.
- Define stop ordering and trip ownership.
- Clarify geographic distance calculations.
- Define expected map interactions.
- Exclude unsupported trail navigation assumptions.

**Approach:** `specs/TRIP_PLANNING_SPEC.md` v1.0 (approved 2026-10-29) already defined most trip behavior, so — like M04-T01 for reviews — M05-T01 reconciles it with ADR-011 to ADR-013, fills the gaps the scope names (distance, map), and records the result as **Specification 5 v1.1** (replaced v1.0 text preserved in its §11) and **ADR-014** — drafted as an approval candidate and a Proposed record, and approved and accepted by the developer on 2026-11-23.

**Approved decisions (2026-11-23; full text in ADR-014 and spec v1.1):**
- **T1 Baseline:** keep Spec 5's substance; amend only for alignment, clarification, and gaps. No approved functionality removed — **sharing stays in scope**; navigation, directions, travel distances and times, route lines, and route optimization stay out of scope.
- **T2 Routes:** owner routes only through `mountProtected` at `/trips`; `GET /api/v1/shared/trips/:shareToken` is the single new GET-only public allowlist entry (compatible with ADR-012 as written).
- **T3 Errors:** reviews' error vocabulary plus `409 TRIP_STOP_ALREADY_EXISTS`, `TRIP_STOP_LIMIT_REACHED`, `TRIP_VERSION_CONFLICT`, `TRIP_SHARING_UNAVAILABLE`; Spec 5's `204` responses kept.
- **T4 Concurrency (clarification 1):** every mutation locks the owner's trip row first; add counts and appends under the lock with the visibility check and `ON CONFLICT (trip_id, landmark_id)`; remove and reorder rewrite positions in single statements; `version` required on reorder (as approved), optional on rename (additive); every mutation increments `version` and sets `updated_at`.
- **T5 Names (clarification 2):** well-formed → `trim()` → no control or line-separator characters anywhere (tabs, CR, LF, NUL, U+0085, U+2028/2029 included) → at least one Letter/Number/Punctuation/Symbol code point (combining marks, variation selectors, zero-width and format characters alone do not count; emoji sequences count) → 1–100 code points; frontend/backend parity tests over a shared corpus. **Tightening** of the v1.0 rule.
- **T6–T7 Representations (clarification 3):** landmark fields (`id`, `display_name`, `category`, `latitude`, `longitude`) only for stops whose landmark is currently active and `PUBLIC`, checked at read time and redacted server-side before serialization, in both the owner and shared views (the owner view thus also hides `UNREVIEWED` — an alignment of §5.3 with §4).
- **T8 Distances (clarification 4):** PostGIS geodesic legs between adjacent stops only when both are available — never across or around an unavailable stop; `distance_summary { total_miles, measured_legs, total_legs }`, partial when `measured_legs < total_legs`; always labelled straight-line, not travel distance. New behavior.
- **T9 Map:** list primary; supplementary map of available stops as numbered markers; no lines between stops.
- **T10 Throttling:** 60 mutations and 120 reads per user per minute (per process); the shared route not throttled.
- **T11 Sharing gate (clarification 5):** SHA-256-hashed 256-bit tokens; `TRIP_SHARING_ENABLED` (off by default in production). **Release blockers for production sharing:** the sensitive-location classification policy and initial review, and the review of share-token exposure in hosting and proxy access logs. The setting does not by itself satisfy either; production enablement also needs the developer's explicit approval.
- **T12–T13:** list fields (`id`, `name`, `stop_count`, `updated_at`, `is_shared`); add-to-trip picker with "New trip" as create-then-add.
- **T14 Task ownership (clarification 6):** sharing endpoints → M05-T03; sharing UI and shared page → M05-T06 (scopes below). Nothing deferred.
- **T15 Offline:** no offline work in M05; responses compatible with Specification 6 snapshots.
- **T16 Data model (clarification 7):** RESTRICT to users and landmarks, CASCADE from trips; `CHECK (position >= 0)`; ordinary `UNIQUE (trip_id, landmark_id)`; **`UNIQUE (trip_id, position) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE`**, hand-written in the migration and preserved by every future migration (catalog test required).

**PostgreSQL probe (2026-11-23, PostgreSQL 17.5, `landmarks_test`, scratch schema created and dropped; no repository or `landmarks_dev` change):** a single-statement reversal of three positions fails with an ordinary unique constraint and succeeds with `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE`; `ON CONFLICT (trip_id, landmark_id)` works beside it, and PostgreSQL refuses a deferrable constraint as an arbiter; under the trip-row lock, concurrent appends got positions 0 and 1, concurrent duplicate appends produced one stop, and concurrent appends to a 25-stop trip were both refused.

**Increment 1 (2026-11-23) — documentation — ACCEPTED 2026-11-23.** `specs/TRIP_PLANNING_SPEC.md` v1.1 (drafted as an approval candidate: amended §§1, 3–8, 10; new §§5.1.1, 5.6, 6.4, 7.1–7.3, 10.6, 11; acceptance tests #23–#31 added, #1–#22 unchanged); ADR-014 (drafted as Proposed) in `docs/DECISIONS.md`; `specs/README.md`; this record and the clarified M05-T02 to M05-T06 scopes.

**Increment 1 corrections (2026-11-23, after conditional acceptance):** the Spec 5 §7 example owner response replaced by a v1.1 example (available and unavailable stops, a measured and an unmeasured leg, a partial total; category slugs `falls`/`arch` as the discovery API emits them), with the v1.0 example preserved in spec §11; the stale Project Phase line in `docs/DECISIONS.md` corrected; the Specification 7 share-token access-log amendment tracked under M07-T05. **API convention review (no contract change):** the trip list `{ trips, page, limit, has_more }` matches the favorites and reviews lists; `201 { stop }` follows Spec 5's own `{ trip }` wrapper (reviews' create returns a bare object and their lookup a `{ review }` wrapper, so the project has no single creation-response convention); `200 { share_url }` updates an existing trip's sharing state rather than creating a resource; Spec 5's approved `204` responses differ from reviews' and favorites' `200` bodies, and the current frontend `requestJson` helper requires a JSON body, so M05-T04/M05-T06 must add a no-content request helper to `frontend/src/api/client.ts`; Spec 5's `is_available` redaction marker (approved in v1.0) differs from favorites' `availability: "redacted"`. None of these conflicts with ADR-012 or requires changing the approved contract.

**Acceptance criteria** (derived from the task scope in the M05-T01 planning review and accepted with the task, 2026-11-23; the plan previously listed none):
- [x] **Itinerary requirements established** — Specification 5 v1.1 §§1–8 and acceptance tests #1–#31; sharing preserved (§5.4).

### M05-T02: Design Trip Data Model

**Status:** **Complete — 2026-11-23** (closed by the developer after Increment 2). Planning authorized 2026-11-23; the plan and decisions D1–D7 approved 2026-11-23; Increments 1a (preparation and review), 1b (`landmarks_test`), 1c (`landmarks_dev`), and 2 (documentation and closure) accepted 2026-11-23. Schema, migration, and schema tests only — no API, service, frontend, or sharing code; no dependency change; Specification 5 v1.1 and ADR-014 unchanged. Uncommitted — the Git checkpoint is deferred until Milestone 05 is complete.

**Dependencies:** M03-T01, M05-T01

**Scope:**
- Define trips and ordered trip stops.
- Establish relationships and constraints.
- Define ownership and modification rules.

**Clarified scope (M05-T01, accepted 2026-11-23; spec v1.1 §3, ADR-014 decision 14):** `trips` and `trip_stops` under ADR-011 conventions, including the SHA-256 `share_token_hash` and `version`; RESTRICT/CASCADE foreign keys; `CHECK (position >= 0)` and the name-length CHECK; ordinary `UNIQUE (trip_id, landmark_id)`; **`UNIQUE (trip_id, position) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE`** hand-written in the reviewed migration, with a catalog test of its deferrability and confirmation that Prisma's tooling leaves it intact; applied to `landmarks_test` before `landmarks_dev` (ADR-010).

**Approved plan and decisions (2026-11-23):** Prisma models `Trip` (`trips`) and `TripStop` (`trip_stops`) under ADR-011 conventions, with back-relations `User.trips` and `Landmark.tripStops` (no columns); four increments with an approval boundary after each. **D1** a database backstop for the 25-stop limit (`CHECK (position BETWEEN 0 AND 24)` plus the position unique); **D2** contiguity enforced by the service, not by a trigger; **D3** declare `@@unique([tripId, position])` in the Prisma schema, subject to the Increment 1b compatibility check; **D4** the share hash as `TEXT` with a lowercase-hex format CHECK; **D5** a length-only name CHECK (the full name rule stays in the service); **D6** `CHECK (version >= 0)`; **D7** constraint behaviour tested here, the locking procedure and concurrent-request behaviour tested in M05-T03.

**What was built** (`backend/prisma/schema.prisma`; migration `backend/prisma/migrations/20261123000000_trips/` — `migration.sql` and a recovery-only `down.sql`):
- `trips(id uuid PK default gen_random_uuid(), user_id uuid → users ON DELETE RESTRICT, name text, version integer default 0, share_token_hash text NULL, created_at / updated_at timestamp(3) default CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)`; unique `trips_share_token_hash_key`; index `trips_user_id_updated_at_id_idx (user_id, updated_at DESC, id DESC)`; CHECKs `trips_name_length_check` (`char_length(name)` 1–100), `trips_version_check` (`version >= 0`), `trips_share_token_hash_format_check` (NULL or `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`).
- `trip_stops(id uuid PK, trip_id uuid → trips ON DELETE CASCADE, landmark_id uuid → landmarks ON DELETE RESTRICT, position integer, created_at timestamp(3))`; ordinary unique index `trip_stops_trip_id_landmark_id_key`; unique constraint `trip_stops_trip_id_position_key` **`DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE`**; CHECK `trip_stops_position_check` (`position` 0–24). All foreign keys `ON UPDATE CASCADE` (Prisma's default, as for `reviews`).
- The migration creates only these two tables; nothing on `landmarks` (including `location` and its GiST index), `users`, `favorites`, `reviews`, or any identity table changes. `down.sql` is never executed by Prisma and refuses to run unless both tables are empty.

**Design notes for later tasks:**
- **Why `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE`.** PostgreSQL checks an ordinary unique constraint row by row, so a single `UPDATE` that rewrites several positions — a reorder, or the shift that closes the gap after a removal — fails as soon as one row momentarily takes a position another row still holds, even when the final order is valid. A deferrable constraint is checked at the end of each statement, so those single-statement rewrites succeed; `INITIALLY IMMEDIATE` (not `INITIALLY DEFERRED`) still reports a genuine duplicate at the statement that causes it rather than at `COMMIT`. A unique *index* cannot be deferrable, so this must be a constraint. The landmark unique, by contrast, must stay ordinary: adding a stop uses it as the `ON CONFLICT` arbiter, and PostgreSQL refuses a deferrable constraint as an arbiter. Both points were verified in M05-T01's probe and are pinned by the schema tests.
- **Why the 0–24 CHECK limits stops but not contiguity.** With unique `(trip_id, position)`, positions 0–24 allow at most 25 stops in a trip, but a trip with stops at positions 0 and 7 satisfies every constraint (a schema test asserts this). Keeping positions contiguous (`0 … n-1`) after every mutation is the service's job (spec §3.2, §6.4; decision D2).
- **Why future Prisma migrations must preserve the deferrable constraint.** Prisma's schema language cannot express deferrability. Prisma currently treats the constraint as matching `@@unique([tripId, position])` (no drift; see below), but a future schema change touching that key — renaming it, changing its columns, or regenerating it — would make Prisma emit an ordinary unique index. Any such generated SQL must be reviewed and rewritten to keep `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE`; the catalog test in `trips-schema.integration.test.ts` fails if the constraint is ever recreated without it.
- **Concurrent mutations are M05-T03's responsibility.** The schema guarantees integrity (no duplicate stop or position, at most 25 stops, valid foreign keys), but the specified locking procedure — lock the owner's trip row, then add, remove, or reorder, increment `version`, and set `updated_at` (spec §6.4) — and its concurrent-request tests belong to the M05-T03 repository and service. The database never changes `version` or `updated_at` by itself (pinned by a test).

**Increment 1a (2026-11-23) — preparation and review — ACCEPTED.** Models, migration, and `down.sql` prepared without touching either database. `prisma validate`, `format --check`, and `generate` passed; backend type check, strict reviews-tests check, ESLint, a build to a scratch folder, and backend unit 376/376 passed. Read-only `prisma migrate diff`: schema-to-schema output was the two tables, their indexes, and foreign keys; against `landmarks_test` and `landmarks_dev` it was identical plus only the two known ADR-010 `location` artefacts. Statement-by-statement comparison: 8 statements identical to Prisma's; Prisma's ordinary `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` for the position key replaced by the deferrable constraint, and the four CHECKs added. Both databases: UTF8, `Etc/UTC`, PostgreSQL 17.5, PostGIS installed, four migrations, no trip tables.

**Increment 1b (2026-11-23) — `landmarks_test` — ACCEPTED.** Target verified (URL and live `current_database()`), migration confirmed pending, then applied with `prisma migrate deploy`. New `backend/tests/trips-schema.integration.test.ts` — **33 tests**, every behavioural test in an always-rolled-back transaction (no truncation, no leftovers): migration record and checksum; exact columns, defaults, indexes, and constraints of both tables; **catalog deferrability** (`condeferrable = true`, `condeferred = false` for the position key; `pg_index.indimmediate` false for it and true for the landmark key); static checks of `migration.sql` (exactly one `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE`, no `INITIALLY DEFERRED`, only the new tables altered) and `down.sql` (guarded, drop order); `location` untouched; UTF8 and UTC; name lengths 0/1/100/101 including astral characters; `version` and share-hash CHECKs and hash uniqueness; positions −1/0/24/25, the 25-stop limit, an accepted gap (0 and 7), duplicate position and landmark; single-statement reversal, swap, and removal shift succeed, while colliding final positions are rejected with the order unchanged; `ON CONFLICT (trip_id, landmark_id)` works and PostgreSQL refuses the deferrable key as an arbiter; RESTRICT and CASCADE behaviour; database defaults; no automatic `updated_at`/`version` change. Results: the new file 33/33 in five consecutive runs; **backend integration 548/548** (36 files; 515 before plus 33); **backend unit 376/376**; Prisma validate, format, and generate; backend type check, strict type check of the new file, ESLint, and root Prettier clean.

The only output is the two known ADR-010 `location` artefacts (`DROP INDEX "landmarks_location_gist_idx"`; `ALTER COLUMN "location" DROP NOT NULL`), never to be applied. Full before/after comparison: settings, extensions, enums, and the first four migration records unchanged; only `trips`, `trip_stops`, and the new migration record added; **every pre-existing table** (`landmarks` 1,692 rows, `spatial_ref_sys` 8,500, and `users`, `accounts`, `sessions`, `verifications`, `rate_limits`, `favorites`, `reviews` at 0) has identical row count, full-row fingerprint, columns, indexes, constraints, and triggers; no invalid index. ### M05-T03: Implement Trip Management API

**Status:** **Complete — 2026-11-23** (formally accepted by the developer after Increment 6). Planning authorized 2026-11-23; the six-increment plan and decisions T3-1 to T3-8 approved 2026-11-23 (T3-2 and T3-4 revised, the add-stop error order amended, controlled lock-order tests and the available-stop shape added); Increments 1 to 5 accepted 2026-11-23; Increment 6 (security regression, API documentation, closure verification) accepted 2026-11-23 with the task. Backend API and tests, plus the README; no frontend application, schema, migration, or dependency change. Uncommitted — the Git checkpoint is deferred until Milestone 05 is complete.

**Dependencies:** M03-T04, M05-T02

**Scope:**
- Support creating, retrieving, updating, and deleting trips.
- Support adding, removing, and reordering stops.
- Enforce authorization.
- Validate trip data.

**Clarified scope (M05-T01, accepted 2026-11-23; spec v1.1 §§4–7, 10):** the owner routes through `mountProtected("/trips")`; **the sharing endpoints** — enable/rotate and revoke (owner) and the public `GET /api/v1/shared/trips/:shareToken` (the single new allowlist entry), with token hashing, `is_shared`, `sharing_enabled`, response headers, and `TRIP_SHARING_ENABLED`; the trip-name rule (server side) and its parity corpus; the transaction and locking rules of spec §6.4; read-time redaction and field allowlists; PostGIS straight-line distances; the four named 409 codes; per-user throttling (60 mutations / 120 reads per minute); route-inventory, guard, two-user, concurrency, redaction, distance, and sharing tests.

**Approved decisions (2026-11-23):** **T3-1** revoke is allowed whether sharing is on or off; **T3-2 (revised)** enable checks ownership first, under the trip-row lock (missing or non-owned → `404`), and only then, for the owner, `TRIP_SHARING_ENABLED` off → `409 TRIP_SHARING_UNAVAILABLE`; **T3-3** the `X-Robots-Tag` header and robots meta tag on the *page* `/shared/trips/*` belong to M05-T06 (this task sets them on the API response); **T3-4 (revised)** the public shared route answers unexpected failures itself with the fixed JSON `500` and a token-free log line, with no app-wide handler change; **T3-5** the trip-name parity corpus lives at `frontend/src/trips/testdata/tripNameCorpus.json` (ASCII, 59 cases, fingerprint `59:1682`); **T3-6** an empty reorder list stays `400`; **T3-7** no retry on a share-hash collision (the unique index turns it into a `500`); **T3-8** browser tests that need sharing set `TRIP_SHARING_ENABLED=true` in M05-T06. **Spec amendment:** the add-stop error order (Spec 5 v1.1 §6.4 and §11, ADR-014 decision 4 clarification, 2026-11-23) — trip `404` → landmark `404` → `409 TRIP_STOP_ALREADY_EXISTS` → `409 TRIP_STOP_LIMIT_REACHED` → insert. **Increment 6 decisions (2026-11-23):** keep a repeated revoke as `204` with `version` + 1; accept ignored query parameters on the public shared GET (documented as not filters or options); keep the flag semantics — switching sharing off hides links but does not revoke them, so unrevoked links work again if it is switched back on (documented, and carried to M07-T05); keep the malformed percent-encoded path behaviour under the existing app-wide follow-up.

**What was built** (`backend/src/trips/`; all owner routes through `mountProtected(apiRouter, "/trips", …)`; the public route through `apiRouter.use`):
- `config/trip-sharing.ts` and `env.trips.sharingEnabled` (`TRIP_SHARING_ENABLED`: off by default in production, on elsewhere, explicit values respected); four error envelopes in `http/error-envelope.ts`.
- `name-rule.ts` (Spec 5 §5.1.1), `request-schema.ts` (strict Zod bodies, fixed messages that never echo input, path IDs, list query, reorder shape), `rate-limit.ts` (60 mutations / 120 reads per user per minute, 10,000-key cap, the shared generic limiter).
- `repository.ts` — owner-scoped SQL only (`WHERE user_id = …` inside every statement); the trip-row lock `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`; read-time visibility and PostGIS straight-line legs in one statement (`LEFT JOIN`, `LAG`); add with visibility re-check and `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; single-statement gap close and `unnest … WITH ORDINALITY` reorder (relying on the deferrable position key); share-hash set/clear and lookup by hash. `user_id` and `share_token_hash` are never selected.
- `service.ts` — create, list, get (REPEATABLE READ), rename, delete, add/remove/reorder stops, enable/rotate and revoke sharing, and the public shared read; each mutation in one transaction that locks the trip row first and increments `version` exactly once. Representations built field by field (never by spreading a row).
- `share-token.ts` — `randomBytes(32)` base64url (43 characters), lower-case hex SHA-256, syntax checks, `share_url` from `env.auth.baseUrl`'s origin.
- `router.ts` (ten owner routes, each with its limiter before validation) and `shared-router.ts` (`GET /shared/trips/:shareToken`; `Cache-Control: no-store` and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` set before any work; generic `404`; fixed JSON `500` with an event-code-only log line).
- The full API contract is documented in the README's "Trips API" section.

**Increment record (all 2026-11-23):**
- **Increment 1 — foundation (accepted).** Setting, envelopes, name rule, request schemas, limiter, the parity corpus and its backend helper; the add-stop amendment documented. 97 new unit tests; backend unit 473/473; the route-inventory reset touched `landmarks_test` (tables already empty), reported and accepted.
- **Increment 2 — repository and service read side (accepted).** Create, list, get, rename, delete; redaction and distances. `trips-repository.integration.test.ts` 34 tests.
- **Increment 3 — stop mutations (accepted).** Add, remove, reorder with the amended precedence, rollback, uncontrolled races, and controlled lock order (`pg_blocking_pids`). `trips-stops.integration.test.ts` 37 tests; integration 619/619; five negative controls caught.
- **Increment 4 — owner HTTP router (accepted).** Eight owner routes mounted; route inventory 15 protected endpoints. `trips.integration.test.ts` 68 tests; integration 687/687; nine router/mounting faults caught (one test added after the identity-override fault was first missed).
- **Increment 5 — sharing (accepted).** Enable/rotate and revoke, the public shared route, the single new GET-only allowlist entry. `trips-sharing.integration.test.ts` 34 tests, `trips-share-token.test.ts` 18 tests; unit 491/491, integration 723/723; eleven sharing faults caught.
- **Increment 6 — security regression, documentation, closure verification (accepted with the task).** `trips-security.integration.test.ts` (9 matrix tests: 401 on all ten owner endpoints for missing and forged sessions, before validation; 403 on all eight writes for missing, foreign, `null`, and look-alike origins; identical `404` for non-owned and missing on all eight trip-scoped endpoints; hostile path IDs, identity fields, and query parameters `400` everywhere with nothing echoed; no public write anywhere; a disclosure scan of every response body in a full lifecycle; seven landmark-state transitions with identical owner and shared redaction; the enable → rotate → flag off → flag on → revoke → re-enable → delete sequence; a static scan that the only log call in `src/trips` is the shared router's event-code line). Three negative controls caught (shared view gaining `id`/`updated_at`; a router logging the request URL; revoke skipping validation). README "Trips API" section added.

**Final verification (Increment 6, 2026-11-23, local):** Prettier (repository), `prisma validate`, backend type check, strict type check of the trip and route-inventory tests, backend ESLint (0 warnings), backend build — all clean. **Backend unit 491/491** (19 files). **Backend integration 732/732** (41 files) — trips-security 9, trips-sharing 34, trips HTTP 68, trips-stops 37, trips-repository 34, trips-schema 33, route-inventory 17, api-route-guard 14, reviews suites 208, favorites suites 121. **Remaining risks and follow-ups:**
- **Production sharing is not approved.** The API exists, but `TRIP_SHARING_ENABLED` stays off in production until both M07-T05 blockers (classification policy and dataset review; share tokens in hosting/proxy access logs) are resolved and the developer approves. Switching the setting off does not revoke links; unrevoked links revive if it is switched back on (documented in the README; carried to M07-T05).
- **App-wide, unchanged:** a malformed percent-encoded path or a malformed JSON body still gets Express's default HTML `400` before the trip routes run.

- **Pre-existing, not changed here:** four type errors that an ad-hoc strict check reports in `api-route-guard.integration.test.ts` (present in the committed version; the project type check is clean).

- **Closure investigation — coincident trip-map markers (2026-11-24; M05-T04 closure withheld pending the decision):** reproduced in Chromium with guarded fixtures (stop 3 and stop 4 of a trip at identical coordinates; temporary spec, removed afterwards; fixtures cleaned up). Findings: an un-excluded axe scan of the trip page and a targeted `target-size` scan of the trip map both report **0 violations**; the two markers occupy the **identical** 28×28 box, so the later one (Stop 3) fully covers the earlier one — the "2" badge is not visible, and every pointer click at that point reaches Stop 3 only (**Stop 2 cannot be reached by pointer on the map**); keyboard access is intact — Tab reaches Stop 1, Stop 2, and Stop 3 in order, Enter and Space open each stop's own popup, Escape and the close button return focus to that marker, and a focused marker is raised above the other. Root cause: markers are placed at their exact (shared) coordinates and stacked in DOM order; nothing groups or distinguishes coincident stops. Every stop remains fully available in the ordered list (name, profile link, controls), which is the primary representation. Proposed correction: render stops at identical coordinates as ONE marker at the true location, numbered with all their stop numbers and listing each stop with its own profile link in its popup. **Approved by the developer 2026-11-24 (trip map only) and implemented — see the next item.**
- **Coincident-stop correction (approved and implemented 2026-11-24; trip map only):**
  - *Decision — exact-coordinate grouping:* available stops are grouped only when latitude AND longitude are exactly equal (a key built from the validated numbers; never rounded), so nearby but distinct points stay separate; one marker per unique pair, at its true location; no offsets, clustering, or dependency. Unavailable stops are never placed, grouped, or mentioned. A single stop is unchanged ("2"; "Stop 2: Name, Waterfall").
  - *Badge rule (deterministic):* up to two stop numbers in ascending trip order, comma-separated, then " +k" with the exact count of further stops there — "2,3", "2,3 +1" (stops 2, 3, 5), "1,2 +23" (25 stops). The badge holds digits, commas, and "+" only (checked against a fixed pattern) and never a name; the pill widens with its text.
  - *Accessible name:* complete for every stop and beginning with the visible badge text (label in name) — "Stops 2,3, 2 at the same location: Stop 2: A, Waterfall; Stop 3: B, Natural Arch". The first browser run caught axe `label-content-name-mismatch` (serious) with the originally proposed "Stops 2 and 3, same location: …"; the name format was changed accordingly and a unit negative control added.
  - *Combined popup:* a group "Stops 2 and 3 details" listing every stop in trip order — number, name (in `<bdi>`), category, and its own "View profile" link named "View profile: Stop N, Name" — in a list that scrolls (max 12rem) for large groups; no coordinates or geometry.
  - *Identity and focus:* a marker's key is its coordinate pair, so reorders, renumbering, and members joining or leaving keep the same marker element and its focus; the viewport refits only when the set of mapped stops and locations changes (not on reorder). If a focused popup link's stop leaves the group, focus moves to the link now at that index (else the last, else the group); focus is moved only when it would otherwise be lost, never from an unrelated control. A focused marker that disappears still hands focus to the Stops heading. Enter, Space, Escape, Shift+Tab, and the close button behave as before.

No backend, schema, discovery-map, or dependency change.

Negative controls, each detected, sources restored byte-identical: coordinates rounded before grouping (3 failures), no grouping (12), a combined popup listing only its first member (4), unavailable stops joined into a group (3), a name without the visible badge text (5).
