#### M05-T06 Increment 4 — Owner sharing interface (authorized 2026-11-24; reported 2026-11-24; **accepted 2026-11-24**)

**Acceptance (2026-11-24):** the developer accepted the owner sharing interface, version-based reconciliation, held-link invalidation rules, uncertain-outcome handling, clipboard behavior, token-confidentiality safeguards, shared mutation locking, session isolation, and verification evidence; the documented limitations (concurrent changes after the latest authoritative read, conservative link invalidation after refused mutations, previously copied system-clipboard contents); and the history-state test-timing correction. The original failed-run history and the existing intermittent-test follow-ups (`DiscoveryPage.realHooks`, `TripDetailPage.map`) are preserved, as is the NC2/NC5 evidence of how redundant safeguards and UI conditions first masked those controls. A reporting clarification corrects the failed-run count below (4 of 8 runs, not 3).

Frontend only — the owner's Sharing section on the trip page through `useTrip`. No public page, no backend page headers, no backend API, schema, migration, dependency, or Playwright change; no database access; production sharing unchanged (off by default; release blockers stand).

- **Backend contract verified before implementing (2026-11-24):** `enableTripSharing` and `revokeTripSharing` (`backend/src/trips/service.ts`) each run one `UPDATE trips SET share_token_hash = …, version = version + 1` (`repository.ts` `setLockedTripShareHash`) under the owner's trip-row lock; every other trip mutation also increments `version` by exactly 1 under that lock; revoking with no active link still increments it. The proposed version strategy is therefore supported; no discrepancy.
- **State (`trips/useTrip.ts`).** New mutations `enableSharing` and `revokeSharing` on the existing single change lock (pending kinds `share`/`unshare`; "Creating share link…", "Turning off sharing…"), with epochs, session isolation, error classification, and re-reads reused; nothing optimistic (`is_shared`, `sharing_enabled`, and `version` come only from validated responses). New stale reasons `shared`, `unshared`, `share_uncertain`, `sharing_unavailable`. The hook exposes `shareLink` (the CONFIRMED link or null) and `isShareLinkCurrent(url)` (a synchronous check for late async callbacks). The link lives only in a ref (`linkRef`, with the version at which it was confirmed) mirrored by a state value for rendering.
- **Enable / rotate.** Capture the current version and whether a link was active; take the lock; clear any held link; `POST …/share`; keep the returned (validated) URL as a PROVISIONAL local value; mandatory re-read under the lock. **Confirmation rule:** the URL becomes the held link only if the re-read succeeds AND `sharing_enabled` is true AND `is_shared` is true AND `version === captured + 1` (exactly our change). Otherwise it is discarded (`share_unconfirmed`, reason `inactive` or `version`) and never rendered, copied, or announced; a failed re-read → `stale` (`shared`; "A share link was created, but the updated trip couldn't be loaded, so the link can't be shown. Any earlier link no longer works."). The page never navigates to a share URL.
- **Revoke.** Clear the held link; `DELETE …/share`; mandatory re-read. Re-read `is_shared` false → "Sharing turned off. The previous link no longer works."; true → `revoke_superseded` ("Sharing was turned off, but the trip is shared again now — it may have been changed in another window…"); failure → `stale` (`unshared`).
- **Held-link rules (applied on every state commit).** The held link is **kept** only when the new state is a ready trip with `sharing_enabled` and `is_shared`, and either (a) its version equals the link's version (nothing changed), or (b) its version is exactly link version + 1 AND the commit is the result of our own confirmed non-sharing change based on the link's version — rename `200`, reorder `200`, add `201` + re-read, remove `204` + re-read (marked just before committing, so that single increment is accounted for). It is **cleared** on: rotation or revocation starting; any non-ready state (loading, idle, stale, error, not found, deleted — so also a session that becomes unconfirmed, a user or trip change, deletion, and failed reconciliation); sharing disabled or inactive — including a server setting switched off at the same version (no increment), with no restoration if it is switched back on; uncertain or conflicting outcomes with any version change; any other version change. When in doubt, the link is discarded. Late responses cannot restore a cleared link (the hook's epoch/scope checks).
- **Limitations.** The rule reduces, but cannot eliminate, the chance of showing a stale link: a rotation or revocation in another window after the most recent read is invisible until the next read (there is no polling or token verification, and no new backend field). A `409 TRIP_SHARING_UNAVAILABLE` or a refused (`403`/`429`) rotation also drops the held link because it is cleared when the change begins (conservative). Clearing application state cannot remove a link the user has already copied to the system clipboard. A link confirmed under rule (b) carries the first link's version forward only for our own confirmed changes.
- **Unavailable, refusals, uncertain.** `409 TRIP_SHARING_UNAVAILABLE` → re-read (held link already cleared), the section hides when the refreshed `sharing_enabled` is false, "Sharing isn't available right now.", no retry; failure → `stale` (`sharing_unavailable`). `404` → generic not found; `401` → session re-check; `403`/`429`/other `400` → the established "Couldn't change the trip…" alert with Retry-After. Uncertain enable → re-read under the lock: sharing on → alert (a new link may have been created and an earlier link may no longer work; Create new link for one to copy); off → "Sharing is currently off for this trip." (never "no link was created"); failure → `stale` (`share_uncertain`). Uncertain revoke → off: "Couldn't confirm the change, but sharing is currently off for this trip."; on: "Couldn't confirm that sharing was turned off. Sharing is still on. Choose Turn off sharing to try again." Nothing is replayed; Reload only reads.
- **Interface (`trips/TripSharingPanel.tsx`, `TripDetailPage.tsx`).** Rendered only when the trip reports `sharing_enabled: true`, after the map. Heading "Sharing" (focusable). Not shared: who can view a shared trip (anyone with the link, without signing in) and that recipients can forward it; **Create share link**. Shared with a held link: labelled read-only **Share link** field (selects its text on focus), **Copy link**, **Create new link**, **Turn off sharing**, and the explanation of rotation and revocation before activation (D8). Shared without a held link: the current link can't be shown again; Create new link (the current link stops working) and Turn off sharing — nothing reconstructed. No sharing controls on My Trips or in the picker. Focus: created → Copy link; turned off → Create share link; unconfirmed/uncertain/superseded/unavailable → the Sharing heading (Stops heading if the section is gone); stale → Reload; the section disappearing with focus inside moves lost focus to the Stops heading.
- **Clipboard.** `navigator.clipboard.writeText` only on an explicit Copy link activation, only with the held link. "Share link copied." only after it resolves. Rejection or no Clipboard API → the field is focused and its text selected (only if focus is still on Copy link or was lost) with a manual-copy alert; otherwise an alert asking the user to select the link. The result is dropped when the page unmounted, the user or trip changed, or the held link changed. No dependency, no `execCommand`.
- **Token confidentiality.** The raw URL exists only in `useTrip`'s link ref/state, the provisional local variable of `enableSharing`, and the read-only field's value. It is not written to localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, router state, the page URL, logs, error messages, or announcements (tests spy on `Storage.prototype.setItem` and console methods, and assert the token appears exactly once in the page — the field value).
- **Existing tests:** unchanged (fixtures already reported `sharing_enabled: true`; no query broke).
- **New tests:** `TripDetailPage.sharing.test.tsx` (46, real `useTrip`), `useTrip.sharing.test.tsx` (10).
- **Tests strengthened during negative controls:** (1) a page test for a server sharing switch at the SAME version (the inactive rule was otherwise masked by the version rule, because every sharing change increments the version); (2) a page test for the rotation re-read window (NC2 was first caught only by the hook test, because the panel shows the field only when the trip is already shared — a first creation could not leak through the UI, a rotation could).
- **Negative controls** (each restored byte-identical, SHA-256 verified): NC1 section shown with `sharing_enabled` false — 4 failures; NC2 provisional link exposed before the re-read — 2 (after strengthening); NC3 mandatory re-read skipped — at least 10 (the control's output listing was capped at 10 lines); NC4 link accepted after an unexpected version transition — 2; NC5 held link kept when sharing is inactive/disabled — 1 (after strengthening); NC6 shared lock bypassed — 4; NC7 uncertain enable replayed — 2; NC8 URL persisted in sessionStorage — 1; NC9 held link retained across a user/session change — 1; NC10 URL in an announcement — 2; NC11 clipboard success reported before it resolves — 3.
- **Intermittent failures found and handled.** During repeated full runs at 1961 tests (before the fix below): **4 of 8 runs** failed, one test each — 4 failure occurrences in total: `DiscoveryPage.realHooks.test.tsx` once (retained markers through a failed refetch; existing intermittent), `TripDetailPage.map.test.tsx` once (focused marker removed after refresh; existing intermittent; 10 of 10 isolated runs passed), and `TripDetailPage.createdNotice.test.tsx` twice (Increment 2's test). *(Reporting clarification, 2026-11-24: the report and this record first said "3 of 8 runs"; the run log shows runs 2, 3, 5, and 6 of the 8 failed — corrected here, no failure evidence removed.)* Diagnosis of the last: the notice and focus assertions passed, but the history state was still present — the router's replace navigation (issued from the page's effect) can commit after the trip-ready render under load, so a synchronous assertion could run first. A test-timing defect, not a product defect (the state is cleared moments later and consumption is keyed per history entry). Correction: the six "history state cleared" assertions in the Increment 2/3 test files (`TripDetailPage.createdNotice`, `MyTripsPage.notice`, `TripDetailPage.manage`) now wait for the replacement. After it: 5 of 5 full runs passed.
- **Regression (local):** frontend unit **1961/1961** (98 files; 1905 + 56 new) in 5 of 5 full runs after the timing correction (failed-run history above); `tsc -b --noEmit`, ESLint, repository-wide Prettier, and the frontend build clean; the existing >500 kB bundle warning unchanged. Backend and Playwright not re-run (frontend-only increment). Real-browser clipboard, keyboard, axe, and responsive checks remain scheduled for Increment 6, together with the Increment 3 observation on pending feedback.

#### M05-T06 Increment 5a — Public shared-trip page, frontend (authorized 2026-11-24; reported 2026-11-24; **accepted 2026-11-24**)

**Acceptance (2026-11-24):** the developer accepted the public route, authentication independence, request lifecycle, read-only presentation, component reuse, presentation-only map identity, redaction and distance safeguards, the robots metadata lifecycle, token-confidentiality safeguards, and the verification evidence; the app-wide session check and favorites membership request under D6 (neither receives the share token nor gates access to shared-trip content); and the Increment 4 failed-run correction (4 of 8). Preserved: the NC3 evidence that checking only the settled UI missed a transient stale-data commit, the original missed control, and the strengthened commit-level test; all existing intermittent-test follow-ups. **NC1 clarification:** the evidence for the intended behavior is the App-level failures in the signed-out, pending, and failing session modes (the gate blocked public access) and the page-level failures; the signed-in failure was incidental — the mutation's early return changed React's hook order — and is not evidence of the intended behavior.

Frontend only. No backend page-header change (reserved for 5b), no backend API, schema, migration, dependency, Playwright, offline, or service-worker change; no database access; production sharing unchanged.

- **Route and authentication independence.** `/shared/trips/:shareToken` (`routes/SharedTripPage.tsx`) inside `AppLayout`, with no authentication gate and no sign-in redirect. The page never reads the session, so a loading, signed-out, signed-in, or failed session check changes nothing for it. It mounts no owner component (`useTrip`, `TripDetailPage`, editing, rename/delete, add-to-trip, nearby, or sharing controls) and makes no owner-trip request. **Shell review (D6):** the app-wide `AuthProvider` session check and, when signed in, `FavoritesProvider`'s membership request run on this page as on every page — neither receives the token (asserted). The components that build a sign-in `returnTo` from the current location (`FavoriteButton`, `OwnReviewPanel`, `AddToTripButton`) are not mounted here, and `AccountNav`'s Sign in link is the static `/sign-in`; no shell change was needed.
- **Data lifecycle (`trips/useSharedTrip.ts`).** One snapshot through `getSharedTrip` → `getPublicJson` (`credentials: "omit"`, only `Accept`), validated by the strict Increment 1 parser (name, stops, summary only — no owner field exists on the type). Views: `loading`, `ready` (with `loadId`), `unavailable`, `error`. Token syntax is checked in the hook before any request (and again in `getSharedTrip` — a redundant layer). Fresh fetch on mount, token change, and explicit retry; per-fetch epochs drop late responses for earlier tokens and after unmount; the view is DERIVED from the current token on every render, so a token change hides the previous trip in the very first commit, before any effect runs. Nothing persisted, prefetched, polled, cached offline, or retried automatically.
- **States.** Loading ("Loading shared trip…", heading "Shared trip"); ready; unavailable — one generic text for a malformed token (no request), `400`, and `404`: "This shared trip isn't available. The link may be incorrect, or the owner may have stopped sharing it." (revoked, rotated, deleted, disabled, and unknown are indistinguishable); error — network, `5xx`, or an invalid response: one alert "Couldn't load this shared trip. Please try again." with **Try again** (no server text). The previous trip is never shown while a new token loads or after it fails.
- **Read-only presentation and reuse.** Heading = the validated name (`<bdi>`); "Shared trip — view only. Someone shared this trip with a link; it can't be changed here."; `TripStopList` without controls and with the new `emptyState` prop ("This trip has no stops."; D12 — omitted, the owner's empty state is unchanged); `TripStopItem` (available: profile link per D9, category, straight-line leg; unavailable: "No longer available" only, D10); `TripDistanceSummary`/`formatTripDistance` (partial and complete totals, the straight-line disclaimer, no total below two stops); `TripStopsMap`/`tripMapMarkers` (available stops only, original numbering with gaps, exact-coordinate grouping, existing keyboard/popup behavior, fitting, tiles and attribution, no lines). No client-side distance calculation.
- **Map identity (R5).** Verified: `TripStopsMap` depends only on `stops` and `onFocusLost`; its IDs are static (`trip-map-heading`); the owner page keys it with the trip ID only to give each trip a fresh map. Here it is keyed with `loadId`, a presentation-only counter that is new for every successful load, and it is unmounted whenever the view is not `ready`. No owner ID is fabricated, the shared response is not expanded, and the token is never used as an identifier. **No adaptation of `TripStopsMap` was needed**; owner-map behavior is unchanged (its existing tests pass untouched).
- **Robots metadata (`trips/useRobotsNoindex.ts`, D2).** While the route is mounted — in every state, including a malformed token — the document has exactly one `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">`. If the document had no robots tag, the hook adds one and removes it on leaving; if one existed, its content is replaced and restored on leaving; no other head element is touched; a token change (same mount) never duplicates it. **Limitation:** client-side metadata is applied only after the script runs and is not a substitute for the HTTP `X-Robots-Tag` (and `Cache-Control: no-store`) on the page response — Increment 5b.
- **Token confidentiality.** The token is in the page URL by necessity; from this page it reaches only the shared-trip request. It is not stored (localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB), logged, put in error or announcement text, page title, metadata, DOM IDs, marker labels, sign-in return paths, navigation state, or any other request (asserted with recorded `fetch` calls in four session modes, storage and console spies, and DOM/head scans). The existing `strict-origin` referrer policy is unchanged; real-browser Referer verification is Increment 6. The application cannot prevent browser history, infrastructure access logs (an M07-T05 release blocker), or a visitor forwarding the URL.
- **Accessibility and focus.** One status region (loading) and at most one alert; the unavailable outcome is plain text; the stop list is the primary representation; names direction-isolated; after Try again (its button then disappears) the heading takes focus only if focus was lost; a token change unmounts the previous map, so no stale popup or focused marker survives.
- **New tests:** `SharedTripPage.test.tsx` (31, real hook and components, client mocked), `SharedTripPage.app.test.tsx` (5, the real App, `AuthProvider`, and `FavoritesProvider` with `fetch` stubbed, in signed-out, signed-in, pending, and failing session modes). No existing test changed.
- **Test strengthened during negative controls:** NC3 (previous trip kept after a token change, with the derived view removed) was first NOT caught — the stale trip is visible for exactly one commit before the hook's effect switches to loading, and the test looked only after effects settled. A layout-effect commit probe now records the heading in every commit under the new token's URL; NC3 is then caught.
- **Negative controls** (each restored byte-identical, SHA-256 verified for all five touched sources): NC1 authentication gate — caught by the App-level tests in the signed-out, pending, and failing session modes (the signed-in case also failed, but only because the mutation's early return changes the hook order) and by the page tests; NC2 request for a malformed token (hook check removed) — 5 failures (redundancy: `getSharedTrip` would still refuse without a network request; the page tests mock it to test the hook's own boundary); NC3 previous trip kept — 1 (after strengthening); NC4 late response for an earlier token (epoch check removed) — 1 (the derived view also hides it, showing "loading" instead of the current trip — caught through that symptom); NC5 owner mutation controls rendered — 1; NC6a unavailable-stop metadata rendered (its opaque landmark ID) — 2; NC6b unavailable stops mapped — 2; NC7 robots meta omitted — 6; NC8 robots meta left on other pages — 1; NC9a token in a sign-in return path — 5; NC9b token in an unrelated request — 4.
- **Regression (local):** frontend unit **1997/1997** (100 files; 1961 + 36 new) in 6 of 6 full runs (one before and five after the negative controls); no failure observed in these runs — the existing intermittent follow-ups (`DiscoveryPage.realHooks`, `TripDetailPage.map`) are NOT considered resolved. `tsc -b --noEmit`, ESLint, repository-wide Prettier, and the frontend build clean; the existing >500 kB bundle warning unchanged. Backend and Playwright not re-run. Real-browser keyboard, axe, responsive, robots, and Referer checks remain scheduled for Increment 6.

#### M05-T06 Increment 5b — Backend page headers (authorized 2026-11-24; reported 2026-11-24; **accepted 2026-11-24**)

**Acceptance (2026-11-24):** the developer accepted the SPA fallback implementation, the route matcher, the final HTTP response headers, authentication and sharing-setting independence, unrelated-route isolation, token-confidentiality safeguards, the negative controls, and the regression evidence; the React Router `matchRoutes` verification used to establish the accepted path variants; and the migration-checksum transcription clarification (the historical M05-T02 record and the read-only verification evidence are preserved). Also preserved: the NC5 initially missed control, the strengthened query test, and its successful verification; and the two invalid mutation-command attempts (NC4, NC6) as reported.

A narrowly scoped backend change (D1 option A, D1a, R1): the existing SPA fallback in `backend/src/app.ts` adds two headers for the shared-trip page. No new endpoint, no route-inventory or allowlist change, no API contract, schema, migration, dependency, frontend, or Playwright change; no production sharing change.

- **Middleware order (unchanged):** client IP → Better Auth (`/api/auth/*`) → `express.json` → `/api/v1` (origin check, API router, including the shared-trip API with its own `no-store`/`X-Robots-Tag`) → `/health` → JSON 404 for any other `/api/*` → `express.static(frontend/dist)` → the GET-only SPA fallback (last). A shared-page path is not a file in `dist`, so static passes it through to the fallback.
- **Implementation.** In the SPA fallback, before `res.sendFile(index.html)`: when `SHARED_TRIP_PAGE_PATH.test(req.path)`, set `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` and `Cache-Control: no-store` (the values are the shared-trip API's existing exported constants). `send` 0.19.2 (used by `sendFile`) sets its own `Cache-Control` only when none is already present, so `no-store` is the final value (asserted on real responses). The headers also apply to the fallback's existing JSON 404 if `index.html` were missing. Nothing is read from the token, looked up, logged, or added to the HTML.
- **Route matching — `/^\/shared\/trips\/[^/]+\/*$/i` against `req.path`.** Derived from the frontend router's actual behavior (React Router's `matchRoutes` with the app's route tree, checked 2026-11-24): the route matches exactly one non-empty segment after `/shared/trips/`, case-insensitively, with any number of trailing slashes, and with a percent-encoded `/` inside the segment; it does not match an empty segment (`/shared/trips/`), extra segments, internal double slashes (`/shared//trips/x`, `/shared/trips//x`), or similar prefixes. The regex mirrors exactly that. Any segment qualifies — valid, malformed, revoked, or unknown tokens alike — with no database lookup, authentication, or dependence on `TRIP_SHARING_ENABLED`. `req.path` excludes the query string, so a query (including one containing `/`) cannot bypass it. Existing malformed-path behavior is unchanged and outside the fallback: a malformed percent-encoding (for example `%E0%A4%A`) still fails in Express's own decoding with its default HTML `400` before any route runs (the existing app-wide follow-up); non-GET requests to the page path still get the JSON 404 (as before).
- **Final headers verified (Supertest, real responses):** shared page → `200 text/html` (the built `index.html`, with its unchanged `<meta name="referrer" content="strict-origin">`), `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, `Cache-Control: no-store`, also for HEAD. Root `/`, `/trips`, `/trips/:id`, `/favorites`, `/landmarks/x`, `/sign-in`, and nine similar non-matching paths → no `X-Robots-Tag`, `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0` (the existing `send`/static default). A static JS asset → `public, max-age=0`, no `X-Robots-Tag`. The shared-trip API (`/api/v1/shared/trips/bad`, with or without a query) → unchanged generic JSON 404 with its own `no-store` and `X-Robots-Tag`; `/api/v1/shared/trips/a/b` → the JSON 404, never the page. The backend sets no other security headers (the referrer policy is the HTML meta tag), so none could be disturbed; no global `noindex`/`no-store` and no static robots meta in `index.html` were added; the frontend's route-specific robots meta (5a) is unchanged.
- **Defensive only.** `noindex` and `no-store` reduce indexing and caching of the page; they are not access control. The share token still travels in the page and API URL paths, so hosting and proxy access logs may record it — the infrastructure access-log review remains a production sharing release blocker (M07-T05), as does the sensitive-location classification.
- **New tests:** `backend/tests/shared-trip-page.integration.test.ts` (35), following `routing.integration.test.ts`: the real `createApp()` over Supertest, the built `frontend/dist` (present from the Increment 5a frontend build — the established build-before-tests convention), the guarded integration setup (importing `app.ts` loads the Prisma module). It creates no fixture and asserts no database query (spies on `$queryRaw`, `$queryRawUnsafe`, `$executeRaw`, `$transaction`) and no token in the response headers or body. Sharing independence is shown by rebuilding the app with `TRIP_SHARING_ENABLED` true and false (fresh module graph); authentication independence with no cookie and a forged one.
- **Negative controls** (each restored byte-identical, SHA-256 verified): NC1 `X-Robots-Tag` removed — 10 failures (output listing capped at 8 lines); NC2 `Cache-Control: no-store` removed — 10 (capped at 8); NC3 headers applied to every SPA page — 15+ (capped at 8); NC4 only syntactically valid 43-character tokens protected — 4; NC5 matching against `req.originalUrl` (query included) — first **not caught**: the regex's `[^/]+` absorbed a query without `/` (`?utm_source=x&ref=1`), so the existing query test still passed; strengthened with a query containing slashes (`?next=/trips/x&back=/`), then caught — 1; NC6 accepted variants dropped (no trailing slashes, case-sensitive) — 3. **Invalid first attempts:** NC4 and NC6 initially failed to apply (the shell collapsed the regex's backslashes in the mutation command, so the search string did not match; no test ran) and were re-run through a small Node mutation script.
- **Regression (local):** backend unit **491/491**; backend integration **767/767** (732 + 35 new) in 2 of 2 full runs; the route-inventory and routing suites pass unchanged; backend `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, the backend build, and repository-wide Prettier (after formatting the new test file) clean. Frontend source unchanged since Increment 5a (frontend unit baseline 1997/1997 not re-run; the existing frontend build was used). Playwright not run (Increment 6).
- **Databases (read-only verification after the suites):** `landmarks_dev` identical to the M05-T02 reference baseline — `landmarks` 1,692 rows with fingerprint `9430b2b0f9a58f5efbcc4ef23c5b55c7`; `users`, `accounts`, `sessions`, `verifications`, `rate_limits`, `favorites`, `reviews`, `trips`, `trip_stops` 0; five migrations with unchanged checksums (trips `ed450889…ce253`); position key `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY IMMEDIATE`. `landmarks_test` empty after the integration suites' guarded resets, same five migrations. *Note:* the M05-T02 baseline abbreviates the init migration's checksum as `4a777d4c…f75f4`; the full value is `4a777d4c…41ed75f4` (identical in both databases and equal to the SHA-256 of its `migration.sql`) — a transcription slip in that abbreviation, not a change.
- **Remaining browser verification (Increment 6):** the headers on the page served to a real browser by the production-mode E2E server, robots meta and header together, and the outgoing Referer behavior.
- **Remaining approval boundaries (at Increment 5b):** Increments 6 and 7 are not authorized.

#### M05-T06 Increment 6 — Integrated browser verification (authorized 2026-11-24; reported 2026-11-24; **accepted 2026-11-24**)

**Acceptance (2026-11-24):** the developer accepted the integrated browser journeys, real API verification, the test-only sharing configuration, the redaction evidence, the HTTP privacy headers, the actual browser credential and Referer behavior, the clipboard integration, responsive verification, the negative controls, and the regression evidence; the narrowly scoped `TripStopsMap` popup-width correction; and the evidence-based nearby keyboard-test corrections. Real Chromium against the production-mode E2E server (`NODE_ENV=production`) on the guarded `landmarks_test`, with synthetic fixtures only (`e2e/helpers/tripFixtures.ts`: PUBLIC stops, a `hidden` fixture made SENSITIVE, a `retired` fixture; recorded accounts; trips and stops deleted before fixture landmarks). The production default (off when `NODE_ENV=production`) is unchanged; CI inherits the setting through the config; no second server. - **Real API journeys ([real]):** My Trips — signed-out return path (`/sign-in?returnTo=%2Ftrips`), nav link only when signed in (`aria-current`), direct navigation and reload, empty account; 21 trips over two pages in exactly the server's newest-first order (checked against the API and its `updated_at` sequence), names, stop counts, dates (`<time datetime>`), Shared indicator, detail links, Next/Previous with heading focus, Back/Forward, `?page=0` replaced with a single request, past-end page, another user's trip never listed. Creation — client validation (field error associated, input focused, nothing sent), duplicate activations → one POST, navigation to the new trip, "Created trip …" once with heading focus, history state cleared, no repeat after reload or Back/Forward, persisted. Rename — prefill and focus, Cancel without PATCH, validation, save with `{ name, version }`, heading and focus, persistence, renamed trip first in My Trips. Two tabs (same user) — tab A renames; tab B's stale rename gets `409`, re-reads (heading shows A's name), keeps its draft, sends nothing more until an explicit save, which carries the refreshed version (`version 0` then `1`, responses `[409, 200]`). Delete — confirmation and Cancel send no DELETE, one DELETE on confirmation, My Trips with "Deleted trip …" once and heading focus, history cleared, not repeated on reload or history navigation, trip gone, direct access shows not found; a trip deleted elsewhere first → "That trip is no longer available.". Sharing lifecycle — Create share link with the mandatory re-read HELD: the received URL was not in the page while the re-read was pending; then the validated URL in the read-only field, focus on Copy link, one POST; token absent from storage, history state, URL, and title; **real clipboard** (Chromium with clipboard permissions: `readText()` equals the reconciled URL; "Share link copied." after it); My Trips "Shared"; reload → "can't be shown again" with no URL in the page; the copied link opens in a fresh signed-out context; rotation → new URL, old URL generically unavailable on a fresh request, new URL works; revocation → held URL cleared, the replacement unavailable (checked on a fresh anonymous request after the DELETE answered), status confirmed; deleting a shared trip kills its link. Public view and redaction — trip with stops [PUBLIC, SENSITIVE, PUBLIC, PUBLIC, PUBLIC at the same point, retired]: the real API response has exactly `name`, `stops`, `distance_summary`, positions 0–5, the two protected stops exactly `{ id, is_available: false }`, distances `null` next to them, summary 2 of 5 legs, and no protected names, coordinates, or trip ID; the DOM shows the name in `<bdi>`, "Stop 1…Stop 6", "No longer available" without links for stops 2 and 6, a profile link for stop 1, "Straight-line total of 2 of 5 legs" and the disclaimer, three markers ("Stop 1", "Stop 3", "Stops 4,5") with no stop 2/6 marker and no route geometry, no owner control or trip ID; keyboard marker popup (Enter → popup group focused, Escape → marker) and keyboard profile link. Empty shared trip ("This trip has no stops.", no map) and all-unavailable trip (placeholders, map explanation, "No straight-line total").
- **HTTP headers, robots, credentials (real server):** page HTML for a valid, a malformed, an unknown, and a trailing-slash-with-query token path → `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, `Cache-Control: no-store` (independent of the API outcome); `/`, `/trips`, `/favorites` → no robots header, `public, max-age=0`; shared API → `no-store`, `noindex, nofollow`, no `Set-Cookie`; unknown token → the generic 404 with the headers. In a signed-in browser, the shared read carried **no `Cookie` header** and set none; the owner stayed signed in; one route-specific robots meta while on the page, none after leaving through the app or on `/trips`.
- **Referer and token propagation (real browser):** the effective policy is the existing `strict-origin` (index.html meta), not `strict-origin-when-cross-origin`. Observed: cross-origin tile requests and a real cross-origin **navigation** from the shared page (the map attribution link to openstreetmap.org, answered locally so the token never leaves the machine) sent `Referer: http://localhost:3000/` only; every same-origin subresource and API request also sent only the origin. So the token and the shared path never appear in any Referer, same-origin included. The token appeared only in the page's own document URL and the shared API request URL (both inherent; hosting/proxy access logs remain an M07-T05 release blocker); not in any other request, link (including sign-in return paths — the header's Sign in link is `/sign-in`), title, DOM ID, or console output. A pending or failing session check did not block the public page.
- **Intercepted coverage ([intercepted]):** uncertain create (`route.fetch()` reached the real server, then the answer was aborted) → no replay, page 1 re-read lists the real new trip without navigating to it, typed name kept; uncertain create whose page-1 check also fails → one combined alert, Try again re-reads; uncertain rename (real rename, answer lost) → "Couldn't confirm the rename, but the trip is now named After."; uncertain delete (real delete, answer lost) → qualified unavailable notice; sharing disabled (owner response rewritten to `sharing_enabled: false`) → no Sharing section; `409 TRIP_SHARING_UNAVAILABLE` → re-read hides the section, focus to Stops; public 503 → one alert, Try again loads and focuses the heading; uncertain enable (real share, answer lost) → may-have-been-created alert, no field; uncertain revoke → "sharing is currently off"; a real create whose re-read is aborted → stale, Reload only reads, no field; a real rotation whose re-read is rewritten with an extra version bump → "couldn't be confirmed", no field — POST/DELETE counts confirm nothing was replayed. Clipboard failure (controlled `writeText` override rejecting) → field focused and fully selected, manual-copy alert; late clipboard success after the link was replaced → nothing reported. Shared lock: during a held rotation, Rename (aria-disabled, still opens) and Remove sent nothing, status "Creating share link…". Signing out clears the held link; signing in again does not restore it. A late shared-trip response for the previous token after in-app navigation never replaces the current trip. **Pending feedback (Increment 3 observation):** while a rename is pending, Delete trip is `aria-disabled` but opens its confirmation, whose button is `aria-disabled`, the status says "Renaming trip…", and activating it sends no DELETE; judged understandable (status names the change in progress), with no product change.

- **Product defect found and corrected — trip-map popup width (TripStopsMap, owner and public pages):** at 320 px a single-stop popup was 327 px wide in a 288 px map (Leaflet's default 300 px content cap plus ~46 px of wrapper margins), extending past the map and the viewport; auto-pan cannot fix a popup wider than the map. Reproduced on the owner trip page with a temporary diagnostic spec (deleted). Correction: `<Popup maxWidth={popupMaxWidth(map.getSize().x)}>` — content capped at the map width minus 64 px (chrome and auto-pan padding), between 160 and 300 px. Evidence: the 320 px containment assertion failed before and passes after on both pages; 375 px had failed only through a mid-animation measurement (fixed by polling until the pan settles); `TripStopsMap`/`TripDetailPage.map`/`SharedTripPage` unit tests 70/70; full frontend unit 1997/1997. **Follow-up (not changed):** check the discovery and nearby maps' popups at 320 px.

- **Diagnosis (temporary probes outside the repository; no tracked changes):**
  - *C1 — `NearbyMap` product defect (zoom-animation race).* After the 50 mi radius change, the stack marker sat 132 px above the nearby map container (the origin marker was inside). The element under its centre was the results list's `<li>`. The container did not resize, and Leaflet's size matched the DOM size. A Leaflet view-change log showed the zoom-in click starting an animated zoom (about 250 ms; `_animatingZoom` was still true at the zoom-out click and at the fit). The zoom-out click and then `FitToResults`' `fitBounds` arrived during that animation, and Leaflet dropped them: the map ended at zoom 11, centred at 0.420,-160.501, instead of the fitted 0.545,-160.455. Counterfactuals: waiting 600 ms before the radius change made the fit apply and a real pointer click reach the marker; Leaflet's public `zoomAnimation: false` option gave an exact fit and a reachable marker. The test reproduced locally with 2 workers (1 of 1) and passed with 11 workers (34/34 for both specs), consistent with a timing window that loaded machines miss.
  - *C2 — trip-map test defect (viewport-relative measurement).* The assertion compared marker `getBoundingClientRect()` values, which are relative to the browser viewport. A probe replay showed no movement within the map, no change of the Leaflet pane transform (the geographic view), and no resize. With Verdana at 720 px, the whole map moved 140 px in the viewport (map-relative 0) because the page scrolled to reach the list button; at 600 px, 84 px (map-relative ≤1, rounding). With the default font, Georgia, or Verdana at 900 px, there was no displacement. The requirement that reordering does not refit or move the geographic view held in every case.
  - The two failures have independent causes, each exposed by CI conditions (fast 2-worker timing; different font metrics). The Linux mechanisms are inferred from local reproduction and remain to be confirmed by remote CI.
- **Approved corrections (2026-11-25):**
  - *C1 (product, `frontend/src/trips/NearbyMap.tsx`):* `zoomAnimation={false}` on the nearby `MapContainer` (Leaflet's documented public option), with a comment describing the race. Zoom changes apply at once, so every new result set is fitted. **Accepted UX tradeoff:** the nearby map's zoom transitions are not animated. Map controls, fit-per-new-set behaviour, no refit on renumbering, membership changes, or pending updates, marker grouping, popups and their containment, keyboard behaviour, and focus restoration are unchanged. No private Leaflet API, wait, or test-only behaviour.
  - *C1 tests:* a new browser test in `e2e/nearby.spec.ts` ("a new result set arriving during a zoom interaction is fitted, contained, and clickable"). With controlled ordering, not timing, it holds the radius request, clicks zoom-in, then releases the response; it checks that every marker of the new set lies inside the map, that a **real pointer click** opens the stack marker's popup (3 links), and that the popup is contained. Plus one unit assertion in `frontend/src/trips/NearbyMap.leaflet.test.tsx` that the nearby map's `zoomAnimation` option is off. The maximum-results test is unchanged.
  - *C2 (test, `e2e/trips.spec.ts`, the reorder check of the map-keyboard test):* marker positions are measured relative to the trip map's Leaflet container, keeping marker identity (by label), both the x and y checks, the 1 px tolerance, the real reorder interaction, and every keyboard and focus assertion; it also checks the marker count. No pane-transform assertion was added: map-relative positions already capture a change of view. `TripStopsMap` product code was not changed.
- **Negative controls (each source restored byte-identical and verified by SHA-256; frontend rebuilt):**

The maximum-results test failed 3/3 with 2 workers (the original "intercepts pointer events" signature) and passed 3/3 with 11 workers. The new unit assertion failed (`expected true to be false`).
  - *C2 layout variation (temporary font injection into the test; restored by hash):* the corrected test passed with the default font and with Verdana. The pre-correction test (from `HEAD`) with Verdana failed exactly as in CI (`Expected: <= 1, Received: 141`).
  - *C2 refit:* the M05-T05 approach (`TripStopsMap` refitting on every reorder) was **not detected** by the corrected test with either font. In this test the view is already the fitted view when measured (the popup is closed), so a refit to the same bounds does not change the geographic view and no position-based check can see it. In the M05-T05 test the popup is open during the reorder, so popup auto-pan had moved the view and a refit moved it back. A stronger temporary mutation that changes the view on reorder (re-centring on Stop 1 at the current zoom whenever stop numbers change) **was detected** with both fonts (`Received: 11.14` px default, `5.55` px Verdana, against the 1 px tolerance).

## Milestone 06: Offline Access

**Objective:** Provide approved offline access to landmark information and supported geographic map regions.

**Related Requirements:** FR-13, FR-14

**FR-14 deferral reconciliation (2026-11-25, M06-T01 Increment 1; accepted by the developer 2026-11-25):** the developer deferred FR-14 (offline map-region downloads) on 2026-10-30 after the M00-T06 feasibility check (record under M00-T06, preserved unchanged). Milestone 06's active scope is therefore **FR-13**: the installable PWA, offline application shell, and explicitly saved landmark and owned-trip snapshots, with account lifecycle, isolation, and cleanup. FR-14 remains a preserved, **deferred** requirement: no tile provider is selected (Stadia Maps remains a research candidate only), M06-T04 is **Deferred**, and reconsidering FR-14 or selecting a provider requires a new, explicit developer decision. The objective and requirement references above are kept as originally written; the "supported geographic map regions" part of the objective is deferred with FR-14. See Specification 6 §7.4 and ADR-004's deferral clarification.

### M06-T01: Define Offline Requirements and Constraints

**Status:** Complete *(2026-11-25; closure authorized by the developer 2026-11-25. History: Proposed → In Progress (authorized 2026-11-25 for requirements analysis and documentation only) → Complete)*

**Dependencies:** M00-T02

**Scope:**
- Identify functionality required offline.
- ~~Evaluate mapping provider licensing.~~ *Removed from active scope 2026-11-25: the evaluation was performed early in M00-T06, and FR-14 was deferred on 2026-10-30. M06-T01 instead records the deferral consistently across the governing documents and performs no provider evaluation or selection.*
- Define download boundaries and storage limits. *(For FR-13 snapshots; map-region download boundaries are deferred with FR-14.)*
- Establish offline data freshness requirements.
- Document technical feasibility.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [x] Offline requirements are approved. *(Specification 6 v1.1, approved 2026-11-25, with AC-1–AC-39 and traceability; the ADR-007 amendment and the Specification 7 §5 amendment were accepted the same day.)*
- [x] Provider restrictions are documented. *(The preserved M00-T06 evidence and the FR-14 deferral record of Increment 1, accepted 2026-11-25: Specification 6 §7.4, ADR-004's clarification, Specification 7 §10.4.2. No new provider research.)*
- [x] Storage and update behavior are defined. *(Specification 6 v1.1: OFF-STORE-1–7 (200/25 per account per device, no silent eviction, quota and unavailable-storage handling); OFF-EV-1–9 (explicit individual refresh only, authoritative redaction precedence, ordering); OFF-SNAP-7 (timestamps); OFF-SW-1 (service-worker update prompt); OFF-FAIL-1–6 (storage-failure handling).)*
- [x] Technical feasibility is established. *(At requirements level: the snapshot contracts are satisfiable from the existing landmark-detail and owner-trip responses with no backend change (OFF-SNAP-9); the architecture is ADR-007 (IndexedDB via `idb`, service worker via `vite-plugin-pwa`); browser limitations are documented (eviction, iOS Safari, suspended tabs, OFF-FAIL-4 and OFF-FAIL-6); FR-14 is infeasible as scoped and deferred. Dependency installation and implementation mechanisms remain for M06-T02 and M06-T03 approval; no offline functionality has been implemented or verified.)*

- **Residual persistent-storage risks** (Specification 6 v1.1 OFF-FAIL-6), carried to M07-T02 and the production-readiness assessment:
  - no remote revocation on a device that stays offline;
  - no guaranteed physical erasure;
  - in-memory-only blocks — including the safety lock — lost on reload if every storage write fails;
  - delayed invalidation in suspended tabs (an inherent notification limit, distinct from preventable races, which must be prevented);
  - reduced availability when operations are refused because safe cross-tab coordination cannot be established;
  - an unrevoked server session after an unconfirmed sign-out until Finish signing out succeeds;
  - browser and iOS eviction, and user clearing of site data, which also removes the safety lock;
  - device-clock timestamps.
- **Increment 2 — accepted by the developer 2026-11-25 as a proposed specification amendment** (five-file inventory, the proposed ADR-007 amendment, the Specification 6 v1.1 requirements, the Specification 7 §5 amendment, acceptance criteria, traceability, security follow-ups, documentation verification, and the correction of seven newly introduced whitespace-only lines). The three-line hard-break exception is preserved.
- **Final refinement decisions (developer, 2026-11-25), approved for incorporation into the proposed documents:**
  - **D22 approved:** a device-wide `localStorage` safety lock holding a single fixed value — the only approved storage exception, and defense in depth only.
  - Unavailable markers apply to owned trips.

That listener calls `onNeedReload()` if one is supplied, and **otherwise calls `window.location.reload()`** — so without `onNeedReload`, accepting an update in one tab would reload every tab that had shown the prompt.
    - `updateServiceWorker(_reloadPage)` ignores its argument and only sends `SKIP_WAITING` to the waiting worker (`workbox-window`'s `messageSkipWaiting` posts `{ type: "SKIP_WAITING" }`), which matches the generated worker's handler.
    - One `controlling` listener is added per prompt, so `onNeedReload` may run more than once.

  - *Registration architecture (`src/pwa/serviceWorker.ts`):*
    - An application-owned controller around `virtual:pwa-register`. The plugin's injection stays disabled (`injectRegister: false`). `main.tsx` calls `serviceWorker.register()` once after render.
    - It registers only when the build is production, the context is secure, and `"serviceWorker" in navigator`. Otherwise its state is `skipped` or `unsupported`.
    - Registration is idempotent; it runs after the load event (`immediate: false`); asynchronous and synchronous failures become `failed` without affecting the application.
    - **`onNeedReload` is always supplied**, so the helper's fallback `window.location.reload()` can never run. Its handler records only `updateActivatedElsewhere` and is idempotent across repeated `controlling` callbacks.
    - `onOfflineReady` (first installation) and `onNeedRefresh` (a waiting update, including one already waiting at startup) only set state flags.
    - The helper's `updateServiceWorker` is discarded: nothing sends `SKIP_WAITING`, activates an update, or reloads.
    - The minimal integration points are `register()`, `getState()`, and `subscribe()`; Increment 4 adds acceptance.
    - `pwa-env.d.ts` references `vite-plugin-pwa/vanillajs` for the module's types. Unit tests resolve the virtual module to `src/test/pwaRegisterStub.ts` (a vitest alias), which throws if reached, and inject fakes.

    The existing request-client tests (`frontend/src/api/client.test.ts` and the other `api/*.test.ts` files) and `frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.test.tsx` needed no change; the client's integration tests are in the new `clientConnectivity.test.ts`. There were no backend, dependency, service-worker, Playwright-configuration, or CI changes.
  - *State model (`connectivity.ts`; in memory only, not account-scoped, never persisted):*
    - `browser` (`online` | `offline`) comes only from `navigator.onLine` and the `online`/`offline` events.
    - `reachability` starts at `unknown` and is set only by request evidence: `reachable` (any HTTP response with a 2xx–4xx status), `server-problem` (5xx including 503, or an unreadable body), or `unreachable` (a fetch that failed without a response).
    - React reads the state with `useSyncExternalStore` (`useConnectivity`). Browser listeners are added on the first subscriber and removed with the last, so repeated initialization never duplicates them.
  - *Request classification (`client.ts`):*
    - `requestJson` and `requestNoContent` take a sequence number before `fetch` and report one outcome.
    - Outcomes: a 2xx or 4xx response (including 401, 403, 404, and 429) is `response`; 5xx, including 503, is `server-problem`; an unreadable body is `server-problem`; a rejected `fetch` is `network-failure`; a `DOMException` `AbortError` is `cancelled` (no evidence).
    - Every return value and thrown `ApiError` (code, status, message, `retryAfterSeconds`) is unchanged — an abort still surfaces as `NETWORK_ERROR`, as before. There are no retries and no extra requests.
  - *Ordering semantics:*
    - Each request takes an increasing sequence number at its start; starting is not evidence.
    - An outcome is applied only if its sequence number is greater than the watermark (the sequence number of the last applied outcome), and it then becomes the new watermark. So an older outcome never overrides newer evidence in either direction, and a cancelled request never moves the watermark — a newer cancelled request therefore cannot suppress an older request's later evidence.
    - An `offline` event changes only the hint.
    - An `online` event changes `unreachable` to `unknown` — not recovery — and raises the watermark to the latest started sequence number, so nothing that started before the reset can restore stale evidence. Other states keep their reachability.
    - The explicit health check goes through the same client and the same rules.
    - There are no timers, timestamps, or polling.
  - *Banner (`ConnectivityBanner`, rendered in `AppLayout` between the header and `<main>`):*
    - **Hint only:** "Your device reports that it is offline. Pages and actions that need the server may not work."
    - **Unreachable, browser offline:** "You appear to be offline. Pages and actions that need the server won't work until you reconnect."
    - **Unreachable, browser online:** "The app can't reach the server right now, although your device reports a network connection."
    - Server problems from ordinary requests are left to the features. Nothing claims that saved data is available offline. Feature errors and their "Try again" buttons are unchanged and remain alongside the banner.
    - Styling follows the existing black-on-white look on `#f4f4f4`, wraps at narrow widths, and has no animation. Focus is never moved.
  - *Announcements:*
    - Messages are in a role-less `aria-live="polite"` region, so it never competes with the features' `role="status"` regions (47 unit-test queries and several browser specs use `getByRole("status")`).
    - The region is created the **first time there is something to say** — empty, then filled on the next commit, so the first message is announced — and then stays. Its text changes only when the situation changes, so identical evidence is not re-announced.
    - *Why the region is created late:* the original regression test `e2e/trips.spec.ts:993` counts the page's `[aria-live='polite']` regions and expects exactly 2. An always-present banner region made it 3, failing that test in the first full browser run. Original specs may not be modified, and `role="status"` would break the `getByRole("status")` queries, so the region is created only when needed. The test passes again.
  - *Explicit recovery:*
    - The button is named **"Check connection"**, not "Try again", so it never collides with the features' own "Try again" buttons.
    - Pressing it sends **one** `GET /health` through the client (contract verified in `backend/src/routes/health.ts`: 200 `{status:"ok"}` or 503 `{status:"unavailable"}`).
    - Outcomes: 200 with `status: "ok"` is healthy — the banner disappears and "Connected to the server." is announced. A 503 or another HTTP error is unhealthy — "The server responded but isn't working normally. Some pages and actions may not work." An unreadable or unexpected body is unexpected. A failed request leaves the server unreachable, with "The server still can't be reached." added.
    - While a check is pending, the button shows "Checking connection…" with `aria-disabled`, and further presses are ignored, so only one request is in flight.
    - There are no automatic checks (not on mount, browser events, or new evidence), no polling, no retries, and no new endpoint.
  - *Unit tests (+56; frontend unit 2,010 → 2,066):*
    - **store:** initial state; every outcome; cancellation; starting is not evidence; all four ordering cases; offline hint; online reset with a stale request; listener deduplication and cleanup; change-only notifications; no browser environment;
    - **client, with deferred promises and fresh modules:** 2xx; 401/403/404/429; 500 and 503; unreadable body; failed fetch; abort; no-content requests; exactly one fetch; the four concurrency cases; a request across an online reset; a health check overlapping an ordinary request; six health-check classifications;
    - **banner:** each wording; no banner for an ordinary server problem; no offline-data claim; online is not recovery; no re-announcement; no focus move; feature errors preserved; the deferred-region mutation order; pending state and duplicate suppression; healthy, unhealthy, and failed checks; keyboard operation; no automatic checks; cleanup on unmount.

    - *Pending-state mapping (existing state only):*

      | Control | Existing pending state | Non-pending restrictions (no marker) | `data-pending` |
      |---|---|---|---|
      | TripPicker "Add to the selected trip" | `busy` = `flow.action !== null` (adding or creating) | landmark unavailable (`blocked`), unreachable | `busy` |
      | TripPicker "Show more trips" | `list.loadingMore` | — | `list.loadingMore` |
      | NewTripForm "Create trip and add" | `busy` (`flow.action`, covering **both** create and add steps) | `disabled` (landmark unavailable), unreachable | `busy` |
      | CreateTripForm "Create trip" | `busy` = `creating \|\| checking` (the creation, or the list check after an uncertain one) | unreachable | `busy` |
      | RenameTripForm "Save name", DeleteTripConfirm "Delete trip permanently" | page `busy` = `useTrip` `pending !== null` (a change or its required re-read) | unreachable | `busy` |
      | TripSharingPanel create / rotate / revoke | page `busy` (the single shared change lock) | unreachable; "Copy link" never marked | `busy` (`pendingFlag`) |
      | TripStopItem Move up / Move down / Remove | `controls.busy` (page lock) | first/last native `disabled`, unreachable; "Find nearby" never marked | `controls.busy` |
      | AddToTripButton (profile) "Try adding again" | `busy` = `flow.action !== null` | unreachable | `busy` |

- **Increment 4 — planning and feasibility (2026-11-25; read-only plus scratch experiments; no production code changed). Every proposal below is PENDING APPROVAL.**
  - *Requirements:* Specification 6 §3.1 (install affordance when the platform exposes a prompt, otherwise concise guidance without claiming installability; installation never a prerequisite) and §5 / OFF-SW-1 / AC-27 (a user-visible reload prompt; never discard an in-progress action); Specification 7 §5 ("service-worker updates" verified in the service-worker project); ADR-007 (installable PWA); planning decisions D3 (event-driven optional install affordance), D6, D9 (pending-mutation guard; no automatic activation when the count reaches zero; no reload of non-accepting tabs; a controlled test-only update server using real production assets).
  - *Verified facts:*
    - `frontend/src/pwa/serviceWorker.ts` (`createServiceWorkerController`, `serviceWorker`; states `registration`, `offlineReady`, `updateWaiting`, `updateActivatedElsewhere`) always supplies `onNeedReload` (records only), never calls the helper's `updateServiceWorker`, and ignores the registration object; `main.tsx` calls `serviceWorker.register()`.
    - Installed helper (`vite-plugin-pwa/dist/client/build/register.js`): in prompt mode a `controlling` listener is added **per prompt** (on `waiting`, or on an external `installed`) and calls `onNeedReload` (else `location.reload()`) only when the workbox-window event's `isUpdate` is true. In `workbox-window` 7.4.1 (`Workbox.js`), `isUpdate` is merely "a worker controlled this page when `register()` ran" — **not** "this tab accepted"; and `controlling` is dispatched on every `controllerchange`. Consequences: (a) a tab that was **uncontrolled** at registration (a first visit; there is no `clientsClaim`) never receives `onNeedReload`; (b) tabs that never showed a prompt get no signal; (c) repeated prompts add repeated listeners. `updateServiceWorker` ignores its argument and posts `SKIP_WAITING` only if `registration.waiting` exists. A worker already waiting at startup is reported (`wasWaitingBeforeRegister`) and reaches `onNeedRefresh`.
    - Generated `dist/sw.js`: `precacheAndRoute([...])` with `{url:"index.html",revision:<MD5 of the file>}` (verified equal to `md5(index.html)`), hashed assets with `revision:null`, `cleanupOutdatedCaches()`, the `SKIP_WAITING` message handler, and the navigation route; no `clientsClaim`/`skipWaiting` by default.
    - `frontend/src/api/client.ts` has the only `fetch` calls (`requestJson`, `requestNoContent`); every helper (`getJson`, `postJson`, `putJson`, `putJsonBody`, `patchJson`, `deleteJson`, `deleteNoContent`, `getPublicJson`) goes through them, including all authentication calls (`frontend/src/api/auth.ts`).
    - Existing locks: `useTrip` `begin(kind)`/`end(epoch)` (`busyRef`, `pending`) spanning each change **and its required re-read**; `useAddToTrip` `setAction(kind)`/`setAction(null)` spanning create-then-add and verify-then-add; `MyTripsPage` `creating || checking`; auth pages `submitting` ref + `pending`; reviews and favorites per-request pending.
    - No existing install, `beforeinstallprompt`, `appinstalled`, display-mode, `beforeunload`, or navigation-blocking code. `AppLayout` renders the skip link, header (with `AccountNav`), `ConnectivityBanner`, then `<main>`.
  - *Feasibility experiment (scratch only; `update-feasibility.cjs` with `playwright-core` Chromium and a throwaway static server on `http://localhost:4317`, an origin separate from the e2e server):* build A = an unmodified copy of the production `dist`; build B = A plus a `<meta name="e2e-build" content="B">` marker, the main JS copied to a new hashed-style name with an appended comment (the old file removed), and `sw.js` rewritten (index revision = the new MD5; the JS URL replaced). Results: both tabs controlled by A; after switching the server to B, `registration.update()` produced a **real waiting worker**; **3 s of postponement: still waiting, 0 document loads in either tab**; an explicit `SKIP_WAITING` activated it and both tabs received `controllerchange`; one reload of the accepting tab → **marker B and the new JS asset**, the precache holding the new JS and not the old; **accepting tab exactly 1 document load, the other tab 0** (still showing A); the real `dist/sw.js` unchanged. *Correction during the experiment:* counting `framenavigated` overstated reloads (it includes same-document URL updates by the discovery map); counting `document` requests is the reliable measure. Both shell (`index.html`) replacement and changed-JavaScript replacement are therefore provable; AC-27 itself only requires the prompt.
  - *Proposed subdivision (order kept):* **4a** lifecycle and user-controlled activation — the state machine, notices, postponement, and the activation code path, with the operational **Update now control not rendered until 4b**; **4b** mutation and unsaved-input protection, which then exposes Update now; **4c** the real service-worker update browser test; **4d** the installation affordance. 4c depends on 4b (acceptance through the real UI); 4d is independent.
  - *Proposed lifecycle (4a):* the wrapper captures the `ServiceWorkerRegistration` (`onRegisteredSW`) and owns acceptance itself — it records `acceptedHere`, posts `SKIP_WAITING` directly to the **captured waiting worker**, and reloads exactly once (a `reloadStarted` guard) when **that worker** reaches `activated` (its own `statechange`), which also covers tabs that were uncontrolled at registration. It adds **one** `navigator.serviceWorker` `controllerchange` listener; a change not accepted here sets `updateActivatedElsewhere` (never reloads). `onNeedReload` stays supplied and becomes a no-op signal (it only suppresses the helper's fallback reload); the helper's `updateServiceWorker` stays unused. States: `idle` → `waiting` (also at startup) → `postponed` (Later: hidden for this page session; shown again on the next start or for a different waiting worker) → `activating` → `reloading`; `activatedElsewhere`; `failed`. Registration failure, unsupported or development environments: no update interface. Offline: activation needs no network (the new shell is already precached); a reload while the server is unreachable shows the shell and the connectivity banner.
  - *Proposed mutation accounting (4b):* in `client.ts`, a shared `updateSafety` module counts in-flight requests whose method is not `GET`/`HEAD` (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE — every trip, favorite, review, sharing, and authentication mutation, including sign-out). The count starts synchronously before `fetch` and ends in a `finally` after the body is read and mapped (success, HTTP error, network failure, abort, unexpected exception); concurrent requests are counted independently; connectivity evidence is unchanged. *Counter alone is insufficient — counterexamples:* (1) `useAddToTrip` create-then-add has a gap between the create response and the add request (the counter is 0; a reload there leaves a created trip without the landmark); (2) trip sharing: a successful share/rotate must be followed by the mandatory re-read **before** the link is shown, and the link is shown only once — a reload in that gap loses it; (3) verify-then-add retries. *Smallest addition:* operation **holds** taken at the existing lock points — `useTrip` `begin`/`end` and `useAddToTrip` `setAction(kind)`/`setAction(null)` — so acceptance is refused while any counted request **or** hold is active. Uncertain outcomes keep the hold through their reconciliation re-read. Single-request flows (favorites, reviews, auth, My Trips create) need no hold: a reload after their request completes discards nothing the server has not settled.
  - *Proposed activation race prevention:* Update now → (1) if any counted request or hold is active, refuse with a visible reason ("Finish or wait for … first"); nothing activates later by itself; (2) if unsaved input exists, show the confirmation; (3) on confirmation, **in the same synchronous task**, re-check and set the transition gate; (4) while the gate is set, `client.ts` refuses every counted request **before** `fetch` with `ApiError(0, "UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS")` (no network, no connectivity evidence; features show their existing generic failure), and new holds are allowed but their requests are refused, so nothing partial reaches the server; (5) post `SKIP_WAITING`; (6) on activation, reload once.
  - *Proposed unsaved-input protection (4b):* an in-memory registry of `{id, category}` only (never values), fed by a tiny `useUnsavedInput(active, category)` hook that registers while `active` and unregisters on change or unmount. Proposed categories: review draft (`hasDraftContent`), new-trip names (`CreateTripForm`, `NewTripForm`), a rename draft that differs from the current name, authentication fields (any non-empty field), the reset page while a token is held in memory (a reload loses it), and a held share link (shown only once). The confirmation is inline in the update notice ("Updating reloads this page and discards: …"; **Keep working** is the default; **Update anyway**). It lists categories live; Update anyway re-checks pending work and unsaved input at the moment of the click. Successful submission and intentional Cancel already clear the corresponding state.
  - *Proposed multiple-tab behavior:* only the accepting tab reloads; other tabs learn of the activation through their own `controllerchange` and show "The app was updated in another tab" with a user-initiated **Reload** that applies the same checks (pending work refused; unsaved input confirmed). Protection is **tab-local**, and that is sufficient for the requirement: activation does not interrupt other tabs' API requests (the worker handles only precached shell requests), and no other tab reloads. A tab opened after activation simply runs the new version. A suspended tab receives `controllerchange` on resume. No new storage or cross-tab channel (and nothing touching M06-T03's sign-out coordination).
  - *Proposed failure handling:* activation is awaited for a bounded time (proposed 10 s; the only timer) and then classified from the captured worker's state: `activated` → reload once; still `installed` → definitively not activated → release the gate and say the update could not be applied (no automatic retry); `redundant` or the worker gone → release the gate and say the update is no longer available (a newer one will prompt again). Duplicate acceptance is a no-op while `activating`. No guarantee is made that an old version can be restored.
  - *Residual risks:* an old, non-reloaded tab keeps running old JavaScript after activation; a lazily loaded chunk it has not yet fetched may no longer exist (today the only lazy chunk is `workbox-window`, loaded at registration); Chromium-only automation; `beforeinstallprompt` cannot be exercised natively in automation; workbox-window's external-update heuristics are bypassed by the proposed own listeners.
  - *Proposed installation affordance (4d):* an `installPrompt` store listening to `beforeinstallprompt` (`preventDefault`, keep the event), `appinstalled`, and `matchMedia("(display-mode: standalone)")` plus `navigator.standalone` as a **hint**; an **Install app** button rendered only while a prompt event is held and the app is not running standalone; one `prompt()` per event on an explicit click; accepted or dismissed outcomes discard the event (no persistent re-prompting); otherwise a short, collapsible "How to install" guidance for browsers without a prompt (for example Safari's Share → Add to Home Screen / Add to Dock), never claiming that installation is available. No new dependency, no storage.
  - *Proposed file inventory:* **4a** `frontend/src/pwa/serviceWorker.ts` (+ `.test.ts`), new `frontend/src/pwa/UpdateNotice.tsx` (+ `.module.css`, + test), `frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx` (+ its test). **4b** new `frontend/src/pwa/updateSafety.ts` and `useUnsavedInput.ts` (+ tests), `frontend/src/api/client.ts` (+ test), `frontend/src/trips/useTrip.ts`, `frontend/src/trips/useAddToTrip.ts`, the unsaved-input registrations in `reviews/OwnReviewPanel.tsx`, `trips/CreateTripForm.tsx`, `trips/NewTripForm.tsx`, `routes/TripDetailPage.tsx` (rename draft and held link), and the four authentication pages, plus `UpdateNotice.tsx` (Update now and the confirmation), with directly corresponding tests. **4c** new `e2e/sw/update.spec.ts` and `e2e/sw/support/updateServer.ts` (an in-spec static server on a dynamic localhost port serving builds A and B derived into the test's output directory, with one deterministically held test endpoint for the pending-mutation case); no Playwright configuration or CI change. **4d** new `frontend/src/pwa/installPrompt.ts` and `InstallAffordance.tsx` (+ CSS, tests), `AppLayout.tsx`, and `e2e/sw/install.spec.ts`.
  - *Proposed verification and negative controls:* 4a — unit: waiting at startup, postpone, repeated events, ownership (only the accepting tab reloads, once), uncontrolled-tab acceptance, timeout classification; NCs: reload on any `controllerchange`; remove the reload guard; auto-accept on waiting. 4b — unit: counting for every outcome, concurrency, holds, the gate refusing before `fetch`, refusal with pending work, confirmation and re-check, registry cleanup on unmount; NCs: count only POST; drop the useAddToTrip hold (create-then-add gap); set the gate after an `await`; skip the re-check at confirmation; auto-activate when the count reaches zero. 4c — browser (real worker): prompt on a real waiting worker; Later does not activate; pending held request refuses Update now; unsaved input requires confirmation; Update now reloads the accepting tab exactly once (document-request count) to marker B and the new JS; the other tab does not reload and shows the elsewhere notice; NCs: auto-reload all tabs; accept without the pending check. 4d — unit with synthetic events; browser with a synthetic `beforeinstallprompt` (a stated limitation) for accepted, dismissed, standalone, and unsupported states, keyboard and axe; NC: prompt on page load. Byte-identical restoration and rebuild comparison throughout.

  - *Files:* `frontend/src/pwa/serviceWorker.ts`; new `frontend/src/pwa/serviceWorker.lifecycle.test.ts` (the existing `frontend/src/pwa/serviceWorker.test.ts` is **unchanged** and passes); new `frontend/src/pwa/UpdateNotice.tsx`, `UpdateNotice.module.css`, `UpdateNotice.test.tsx`; `frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx` (+1 test in `frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.test.tsx`); this plan.   - *Controller (extended, not replaced):* the same `virtual:pwa-register` registration and states (`registration`, `offlineReady`, `updateWaiting`, `updateActivatedElsewhere`) plus an `update` phase; injectable runtime (`container`, `setTimer`/`clearTimer`, `reload`) with browser defaults; the `ServiceWorkerRegistration` captured from `onRegisteredSW`; `onNeedReload` still always supplied (so the helper never reloads) and used only as evidence of a controller change when no attempt exists — never for ownership; the helper's `updateServiceWorker` never called. New methods: `postpone()`, `acceptUpdate()` (the 4b integration point; **no production caller**), `dispose()`.
  - *State-transition model (`update`):* `none` → `waiting` when a waiting worker W is observed (`postponed` if W was postponed); `waiting` → `postponed` (Later; W only, this page session); `waiting|postponed` → `activating` on acceptance (SKIP_WAITING posted to W), or → `failed` when confirmed before dispatch (no registration, W not the registration's current waiting worker, W not `installed`, or posting throws); `activating` → `reloading` when W reaches `activated` while the attempt is authorized (the single reload); `activating` → `unresolved` when the 10 s observation ends with W unsettled (authorization revoked permanently); `unresolved` → `reload-required` on a late activation (no automatic reload); `activating|unresolved` → `unavailable` when W becomes `redundant`; any phase without an attempt → `activated-elsewhere` when the observed W activates without acceptance here, when the controller changes from one worker to another, or on the helper's signal; `waiting|postponed` → `none` when W becomes redundant, after which a newer waiting worker is evaluated afresh. `activated-elsewhere` and `reload-required` are kept until the page reloads.
  - *Detection:* the helper's `onNeedRefresh` (including a worker already waiting at startup, possibly before the registration is captured) triggers a read of `registration.waiting`; the controller watches exactly that worker's `statechange` (one listener; repeated notifications add none) and reacts to its **current** state after attaching, so a change before or during listener registration is not missed. A replaced worker is detected when it becomes `redundant`.
  - *Ownership and idempotency:* an attempt binds the exact accepted worker, its own reload authorization, and its own timer; only that worker's activation, observed while authorized, reloads — guarded by a page-wide `reloadInvoked` flag. Duplicate acceptance returns `already-activating` and sends nothing; repeated `statechange`/`controllerchange`/helper signals never reload again; unrelated controller changes and other workers' activations never consume the attempt's authorization; a tab that never accepted never reloads. An initially uncontrolled accepting tab (no `controllerchange`) still reloads once from the worker's own `activated` state. Two tabs that each accept would each reload once (each has its own attempt).
  - *Postponement:* Later records the observed worker (or, before capture, applies to the worker captured next); it sends nothing, reloads nothing, leaves `registration.waiting` untouched, is not persisted, does not reopen for repeated notifications of that worker, and does not suppress a different worker.
  - *Activation elsewhere:* observed through the waiting worker's own `activated` state (covers initially uncontrolled tabs that observed it), one `controllerchange` listener (previous controller → a different one), and the helper's signal. **Limitations:** a tab that never observed the waiting worker and was uncontrolled gets no signal; a suspended tab is informed only when events are delivered on resume; immediate notification is not guaranteed in every browser. Tab-local protection does not guarantee compatibility between old frontend code still running in a non-reloaded tab and a newly deployed backend.
  - *Timeout:* after 10 s, an `activated` worker reloads (an activation whose event had not yet arrived); a `redundant` one → `unavailable`; otherwise → `unresolved` with automatic reload authorization revoked, so a later activation only reaches `reload-required` (an explicit, safety-checked reload is 4b's). There is no automatic retry. Both orderings at the boundary are tested.
  - *UpdateNotice:* rendered in `AppLayout` after `ConnectivityBanner` and before `<main>`. One role-less `aria-live="polite"` region, mounted only when there is first something to say (empty, then filled), as the banner does — none by default, so existing live-region counts are unchanged. Messages: waiting ("…will be used after every tab of this app has been closed"), activated elsewhere, failed, unavailable, unresolved, reload required — none claims an automatic reload. **The only control is Later** (while waiting); it postpones and moves focus to `#main-content` because the button disappears. Focus is never moved by a phase change. **No Update now, Reload, or other activation control exists in production**, no browser global, and no test-only path; `acceptUpdate()` is exercised only by unit tests with injected dependencies.
