  - *Share-link ownership (discrepancy resolved):* the server URL is returned by `enableTripSharing` (`frontend/src/api/trips.ts`) to `useTrip.enableSharing` (`frontend/src/trips/useTrip.ts`), which keeps it only in a local `provisional` variable until the mandatory re-read under the change lock (`reread(…, "shared")`) confirms it (sharing enabled and active, version exactly captured + 1). Only then is it held: `linkRef.current = { url, version }` and its render mirror `setShareLink(url)` — **`useTrip` owns it**. `TripDetailPage.tsx` only reads `shareLink` (and `isShareLinkCurrent`), passes it to `TripSharingPanel` (`link` prop; display only), and copies it on explicit "Copy link" (`navigator.clipboard.writeText`). Clearing: `clearLink()` (at the start of every share/rotate **and** revoke — immediately after `begin()`, before any request), the held-link rules in `reconcileHeldLink` on every `commit` (non-ready state, sharing off, or an unexplained version change), and unmount of the page (the hook's memory disappears). **Registration boundary:** `useTrip`, imperatively — register exactly where `linkRef.current` is set, unregister in `clearLink()`, and in a mount/unmount effect (re-registering after StrictMode's simulated remount if `linkRef.current` is still set). The registry never receives the URL. **Copying does not end protection** (it proves nothing about retention); protection ends when the link is cleared or the page unmounts.
  - *Mutation-workflow coverage:*

    | Workflow (owner) | Lock | Requests → follow-up | Terminal point | Request accounting enough? |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | Trip changes: move, remove, add stop, rename, delete (`useTrip` `begin`/`end`) | `busyRef` (sync) + `pending` | one mutation → mandatory re-read (also on uncertain outcomes) | `end(epoch)` in `finally`, or `invalidate()` | **No** — gap between the mutation response and the re-read request |
    | Share / rotate (`useTrip.enableSharing`) | same | POST share → mandatory re-read → link held | `end(epoch)` after the link is held | **No** — a reload between the POST response and the re-read loses the only display of the new link |
    | Revoke (`useTrip.revokeSharing`) | same | DELETE share → re-read | `end(epoch)` | No (same gap; lower impact) |
    | Add to selected trip; create-then-add; verify-then-add retry (`useAddToTrip` `begin`/`end`) | `busyRef` (sync) + `action` | POST add; or POST create → POST add; or GET trip → POST add | `end(epoch)`, or `clearAll()` | **No** — create-then-add and verify-then-add have request gaps |
    | My Trips create (`MyTripsPage.handleCreate`) | `creatingRef` (sync) | POST create → client navigation (uncertain → page-1 list check) | navigate / alert | Yes — after the response the trip exists; a reload loses only the one-time "created" notice |
    | Favorite add/remove (`FavoritesProvider` `save`/`remove`) | `pendingRef` per landmark | one PUT/DELETE | `finally` | Yes |
    | Review create/edit/delete (`OwnReviewPanel` `submit`/`saveEdit`/`confirmDelete`) | `submitting`/`saving`/`deleting` (React state) | one POST/PATCH/DELETE → reloads of own review and list | `finally` | Yes — the follow-up reads only re-read settled server state; drafts are unsaved input (below) |
    | Sign-in (`SignInPage`) | `submitting` ref | POST → `refresh()` GET → navigate | navigate | Yes — a reload after the POST lands signed in |
    | Registration | `submitting` ref | POST → navigate (notice) | navigate | Yes — a reload loses only the "Registration received" notice |
    | Forgot password | `submitting` ref | POST → confirmation | confirmation | Yes — a reload loses only the confirmation |
    | Reset password | `submitting` ref | POST → `clearResetToken()` → `refresh()` GET → navigate | navigate | Yes for data; a reload during the `refresh()` gap shows "link incomplete" although the reset succeeded (accepted limitation, V10) |
    | Sign-out (`AuthProvider.signOut`) | — | POST | — | Counted only; behavior unchanged (M06-T03 boundary) |

  - *Required holds (V3), each justified by a request gap:* `useTrip` — acquire in `begin()` (before `busyRef`, `setPending`, and before `enableSharing`/`revokeSharing` call `clearLink()`), release in `end(epoch)` and in `invalidate()` (which already drops the lock without `end`); `useAddToTrip` — acquire in `begin()` (before `busyRef`, `setAction`, `setFeedback(null)`), release in `end(epoch)` and `clearAll()`. **No holds** for My Trips create, favorites, reviews, or authentication. When the transition gate is held, `begin()` returns `null` (the existing "ignored"/busy path) **before any side effect**, so no share link is cleared and no partial workflow starts. Holds are idempotent tokens; exceptions are covered because both hooks release in `finally`; unmount does not abort a request, so the hold lasts until the request settles; concurrency is already excluded by the existing per-hook lock.
  - *Request-accounting contract (U4):* one wrapper around `fetch` in `requestJson` and `requestNoContent` (`frontend/src/api/client.ts`): for a method other than `GET`/`HEAD`, a synchronous `updateSafety.beginMutationRequest()` **before** `connectivity.beginRequest()` and `fetch`; if the gate is held it throws `ApiError(0, "UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS", …)` at once (no `fetch`, no connectivity sequence, nothing counted, nothing queued or retried); otherwise it returns an idempotent `release`, called in a `finally` that encloses `fetch`, body parsing, evidence reporting, and error construction — so success, HTTP errors, network errors, aborts, invalid bodies, and unexpected exceptions all release exactly once; concurrent requests are counted independently. Connectivity evidence is unchanged. No backend contract change.
  - *Feature compatibility of the refusal (V2):* `useTrip` and `useAddToTrip` never reach it (their `begin()` refuses first). Favorites, reviews, and authentication map an unfamiliar status-0 `ApiError` to their existing generic failure. **But `MyTripsPage.classifyCreateFailure` maps it to `uncertain`** (a misleading "couldn't confirm" alert plus a list check), and a stale render could let a click through. Recommended: also make the accepted online-only abstraction report "unavailable while the app updates" while the gate is held (a change to `useOnlineOnlyAction`/`OnlineOnlyReason`, which needs approval), keeping the client refusal as the synchronous backstop.
  - *Transition-gate contract (V8, V9):* an `updateSafety` module (tab-local, in memory) exposes `snapshot()` (pending request count, hold count, unsaved categories, registry revision), `tryAcquireGate(expected)` (synchronous; returns `busy` if any request or hold is active, `stale` if the registry revision or the target worker token differs from what the confirmation showed, otherwise `acquired`), and `releaseGate()`. The controller gains a per-observed-worker opaque `waitingToken` in its state and `acceptUpdate(expectedToken)` (refuses with `stale` if the worker changed), plus a guarded `reloadPage()` for the explicit Reload (activated elsewhere / reload required). Update now: re-check and acquire the gate in one synchronous handler → `acceptUpdate(token)`; any result other than `activating` (including an exception) releases the gate at once; during the attempt the gate is released on `failed`, `unavailable`, or `unresolved` — the controller revokes automatic reload authorization **before** it emits `unresolved` (verified in 4a), so the gate is never released while an automatic reload remains possible; `reloading` keeps it (the page unloads); `reload-required` releases it and offers the explicit, checked Reload. Duplicate acceptance is refused because the gate is already held. Nothing activates when pending work reaches zero; nothing is retried.

    | Review edit | `OwnReviewPanel` `editDraft` (mode `edit`) | differs from the review's own rating/text | save success, Cancel, unmount |
    | New-trip name (My Trips) | `CreateTripForm` `value` | trimmed non-empty | navigation after success (unmount) |
    | Create-then-add name | `NewTripForm` `name` | trimmed non-empty | picker closed or unmounted; the operation itself is covered by the hold |
    | Rename draft | `TripDetailPage` `renameDraft` (`currentDraft.value`) | differs from the trip's current name | success, Cancel, scope change |
    | Sign-in / registration / forgot-password fields | each page's `values` / `email` | any field non-empty (forgot: until `sent`) | navigation or confirmation; unmount |
    | Reset-password fields | `ResetPasswordPage` `values` | any field non-empty | navigation; unmount |
    | Reset token (not a draft) | `auth/resetToken.ts` `capturedToken`, read once into `ResetPasswordPage` `token` | page in `form` state with a token | `clearResetToken()` (success or rejection); unmount |
    | One-time share link (not a draft) | `useTrip` `linkRef` | held | `clearLink()`; unmount |

  - *Registry and revision (V6):* entries `{ id, category, active }` plus one global monotonic `revision`, incremented on every register, unregister, or `touch(id)`. Owners call `touch(id)` from their existing change handlers (a counter, never a value), so editing an already-active draft changes the revision; no value, hash, or serialization is ever used. Ids are opaque (`useId` or a module counter).
  - *React timing (V6):* drafts register and touch in `useLayoutEffect`, which runs synchronously in the commit that follows a discrete input event, before any later user event can be dispatched. The reset token registers in a layout effect on mount (no event can intervene between the first commit and its layout effects). StrictMode: registration is idempotent by id, and the simulated unmount/remount unregisters and re-registers.
  - *Confirmation state model (V7):* `closed` → (Update now with unsaved work) `open{target, revision, categories}`; while open the list is live (subscribing to the registry); Keep working → `closed` (nothing activated or discarded); Update anyway → synchronous `tryAcquireGate({revision, target})`: `busy` (a mutation or hold began) → stays open with "Finish or wait for … first"; `stale` (input changed, a form appeared or disappeared, or the worker was replaced) → refreshed, requiring another click; `acquired` → proceeds. Activation elsewhere or worker replacement while open → closed and replaced by the matching notice. Input is never discarded by opening or cancelling.

V3 approved for `useTrip` and `useAddToTrip`, with request-only accounting elsewhere to be justified (below). V4 approved (registration in `useTrip`; copying never ends protection). V5 approved, with the unfinished create-then-add retry state to be analyzed. V6 approved with synchronous protection and explicit lifecycle verification. V7 approved (bound to the current action, worker, and registry revision). V8 approved with attempt-specific gate ownership and release safeguards. V9 approved (explicit Reload uses the same checks). Drafts: identifiers, categories, active state, and revision only; protect synchronously through existing input handlers where practical, with layout effects reconciling committed state and cleanup — never relying only on a later effect without proving the ordering; edits to an active draft increment the revision; StrictMode cleanup and re-registration verified; no values or hashes of values.
- **Increment 4b-i — mutation safety infrastructure: implemented and verified 2026-11-25; awaiting developer acceptance.**
  - *Supplemental workflow coverage (request-only accounting justified per workflow; "settled" = server state final, "reconciled" = application state matches it):*

    | Workflow | After the mutation response | Reload in that window loses | Classification |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | My Trips create | `navigate` to the trip with a one-time "created" notice; uncertain → page-1 list GET + alert | the notice (the trip appears in the list after reload); for uncertain, the alert (the reload's list read reconciles) | settled; ordinary notice only |
    | Favorite add / remove | local override, pending cleared | nothing (statuses are re-read on load) | settled; reconciled by reload |
    | Review create / edit / delete | draft cleared, own-review and list reloads (GET) | nothing beyond the success announcement; a failed mutation keeps the draft (unsaved input, 4b-ii) | settled; ordinary notice only |

    | Registration | `navigate` to sign-in with a notice | the "Registration received" notice | settled; ordinary notice only |
    | Forgot password | confirmation state | the neutral confirmation | settled; ordinary notice only |

  - *Gate ownership and release:* each attempt owns its gate. **Activated while authorized** → the single authorized reload is consumed and started; the gate is **kept** through unloading. **Reload throws** → phase `reload-required`, gate released. **Document still active** 10 s after the reload started (stall watchdog) → `reload-required`, gate released, no second reload. **Redundant** → `unavailable`, gate released. **Observation timeout** (10 s, unchanged) → reload authorization **revoked first**, phase `unresolved`, **then** the gate released; a later activation → `reload-required`, never an automatic reload. Pre-dispatch failures release immediately. There is no generic `catch`/`finally` release after a possible dispatch. Releases are per acquisition, so a stale lifecycle event cannot release a newer gate; while a reload is in progress, late worker events change nothing. Phase changes precede releases so a listener reacting to a release sees the settled phase. No automatic retry.
  - *Explicit Reload:* `reloadPage({ protectedRevision })` only in `activated-elsewhere` or `reload-required` (an activation actually observed elsewhere or late); same revision check, pending/hold check, and gate; `reload()` throwing or a stalled reload releases the gate and restores the phase. Messages never claim that this page's version was replaced: "…This page keeps running the version it opened with until it is reloaded."
  - *Controls (`UpdateNotice`):* waiting → **Update now** and **Later** (Later keeps the worker-specific page-session postponement and moves focus to `#main-content`); `activated-elsewhere` / `reload-required` → **Reload**; `failed` → **Check again** (re-reads the waiting worker; acceptance remains a new user action); `activating` and `reloading` show status text without controls. While a request or hold is active, Update now / Reload are refused with "Updating (Reloading) isn't available while changes are still being saved. Try again when they finish." — announced in the single existing polite region, focus kept on the control; nothing activates or reloads when the work finishes.
  - *Confirmation:* inline (not a dialog, not a live region), opened when protected categories exist; focus moves to its text. It lists human-readable labels only (never values), states "Anything already saved on the server is not affected.", and offers **Keep working** (focus returns to the opening control) and **Update anyway** / **Reload anyway** (action-specific wording: "Updating reloads this page. Information held only on this page will be lost:" / "Reloading this page loses information held only on this page:"). It is bound to the action, the worker token, and the revision whose list it shows; a revision change (including an edit within the same category) refreshes the list with "What's on this page changed. Review the list and confirm again." and refocuses it; if nothing remains protected it closes (focus to the control) and nothing is sent; a different action or worker closes it. The controller's `stale` or `busy` result is handled the same way, so a click between a revision change and the refresh is still refused.

  - *Infrastructure and event ownership:* `installPrompt.ts` owns the only installation listeners (`beforeinstallprompt`, `appinstalled` on `window`; `change` on `matchMedia("(display-mode: standalone)")`). The application store is created and started when the module is first evaluated — through `AppLayout`'s static imports, i.e. during main-bundle evaluation, before the first render and before `DOMContentLoaded`. `start()` is idempotent (one listener of each kind); `dispose()` removes them (tests). An event dispatched before the bundle evaluates would be missed — not observed, and not verifiable natively. State (`useSyncExternalStore`, stable snapshots replaced only on change): `promptEventSupported` (`"onbeforeinstallprompt" in window`, a capability hint only), `available`, `pending`, `outcome` (`accepted`/`dismissed`/`failed`), `installedReported`, `standalone`. Memory only; nothing persisted.
  - *Capture and prompting:* a `beforeinstallprompt` event with a `prompt` function is retained and its default prevented **only** when retained; while standalone it is neither retained nor prevented. `promptInstall()` is synchronous: it refuses while pending, consumes the retained event **before** calling `prompt()` (no `await` first, preserving transient user activation), then records `userChoice` — "accepted" (the user accepted the browser's prompt; **not** proof of installation), "dismissed", or "failed" (`prompt()` throwing or rejecting, or `userChoice` rejecting). Completions apply only to the current prompt generation and never touch a retained event, so a stale completion cannot clear or replace a newer browser-provided event; a later event makes Install app available again. Nothing prompts automatically or on a schedule; dismissal never re-prompts; acceptance never reloads.
  - *`appinstalled` and standalone:* `appinstalled` (the browser's report) clears a retained event and ends promotion. Standalone evidence — `(display-mode: standalone)` or iOS Safari's `navigator.standalone === true` — is a **hint** (U13), not proof of installation on every device; entering it clears promotion, leaving it does not invent a prompt.
  - *Affordance and placement:* `InstallAffordance` at the end of the header, after the account area (skip link, navigation, notices, and `<main>` unchanged). Prompt retained → **Install app** button (`aria-disabled` while pending; repeated activation ignored in the handler and the store). No prompt → a collapsed `<details>` "Install this app" with generic guidance: "Some browsers let you install this app from their menu, with an option such as Install app or Add to Home Screen. Not every browser offers this." — never a non-functional button. Standalone, or `appinstalled` reported → no promotion. No modal, banner, or repeated promotion.
  - *Truthful messaging:* outcomes — pending ("Your browser is asking whether to install this app."), accepted ("…accepted the installation request. Depending on your browser and device, the app may now be available…"), dismissed ("…Nothing was installed."), failed, and "Your browser reports that this app was installed." The guidance's note keeps installation distinct from data availability: "Installing doesn't download landmarks, trips, maps, or your account for use without a connection: the app itself opens, but information from the server still needs one." (the worker caches only the shell; offline snapshots remain M06-T03; offline maps remain deferred under M06-T04).
  - *Update safety:* installation never activates a worker, posts `SKIP_WAITING`, reloads, acquires or releases the gate, touches the registry or revisions, starts a mutation, produces connectivity evidence, or changes postponement. While the update gate is **held** (an update is being applied) the affordance renders nothing — it only **reads** `gateHeld`, avoiding a competing interaction; no update or safety code changed.

  - *Q4 — new evidence from the final regression (2026-11-26):* the complete Playwright run failed **2/213** (exit 1; evidence preserved): `favorites.spec.ts:236` **recurred** with the same symptom, and `my-trips.spec.ts:677` ("[real] keyboard: nav, create, pagination…") timed out waiting for "Next page" — its earlier assertion that the My Trips heading was visible had **passed**, yet its snapshot shows the page back on Discover (focus on Sign out). Both tests navigate away from Discover shortly after it loads. A second bounded experiment (temporary spec, deleted; anonymous user; Discover loaded and settled, then a map control activated and "Sign in" clicked at once): a keyboard pan before leaving — 10/10 stayed on `/sign-in`; **Zoom in before leaving — reproduced 2/10**: history `push /sign-in`, then four `replaceState` calls to `/` from the Discover page, ending on `/` (`Expected: "/sign-in" Received: "/"`); two further batches (10, 20) did not reproduce (**2/60 overall**).
    - **Production defect established:** a navigation away from the discovery page can be **reverted to Discover** by URL updates the discovery page issues after the user has left it. This is not caused by the installation affordance (the investigation found no layout interaction, and the mechanism is in the discovery page's URL synchronization). It is intermittent and timing-dependent (a map zoom or pan animation in progress when the user navigates).
    - *Most likely root cause (not yet proven at line level):* `MapViewportTracker` (`frontend/src/map/MapViewportTracker.tsx`) reports Leaflet `moveend`/`zoomend`/`whenReady` to `useGeographicDiscovery`, whose `updateViewport` (`frontend/src/routes/useDiscoveryUrlState.ts`) calls `setSearchParams(…, { replace: true })`. `setSearchParams` navigates relative to the Discover route, so a report delivered after the route changed — for example a zoom animation's end, or `map.remove()` stopping an animation during unmount, before the listeners are removed — replaces the new location with `/?…`. Which Leaflet path fires (and whether `whenReady`'s never-removed registration contributes) was not isolated; the replacement URLs were not captured in a reproducing run.
    - *Affected files (expected):* `frontend/src/map/MapViewportTracker.tsx` (and possibly `frontend/src/routes/useDiscoveryUrlState.ts`); tests `frontend/src/map/MapViewportTracker.test.tsx` and a browser regression (e.g. in `e2e/sw/` or the regular project).
    - *Smallest proposed correction (requires approval; not implemented):* stop viewport reporting once the tracker is leaving — an `active` ref cleared in a `useLayoutEffect` cleanup (which runs before `MapContainer`'s passive cleanup removes the map) and checked in `report`, so no `onViewportChange` runs after unmount begins; optionally make `updateViewport` a no-op when the router location is no longer the discovery route. No change to URL semantics while the page is shown.
    - *Proposed regression tests:* a unit test that unmounts the tracker and then fires `moveend`/`zoomend` (and a `whenReady` callback) on the map, asserting `onViewportChange` is not called; a browser test that activates Zoom in and navigates away at once, repeated a bounded number of times, asserting the destination route persists (its detection is probabilistic, so the unit test is the primary guard).
    - Until approved and corrected, the intermittent `favorites.spec.ts:236` and `my-trips.spec.ts:677` failures are attributed to this defect with the above confidence, recorded under **M07-T04**, and M06-T02 is **not** ready for closure.

    - *Stale tracker callbacks:* Leaflet listeners (`moveend`/`zoomend`) are removed in the tracker's passive cleanup and the map is removed with `MapContainer`; the `whenReady` registration is never removed. Every one of these callbacks calls `report`, which is bound to its own instance's `active` ref; that ref is cleared in the layout cleanup and, being per instance, is **never set again** — a new Discover visit mounts a new tracker with its own ref. A callback from an ended lifecycle therefore cannot publish, before or after a return to `/`. *Evidence:* `MapViewportTracker.test.tsx` — captured `moveend`/`zoomend`/`whenReady` after unmount; an event delivered in the passive cleanup phase; "a stale handler from an ended lifecycle never publishes into a later lifecycle" (stale callbacks invoked while a new instance is mounted: neither instance reports; the new instance's own handler does).
    - *Stale text debounce:* `useDiscoveryFilters`' effect clears its pending timer in its cleanup on every change and at unmount (verified by inspection). Unmount cleanup runs when the navigation away commits; React flushes pending passive effects before committing a later update, so the cleanup has run before any navigation back to Discover can render. A timer firing in the gap between the history change and that cleanup is dropped by route ownership (the router's current pathname is no longer `/`). *Evidence:* inspection; the URL-state Order C test for `commitText`; existing `useDiscoveryFilters.test.ts` covers cancellation on Enter and category toggles. *Limitation:* no dedicated unit test asserts the unmount-time `clearTimeout` (that file was outside the 5a inventory).

No application path keeps an old instance's actions reachable after a return to `/`. Pathname-based ownership alone would allow such a write on the same path (it cannot distinguish instances), so the protection for that case is the lifecycle cleanup above, not ownership. *Evidence:* the URL-state test "after a real navigation away and back, the new Discover instance updates the URL normally"; the tracker cross-lifecycle test.

  - *Two databases.* **`tnle-offline-data`** (schema v1) holds the account marker and all account content, so OFF-LIFE-6's lifecycle check can run in the **same transaction** as every commit. **`tnle-offline-state`** (schema v1) holds only records that "Delete all offline data" must not remove (OFF-LIFE-9): the sign-out intent and the durable failure record. Delete all deletes `tnle-offline-data` only.
  - *Stores in `tnle-offline-data`:* `meta` (keyPath `key`): `marker` `{ key, schema_version, account_id, lifecycle_id, verified_at }` and `sequence` `{ key, schema_version, account_id, lifecycle_id, value }` (the lifecycle-scoped invalidation sequence). `landmarks` (keyPath `[account_id, lifecycle_id, landmark_id]`; index `by_lifecycle` on `[account_id, lifecycle_id]`). `trips` (keyPath `[account_id, lifecycle_id, trip_id]`; index `by_lifecycle`). `invalidations` (keyPath `[account_id, lifecycle_id, landmark_id]`; `{ seq, recorded_at }`). `deletions` (keyPath `[account_id, lifecycle_id, kind, item_id]`; `{ seq }` — tombstones for OFF-EV-5(j)). Trip-to-landmark lookups scan the lifecycle's trips (at most 25) instead of adding a non-allowlisted index field.
  - *Store in `tnle-offline-state`:* `state` (keyPath `key`): `signout_intent` `{ key, schema_version, pending: true, created_at }` (OFF-OUT-2) and `failure` `{ key, schema_version, kind: "invalidation" | "cleanup" | "migration", recorded_at }` (OFF-FAIL-3) — no identifiers or content.
  - *Versioning and migration:* the IndexedDB version equals the schema version; `onupgradeneeded` creates or migrates stores; every record carries `schema_version`. An unknown record version or failed migration never displays content, lists the record as unreadable, and locks the library with OFF-LIFE-9 recovery (OFF-SNAP-8). Opening a database whose version is newer than the app's (`VersionError`) locks the library with an explanation.
  - *Open, upgrade, and blocked handling:* every connection handles `versionchange` by closing itself and dropping in-memory account data; upgrades and deletions report `blocked` truthfully ("close the app's other tabs") and never claim completion before `success` (OFF-LIFE-9).
  - *Transactions:* every commit is one `readwrite` transaction over `meta` and the affected stores, performing in order: marker matches the operation's lifecycle; invalidation and deletion sequence checks; revision check; limit check (count on `by_lifecycle`); write. The D22 lock (synchronous `localStorage` read) is checked immediately before the transaction opens, and the intent (state database) at the start of the operation and before commit. No `await` on non-IndexedDB work inside a transaction.
  - *Runtime validation:* hand-written exact-key validators per record type, applied when building a record (from the allowlist only, never by spreading a response) and on every read.
  - *Explicit operations only:* a single `offlineStore` module exposes open, read, save, refresh, remove, cleanup, delete-all, and lifecycle operations; nothing writes in the background.
- **P2 — dependencies (proposed; nothing installed):**
  - **`idb` 8.0.4, exact, frontend production dependency.** Purpose: a small promise wrapper over IndexedDB (typed schemas, `await`-able requests, `tx.done`). Necessity: moderate — ADR-007 already selects IndexedDB *via `idb`*; using the raw API would be a documented deviation. License ISC; no runtime dependencies; ES module; released 2026-10-06 (registry read 2026-11-26). Security: no findings known from the registry metadata; a dry-run and a local `npm audit` comparison at installation (stop on any new high or critical finding, as in M06-T02 1b). Alternatives: the native IndexedDB API with local promise helpers (no dependency, more transaction-lifetime pitfalls); `idb` 7.1.1 (already resolvable transitively, but older). Impact: about 1–2 KB in the production bundle; a second `idb` major in the tree (Workbox's build packages keep 7.x).
  - **`fake-indexeddb` 6.2.8 (or 6.2.7), exact, frontend development dependency (D21).** Purpose: an in-memory IndexedDB for Vitest/jsdom, which has none. Necessity: high for deterministic unit tests of transactions, sequences, limits, and concurrency with deferred promises. License Apache-2.0; Node ≥18; no runtime dependencies; 6.2.8 released 2026-11-08 (6.2.7 on 2026-10-30, if a version older than two weeks is preferred). Security: development-only; audited at installation. Alternatives: hand-written store fakes (would not exercise real transaction semantics); browser-only testing in Playwright (slower; less deterministic). Limitations: not a perfect emulation (quota, eviction, and some `blocked`/`versionchange` timing) — those are verified in Chromium.
- **P3 — persisted allowlists (exact; every record also carries `schema_version`, `account_id`, `lifecycle_id`, `revision` where applicable):** available landmark — `landmark_id`, `status: "available"`, `display_name`, `category`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `saved_at`, optional `source_description`, `source_access_label`, `source_url`, `refreshed_at`; unavailable landmark marker — `landmark_id`, `status: "unavailable"`, `saved_at`, `unavailable_recorded_at`; available trip — `trip_id`, `status: "available"`, `name`, `stops[]`, `distance_summary` (`total_miles`, `measured_legs`, `total_legs`) or `null` with `distance_summary_state` `"server"` or `"invalidated"`, `saved_at`, optional `trip_updated_at`, `refreshed_at`, `partially_invalidated_at`; available stop — `stop_id`, `position`, `is_available: true`, `distance_from_previous_miles`, `landmark: { id, display_name, category, latitude, longitude }`; unavailable stop — `stop_id`, `position`, `is_available: false`, `distance_from_previous_miles: null`, `landmark: { id, is_available: false }`; unavailable trip marker — `trip_id`, `status: "unavailable"`, `saved_at`, `unavailable_recorded_at`; lifecycle metadata — the marker and sequence records above; invalidation metadata — `invalidations` and `deletions` records above; state records — intent and failure above. **Never persisted:** raw API or authentication responses, session tokens or IDs (including the `get-session` and sign-in body tokens), cookies, passwords, reset tokens, share tokens or URLs, email addresses, reviews, ratings, favorite state, `sensitivity_status`, `is_active`, `version`, `is_shared`, `sharing_enabled`, `distance_miles`, source codes or files, and any other field.
- **P4 — account lifecycle and security (proposed):**
  - *Identity:* `account_id` is the user `id` from a successful `GET /api/auth/get-session` (verified identity); nothing else from the session response is kept.
  - *Startup order:* safety lock → state database (intent, failure) → data database open/upgrade → marker versus the session check. Lock present or intent pending: no offline access and no authenticated restoration from `get-session` (OFF-OUT-4, OFF-FAIL-5); Finish signing out / Sign in again offered. Recorded failure: library locked with recovery (OFF-FAIL-3).
  - *Lifecycle:* created only on verified identity with no marker (or an invalidated one), no intent, and no unresolved cleanup (OFF-LIFE-2); continuity updates only `verified_at` (OFF-LIFE-3); invalidation by local sign-out, confirmed absence of a session, account switch, or Delete all (OFF-LIFE-4); account switch cleans up before showing or saving anything (OFF-LIFE-8).
  - *Sign-out ordering (OFF-OUT-1):* (1) in-memory block of offline data and authenticated functionality; (2) BroadcastChannel notice; (3) write the intent to `tnle-offline-state` **first**, then remove the marker in `tnle-offline-data` (two databases cannot share a transaction — the intent alone already blocks access, so this order is fail-safe); on failure, the OFF-FAIL-1 sequence including the D22 lock; (4) best-effort cleanup of the lifecycle; (5) the server request. The server outcome, the device state, and the cleanup status are reported separately; no automatic retry. Local sign-out therefore works offline (it is no longer an online-only action).
  - *Finish signing out / Sign in again (OFF-OUT-5, OFF-OUT-6):* explicit, sequential; credentials are sent only after a confirmed server sign-out.
  - *Serialization (OFF-OUT-7):* sign-in, sign-out, and Finish signing out run under an exclusive Web Locks lock (`navigator.locks`, `ifAvailable` where the operation must not wait); a result arriving after a newer authentication operation began is ignored (generation counter). **Where Web Locks is unavailable, these operations are refused (fail closed) with an explanation** — no `localStorage` or other fallback is introduced (only D22 is approved).
  - *Cross-tab:* BroadcastChannel (`tnle-offline`) messages — lifecycle invalidated, lock set or cleared, intent changed — carry no identifiers; receivers discard in-memory account data and leave offline views. Fallback and backstop: re-validation on focus, visibility, and every library access (OFF-LIFE-7); suspended-tab delay is the accepted limitation.
  - *Delete all offline data:* confirmation text per OFF-LIFE-9; deletes `tnle-offline-data` only; the intent survives in `tnle-offline-state`; if the state database cannot confirm the intent, set the D22 lock first or block the action (OFF-LIFE-9); `blocked` reported truthfully.
  - *Reload and restart:* everything above is re-evaluated at startup; nothing is retried automatically.
- **P5 — invalidation and stale responses (proposed mechanism for OFF-EV-5):** each operation reads the lifecycle `sequence` value at its start (`start_seq`). Applying authoritative unavailability (landmark `404` or valid minimal profile, or a validated unavailable stop) increments the sequence and, in **one** transaction, writes `invalidations[landmark] = seq`, turns the landmark snapshot into an unavailable marker, and rewrites every trip snapshot containing it (exact placeholder stop; `null` for its leg and the next; `distance_summary: null` with `"invalidated"`; `partially_invalidated_at`). An "available" commit may write a landmark's protected fields only if that landmark's invalidation `seq ≤ start_seq`; otherwise a trip stores the stop as unavailable and a landmark save or refresh writes nothing (OFF-EV-5(a)–(c), (g), (i), (k)). Removal writes a deletion tombstone; a save or refresh started before it never recreates the item (j). Overlapping operations have no established order, so unavailability prevails (d), (f). Delayed authoritative unavailable responses are applied when received (h). Restoration is only by an explicit refresh that started after the latest invalidation (OFF-EV-8). Each record's `revision` must match the revision read at the operation's start (e). Trip `404` creates only the trip marker (OFF-EV-7). `401` changes nothing and triggers session verification; transient (`429`, `5xx`, network) and invalid responses leave content unchanged, labelled stale, with distinct messages (OFF-EV-4, AC-18). Persisting a redaction that fails follows OFF-FAIL-1 (block in memory → fallback deletion → D22 lock → disclose).
- **P6 — save, remove, refresh (proposed):** explicit buttons only — **Save for offline**, **Remove offline copy**, **Refresh** — on the landmark profile (full, available profiles only) and the owner trip page; per-item refresh from the library. Save and refresh are online-only actions (they need the server); remove is local and works offline. Limits 200 landmarks and 25 trips per account per device, counted inside the write transaction (markers count; refresh at the limit allowed); quota errors, unavailable IndexedDB, and unreadable records each have their own message; `navigator.storage.persist()` requested once at the first successful save and its result reported honestly; no background save, bulk refresh, automatic eviction, or silent stale fallback (OFF-EV-9, OFF-STORE-1–7).
- **P7 — offline library and presentation (proposed):** routes `/offline` (saved landmarks and trips, unavailable markers, unreadable copies, locked and storage-unavailable states), `/offline/landmarks/:id`, `/offline/trips/:tripId` — served by the existing navigation fallback (no exclusion matches). Snapshot views show no map; coordinates as text with Specification 2's statement that they do not establish public access, legal entry, maintained trails, or safety; "Last synced <approximate date>" and the may-be-outdated warning on every view; markers say "No longer available — recorded <date>"; invalidated trip summaries say the distance summary is unavailable until refreshed; no routing or navigation implied. Online profile and trip pages are never silently replaced; when they fail to load they may link to the saved copy (OFF-UX-2). A navigation entry appears while a valid, unlocked marker exists. Accessible status for every action; neutral empty state (OFF-STORE-7); 320 px layout.
- **P8 — integration with the M06-T02 infrastructure (proposed):** the shell-only service worker, the five exclusions, the connectivity evidence model, request accounting, holds, the registry, the gate, and explicit update acceptance are unchanged. Offline writes are local IndexedDB transactions (atomic; a reload aborts them cleanly), so save, refresh, and remove need **no** gate coordination; the network step of save and refresh is an ordinary counted-free GET. **Lifecycle-critical sequences** (sign-out, Finish signing out, Sign in again, Delete all, cleanup) take an existing **operation hold** for their duration and are refused while the gate is held — consumers of the existing API, no infrastructure change. *Q2:* the reworked sign-out control shows the "Unavailable while the app updates." reason when the hold is refused. *Q5:* the installation note is revised in the library increment to point to explicit "Save for offline" and to state that installation does not save anything (wording for approval then).
- **P9 — verification strategy (proposed):** *unit (Vitest + `fake-indexeddb`):* allowlist enforcement and a storage scan for forbidden values (AC-21: synthetic tokens and emails injected into responses never appear); read validation and unreadable records; lifecycle isolation (AC-1, AC-2); limits inside transactions (AC-23); concurrency with deferred responses — every AC-16 case, AC-3, AC-17; propagation and summary invalidation (AC-13–AC-15); transient/invalid/`401` handling (AC-18, AC-37); storage-failure injection (wrapped `IDBFactory`/`localStorage` stubs; AC-19, AC-20, AC-31, AC-32); safety-lock rules (AC-33, AC-34); migration (open v1, upgrade to a test v2, unknown versions). *Component:* every status and message, focus, freshness labels (AC-22, AC-39). *Real browser (Chromium, chromium-sw):* offline reload of the library (AC-27/AC-28 parts), two accounts on one profile (AC-1), offline sign-out and recovery (AC-6–AC-10, AC-35), two-tab invalidation and fail-closed coordination (AC-5, AC-36 — Web Locks absence emulated by an init script that removes the API, test-only), quota and private-mode limits where reproducible, axe and 320 px. *Manual (recorded):* screen readers (M07-T03), iOS/Safari eviction and Firefox (Specification 7 §10.3), physical erasure (never claimed). *Negative controls (security-critical):* drop the lifecycle check from a commit; persist a raw response (allowlist bypass); ignore the invalidation sequence; ignore deletion tombstones; restore authenticated state from `get-session` while an intent is pending; skip the lock check before a read; count limits outside the transaction; reuse a marker across accounts; let Delete all remove the intent; run two authentication operations concurrently without the lock.
- **P10 — proposed increments (each separately authorized; no snapshot is exposed before 3c is accepted):**
  - **3a — dependencies and storage foundation.** Install `idb` and `fake-indexeddb` (dry-run and audit gate); `frontend/src/offline/` modules for database definitions and opening (two databases, v1, upgrade, `versionchange`, `blocked`), record schemas, allowlist builders, exact validators, the D22 lock module, the state-database records; not wired to the app. *Invariants:* allowlists, validation, no forbidden field ever writable. *NCs:* allowlist bypass; validator accepting extra keys; lock ignored. *Boundary:* nothing user-visible; no IndexedDB opened by the running app.
  - **3b — lifecycle, cleanup, coordination core.** Marker management, lifecycle creation/continuity/invalidation, strict cleanup lock, Delete all (with intent survival and blocked handling), OFF-FAIL-1 sequence and failure records, BroadcastChannel notices, Web Locks serialization helper with fail-closed refusal, startup evaluation; not wired. *NCs:* marker reuse across accounts; Delete all removes the intent; cleanup lock bypass; failure not recorded.
  - **3c — authentication integration.** `AuthProvider`/`AccountNav` changes for OFF-OUT-1–10 (immediate local block, intent, Finish signing out, Sign in again, account switch, confirmed absence of a session), serialized authentication operations, operation holds and the Q2 sign-out reason; existing sign-out tests amended **only with approval** (see decisions). Browser tests for offline sign-out and recovery. Still no snapshot save or read.
  - **3d — snapshot operations core.** Save, refresh, remove for landmarks and trips with evidence classification, the sequence mechanism, propagation, revisions, limits, quota, persistence request; not wired to the UI. Full concurrency suite.
  - **3e — save controls.** Save for offline / Remove offline copy / Refresh on the profile and trip pages with statuses and online-only behavior.
  - **3f — offline library.** Routes and views, freshness and marker labels, unreadable and locked states, the Q5 installation-wording revision.
  - **3g — verification and closure.** The AC-1–AC-40 traceability *(AC-40 added 2026-11-26)* (M06-T03 share), real-browser suites, regression, documentation, and the closure report.
  - *Superseded 2026-11-26 for the remaining increments (3c–3g):* by the approved simplified roadmap — 3c-1, 3c-2, 3d (including the redistributed 3b-iv scope), 3e (save and refresh controls plus the offline library), 3g; see "M06-T03 policy amendments — approval and Step P application". AC-41 is added to the 3g traceability.
- **Risks and ambiguities:** Web Locks unavailability refuses authentication operations (availability cost, by design); BroadcastChannel cannot reach suspended tabs (accepted); `fake-indexeddb` fidelity (mitigated by Chromium tests); storage eviction and private modes (disclosed); `get-session` body tokens must never be persisted (tests scan storage); two-database ordering for OFF-OUT-1 step 3 ("one storage transaction where possible" cannot hold across databases — intent-first ordering proposed); the offline library is reachable on a marker without a live session (by design: the marker selects the library, it is not authentication).
- **Decisions requiring approval:** (D-a) `idb` 8.0.4 as a production dependency; (D-b) `fake-indexeddb` 6.2.8 or 6.2.7 as a development dependency (D21); (D-c) the two-database split and the intent-first ordering for OFF-OUT-1 step 3; (D-d) the lifecycle sequence plus invalidation/deletion records as the OFF-EV-5 mechanism; (D-e) Web Locks for OFF-OUT-7 with fail-closed refusal where unavailable, and BroadcastChannel with focus/visibility re-validation for OFF-LIFE-7; (D-f) **the change to the accepted sign-out behavior** — today a failed sign-out keeps the signed-in interface ("Sign-out didn't complete. You're still signed in."), asserted by `AccountNav.test.tsx` and `e2e/sign-in.spec.ts`; OFF-OUT-1/OFF-OUT-3 require an immediate local sign-out with the server outcome reported separately, so those tests need an approved amendment in 3c (Specification 3 §4.4 itself is consistent with OFF-OUT); (D-g) local sign-out available offline (no longer online-only); (D-h) operation holds for lifecycle-critical sequences; (D-i) routes `/offline`, `/offline/landmarks/:id`, `/offline/trips/:tripId`; (D-j) the increment order 3a–3g. **No conflict with an approved specification or ADR was found**; D-c is an implementation consequence of OFF-OUT-1's "where possible" wording and OFF-LIFE-9's separate-store requirement.
- **Recommended first increment:** **3a** — after approval of D-a and D-b (and preferably D-c), install the two dependencies under the dry-run/audit gate and build the storage foundation with its validators, allowlists, and the D22 lock module, unit-tested with negative controls, without opening any database from the running application.

#### M06-T03 decision dispositions (2026-11-26)

- **Architecture direction and the 3a–3g sequence accepted** with these dispositions; each increment requires separate approval, and no offline snapshot is exposed before account-lifecycle security and the applicable invalidation protections are accepted.
- **D-a — approved:** `idb@8.0.4`, exact, frontend production dependency, subject to the verification and installation gate.
- **D-b — approved:** `fake-indexeddb@6.2.8`, exact, frontend development dependency, subject to the same gate (not substituted with 6.2.7).
- **D-c — approved:** `tnle-offline-data` (the account lifecycle marker colocated with snapshots) and `tnle-offline-state` (the durable sign-out intent and the durable failure record), plus separate minimal D22 storage. **Transactions cannot span the two IndexedDB databases, and the split is not itself proof of safe cross-database coordination.** Before 3b approval: how lifecycle transitions, reads, and writes are coordinated when security state can change between operations on the two databases. BroadcastChannel delivery is not an atomic security barrier. The database definitions are authorized in 3a; the coordination protocol is subject to 3b approval.
- **D-d — approved in principle:** the sequence-based architecture, distinguishing lifecycle identity, the operation-start sequence, the snapshot revision, the authoritative invalidation sequence, and explicit deletion records; all OFF-EV ordering requirements preserved; no generic latest-response-wins rule. Before snapshot operations: precise ordering rules for overlapping available and unavailable responses, deleted copies, lifecycle termination, and later non-overlapping refreshes; safe retention and cleanup rules for invalidation and deletion metadata. Not implemented in 3a.
- **D-e — approved in principle:** Web Locks provide coordination; BroadcastChannel provides notification; durable security state remains authoritative. Before 3b approval: lock names and scopes; acquisition and release ordering; read/write versus lifecycle-transition coordination; cross-database race prevention; interrupted operations; behavior without Web Locks, without BroadcastChannel, and with storage denied; suspended-tab limits; focus and visibility revalidation; recovery and deadlock avoidance; and how unavailable coordination capabilities affect ordinary online authentication (existing authentication is not silently disabled where safe operation can still be established; fail-closed requirements are not weakened).
- **Sign-out behavior amendment (D-f) — approved:** from keeping the signed-in interface after a failed server sign-out (*old:* "Sign-out didn't complete. You're still signed in.") to an immediate local sign-out with separate server-outcome and cleanup reporting (*new:* OFF-OUT-1/OFF-OUT-3). The corresponding amendments to `frontend/src/layout/AccountNav.test.tsx` and `e2e/sign-in.spec.ts` are approved for **Increment 3c only**; the existing expectations are preserved until then.
- **D-g — approved:** offline (local) sign-out per OFF-OUT, OFF-LIFE, and D22; no automatic server sign-out retry; no silent session restoration while an unresolved intent exists.
- **D-h — revised (not approved as proposed):** IndexedDB transaction atomicity does not establish that a complete user-initiated operation can be interrupted safely. Before the relevant increments, provide a coordination design that assesses save, refresh, remove, invalidation, cleanup, and authentication-lifecycle operations across their complete boundaries — the network request before the transaction, an authoritative unavailable response before its durable invalidation, transaction completion, required follow-up security operations, user-visible completion or failure, reload interruption, and the existing update-gate refusal behavior. Lifecycle-critical sequences require the existing operation-hold coordination; whether snapshot operations need additional holds or gate checks is to be determined. No update-safety change in 3a.
- **D-i — approved:** the `/offline` route family; no route implementation in 3a.
- **D-j — approved:** 3a–3g as proposed, each separately authorized.

#### M06-T03 Increment 3a — dependencies and storage foundation: implemented and verified 2026-11-26; awaiting developer acceptance

- *Files (exact):* `frontend/package.json` (two lines added); root `package-lock.json`; new `frontend/src/offline/records.ts` (contracts and stored-record validators), `frontend/src/offline/projection.ts` (allowlist projections), `frontend/src/offline/db.ts` (database definitions; explicit open and close), `frontend/src/offline/safetyLock.ts` (D22 primitive); tests `frontend/src/offline/records.test.ts`, `projection.test.ts`, `db.test.ts`, `safetyLock.test.ts` (each sets up `fake-indexeddb` locally); this plan. No test setup, Vitest, or TypeScript configuration changed. No application file imports `src/offline` (verified by search); the production bundle contains neither the database names, the lock key, nor `idb`.
- *Dependency verification (before installation):*
  - `idb@8.0.4` — registry: license ISC; ES module (CJS `main`, ESM `module`, typed); no `dependencies`, `peerDependencies`, or `optionalDependencies`; no `engines`; integrity `sha512-jd0ITCrN…i30Q==` (shasum `95405f3d…`); 13 files, 82,588 B unpacked; npm registry signatures present; no SLSA provenance attestation published. Repository `github.com/jakearchibald/idb`: tag `v8.0.4` (2026-10-06, commit `654c746`), release body "8.0.4", no breaking or security note shown; repository not archived. Compatibility: a thin wrapper over the standard IndexedDB API available in all current browsers.
  - `fake-indexeddb@6.2.8` — license Apache-2.0; ES module with CJS build and types; no runtime, peer, or optional dependencies; `engines.node >=18` (local Node 22); integrity `sha512-mpVW/HLU…59XEQ==` (shasum `79593572…`); 120 files, 348,645 B; registry signatures present; no provenance attestation. Repository `github.com/dumbmatter/fakeIndexedDB`: tag `v6.2.8` (2026-11-08) at `a58f9b9…`, **matching the registry `gitHead`**; release notes: two fixes, including a regression introduced in 6.2.6 (`transaction.abort()` in an error handler) — a reason to prefer 6.2.8 over 6.2.7; no security note.

No `change`, `update`, or `remove` entries. Both dry-runs left `package.json` and the lockfile byte-identical (SHA-256).

Lockfile: **3 package entries changed** — the `frontend` workspace entry, a new `frontend/node_modules/idb` 8.0.4 (nested because Workbox's build packages keep `idb` 7.1.1 at the root), and a new `node_modules/fake-indexeddb` 6.2.8; no other package changed. *After:* audit still **16 (1/12/3/0), identical per package, advisory, and path**; neither new package appears in it (absence of a finding is not a claim that the packages are vulnerability-free). `npm audit signatures`: 799 packages with verified registry signatures, 246 with verified attestations. No `npm audit fix`.
- *Record contracts (exact allowlists; validated on write and read; `schema_version` 1 everywhere; UUIDs canonical lower case; timestamps in `Date#toISOString` form — ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds, round-trip checked):*
  - **Available landmark** — key `[account_id, lifecycle_id, landmark_id]`; required `schema_version`, `account_id`, `lifecycle_id`, `revision` (integer ≥1), `landmark_id`, `status: "available"`, `display_name` (non-empty), `category` (one of `arch`, `bald`, `falls`, `lake`, `other`, `peak`, `rock`, `sink` — the backend's `CATEGORY_DEFINITIONS`), `latitude` [−90, 90] and `longitude` [−180, 180] (finite), `saved_at`; optional `source_description`, `source_access_label`, `source_url` (string or null), `refreshed_at`.
  - **Unavailable landmark marker** — required `schema_version`, `account_id`, `lifecycle_id`, `revision`, `landmark_id`, `status: "unavailable"`, `saved_at`, `unavailable_recorded_at`; nothing else (no name, category, coordinates, source, or `refreshed_at`).
  - **Available trip** — key `[account_id, lifecycle_id, trip_id]`; required ownership, `revision`, `trip_id`, `status: "available"`, `name` (1–100 code points), `stops`, `distance_summary`, `distance_summary_state` (`"server"` with a summary consistent with the stops — `total_legs = max(n−1, 0)`, `measured_legs` equal to the measured legs, `total_miles` null exactly when none are measured and otherwise their sum within rounding — or `"invalidated"` with `distance_summary: null`), `saved_at`; optional `trip_updated_at`, `refreshed_at`, `partially_invalidated_at`. **Prohibited** (also by exact keys): `version`, `is_shared`, `sharing_enabled`, `share_url`, `created_at`, tokens, owner identifiers.
  - **Available stop** — exactly `stop_id`, `position` (= index), `is_available: true`, `distance_from_previous_miles` (finite ≥0 or null; non-null only after an available stop; null on the first stop), `landmark` exactly `{ id, display_name, category, latitude, longitude }`. **Unavailable stop** — exactly `stop_id`, `position`, `is_available: false`, `distance_from_previous_miles: null`, `landmark` exactly `{ id, is_available: false }`. At most 25 stops; unique stop and landmark IDs.
  - **Unavailable trip marker** — ownership, `revision`, `trip_id`, `status: "unavailable"`, `saved_at`, `unavailable_recorded_at`; nothing else.
  - **Account marker** (`meta`, key `"marker"`) — `key`, `schema_version`, `account_id`, `lifecycle_id`, `verified_at`; no email, session ID, token, or cookie value.
  - **Lifecycle sequence** (`meta`, key `"sequence"`) — `key`, ownership, `value` (integer ≥0).
  - **Invalidation** — key `[account_id, lifecycle_id, landmark_id]`; ownership, `landmark_id`, `seq` (≥1), `recorded_at`.
  - **Deletion** — key `[account_id, lifecycle_id, kind, item_id]`; ownership, `kind` (`"landmark"` or `"trip"`), `item_id`, `seq` (≥1).
  - **Sign-out intent** (`tnle-offline-state`, key `"signout_intent"`) — `key`, `schema_version`, `pending: true`, `created_at`; no identifier or credential.
  - **Failure record** (`tnle-offline-state`, key `"failure"`) — `key`, `schema_version`, `kind` (`invalidation`, `cleanup`, `migration`), `recorded_at`; no detail.
  - `revision` is carried by every content record (snapshots and markers); metadata and state records carry none. The 200/25 limits are constants only (transactional enforcement is a later increment).
- *Validation and projection:* stored records are validated as untrusted data — exact key sets (any unknown field rejects), plain-object prototypes only, every type and range checked; a rejection returns only a reason code (`unknown-or-missing-field`, `schema-version`, `ownership`, `identifier`, `status`, `timestamp`, `revision`, `value`, `not-object`), never record contents. Projection (`projection.ts`) is separate: it builds each record field by field from **already validated** API data (`isValidFullProfile`; `parseOwnerTripResponse`, which rebuilds owner trips from approved fields), additionally requires the requested ID and known categories, never spreads a response, and re-validates its own output with the stored-record validator (returning `null` rather than an invalid record). Markers are projected from the previous record's identifier and original `saved_at` only. No user-facing recovery in 3a.
- *Database schema (v1; IndexedDB version = schema version):* `tnle-offline-data` — `meta` (keyPath `key`; marker and sequence), `landmarks`, `trips`, `invalidations` (each keyPath `[account_id, lifecycle_id, <id>]`), `deletions` (keyPath `[account_id, lifecycle_id, kind, item_id]`); each content store has index `by_lifecycle` on `[account_id, lifecycle_id]` (`unique: false`, not multi-entry); no auto-increment. All five stores can join one `readwrite` transaction, so the marker check can share a transaction with snapshot writes. `tnle-offline-state` — `state` (keyPath `key`). Values are typed `unknown` so every read must be validated. Upgrade structure: `if (oldVersion < 1)` creates v1; later versions add their own steps; no historical migrations invented.
- *Open and close:* `openOfflineDataDatabase` and `openOfflineStateDatabase` are explicit calls (importing opens nothing — tested); results `open`, `unavailable` (no IndexedDB, or `SecurityError`), `newer-version` (`VersionError`; the newer database is left untouched — tested), `failed` (anything else; nothing created — tested). A connection that blocks another context's upgrade or deletion closes itself and reports `onVersionChange` (tested: another context's deletion then succeeds); `onBlocked` and `onTerminated` are forwarded. No database is ever deleted or recreated on failure, and no security state is cleared. *Limitation:* a blocked **upgrade** cannot be exercised until a v2 exists (`onBlocked` is wired but untested).
- *D22 primitive (`safetyLock.ts`):* one `localStorage` entry `tnle-offline-safety-lock` = `"true"`, nothing else. `read()` returns `absent`, `present` (any stored value), or `unreadable` (storage unreachable or throwing — never reported as absent); `isBlocked()` is true for an in-memory block, a present lock, or an unreadable store. `set()` blocks in memory first, then writes and reads back; it returns `{ durable: true }` only when the value reads back, otherwise `{ durable: false, reason: "unavailable" | "write-failed" }` with the in-memory block kept (the OFF-FAIL-4 limitation applies). `clearAfterVerifiedRecovery()` is **restricted** to the verified recovery of 3b/3c (documented; no application path calls it — the module is not imported by the app); it removes the durable lock and verifies the removal before releasing the in-memory block, otherwise it returns `clear-failed` or `unavailable` with every block kept. No storage is touched until a method is called.
