#### M06-T03 Increment 3b — architecture plan (2026-11-26) — PENDING APPROVAL; nothing implemented

- *Inputs reviewed (targeted):* Specification 6 v1.1 §12.1–§12.8 (OFF-LIFE, OFF-OUT, OFF-EV, OFF-FAIL, OFF-CONC, OFF-STORE), the ADR-007 amendment (D22), the accepted 3a modules (`records.ts`, `db.ts`, `safetyLock.ts`), `AuthProvider`/`AccountNav`/`api/auth.ts`, and `pwa/updateSafety.ts` (`acquireHold()` returns `null` while the gate is held; `tryAcquireGate()` refuses while any hold or mutation request is active; every release is per-acquisition and idempotent).
- **Q13 finding:** our own connections close on `versionchange`, so a blocked upgrade of *our* open can only be produced when another connection that ignores `versionchange` holds an older version open. With production v1 the only older version is "none", which cannot be held open. A test can still exercise the identical code path **without a production v2** if the generic `openWith(name, version, upgrade, events)` helper in `db.ts` is exported (no behavior change; it already takes name and version as arguments): a test opens a test-only database at v1 through a raw connection that ignores `versionchange`, then calls `openWith` for v2 of that test-only name — `onBlocked` fires; closing the raw connection lets it complete. Proposed for 3b-i (a one-line export in an accepted 3a file — **requires approval**).

##### D-c — cross-database coordination protocol

- **Premise:** IndexedDB transactions cannot span `tnle-offline-data` and `tnle-offline-state`, and the D22 lock lives in `localStorage`. Atomicity across them is replaced by **mutual exclusion**: every operation that reads or writes offline security state runs inside one Web Lock, the **offline security lock** `tnle-offline-security` — **shared** for short offline-access operations (reads, snapshot commits), **exclusive** for every lifecycle transition (lifecycle creation, termination, sign-out intent record and clear, marker removal, cleanup, delete all, failure record, D22 set and clear). Because transitions are exclusive, no transition can occur between an access operation's authorization checks and its read or commit. Locks are held only around storage work — never across a network request. BroadcastChannel only *notifies*; it is never relied on for atomicity.
- **Tab-local security generation:** each tab keeps an in-memory `securityGeneration` counter and a `blocked` flag. Any local block, received notice, focus/visibility revalidation that finds a change, or lifecycle transition increments the generation synchronously. Every read result is tagged with the generation and `lifecycle_id` at which it was authorized; it is **published into application state only if** the generation is unchanged and the tab is not blocked at publication time (checked synchronously just before publishing). A late result is discarded.
- **Operation protocol** (✓ = required):

  | Operation | Lock | Durable checks (in order) | Transaction boundaries | Memory changes | Notification | Failure | Interruption |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Read security state (startup, focus, visibility, before any library access) | shared | D22 `read()`; state DB `failure`, `signout_intent`; data DB `marker` | one readonly tx per database | sets the evaluated state; increments generation if it changed | — | any read failure → *storage unavailable* (blocked) | nothing written |
  | Read marker | shared (within the read above) | as above | readonly data tx | — | — | invalid marker → treated as unreadable (cleanup required) | — |
  | Read snapshots | shared | D22, intent, failure, then marker matches the expected lifecycle **in the same readonly data tx** as the snapshot reads; every record validated | state readonly tx, then one data readonly tx | none until publication | — | invalid records → listed unreadable, never shown | — |
  | Publish snapshots | none (synchronous) | generation and `lifecycle_id` unchanged; not blocked | — | publishes or discards | — | discard silently | — |
  | Commit snapshot change (3d) | shared | D22 `isBlocked()` immediately before; intent/failure absent; then **in one readwrite data tx**: marker = operation's lifecycle, sequence/invalidation/deletion/revision checks (D-d), limits, write | state readonly tx, then one data readwrite tx | publication of the result as above | — | commit nothing; report | IndexedDB aborts the tx; nothing partial |
  | Create lifecycle | exclusive | verified session (fetched **before** the lock); D22 absent (not unreadable); no intent; no failure; no marker or residual records | data readwrite tx (marker + sequence) | generation++, state *active* | `lifecycle-changed` | create nothing; state unchanged | marker absent → nothing created |
  | Terminate lifecycle (sign-out, confirmed absence, account switch, delete all) | exclusive | — | see sign-out ordering; marker removal in a data readwrite tx | blocked, generation++ **before** acquiring the lock | `lifecycle-ended` **before** acquiring the lock, again after commit | OFF-FAIL-1 escalation | see sign-out ordering |
  | Record sign-out intent | exclusive | — | state readwrite tx (`signout_intent`) | already blocked | — | → D22 `set()` | intent absent: D22 or in-memory only (disclosed) |
  | Remove marker | exclusive (same hold as the intent) | intent recorded (or D22 set) first | data readwrite tx | — | — | marker remains but the intent/D22 blocks it; cleanup reported incomplete | intent already durable → safe |
  | Record durable failure | exclusive | — | state readwrite tx (`failure`) | — | `failure-changed` | → D22 `set()` | — |
  | Delete the data database | exclusive | intent preservation checked first (see Delete all) | `deleteDatabase`; then a verification open and read | — | `lifecycle-ended`; other tabs' connections receive `versionchange` and close | blocked → reported; failure recorded | partially deleted → next startup sees residual records → cleanup required |
  | Clear security state after verified recovery | exclusive | all clearing conditions (D22 protocol) re-verified **inside** the lock | state readwrite tx (failure/intent), then D22 `clearAfterVerifiedRecovery()` last | generation++ | `recovered` | nothing cleared; state unchanged | earlier steps done, lock still set → still blocked (safe) |

- **Already-rendered information in another tab:** durable protection is immediate for every subsequent read in every tab (they must take the shared lock and see the new state). Information *already rendered* in another tab is removed only when that tab processes the notice or revalidates on focus/visibility/access; suspended or frozen tabs cannot be reached (accepted, OFF-LIFE-7). This is not claimed to be instantaneous.

##### D-e — lock architecture

- **Exactly two locks** (Web Locks, origin-wide across tabs):
  - `tnle-offline-security` — **shared** for offline reads and snapshot commits; **exclusive** for lifecycle transitions, cleanup, delete all, failure records, and D22 changes. Storage-only, held for milliseconds, never across a network request.
  - `tnle-auth` — **exclusive** for authentication operations (sign-in, server sign-out, Finish signing out, Sign in again). It **spans the server request** (demonstrated necessity: OFF-OUT-7 forbids overlapping authentication operations, including across tabs).
  - No separate lock for database deletion or recovery: both are exclusive `tnle-offline-security` operations.
- **Ordering:** `tnle-auth` → `tnle-offline-security`, never the reverse. A storage transition inside an authentication operation takes `tnle-offline-security` (exclusive) briefly and releases it **before** the network request. Nothing acquires `tnle-auth` while holding `tnle-offline-security`, so no lock cycle exists.
- **Nesting and reentrancy:** Web Locks are not reentrant (a nested request for a held lock would wait forever). A tab-local guard records which lock this tab holds and **throws a programming error** on any nested or reverse-order acquisition. There is no shared-to-exclusive upgrade: an operation that needs a transition releases its shared hold first and re-validates under the exclusive lock.
- **Cancellation and waiting:** requests carry an `AbortSignal`. Short access operations use `ifAvailable` where waiting would be pointless (for example a background revalidation) and otherwise wait. A transition that has been waiting more than a few seconds shows "Waiting for this app's other tabs…" with a Cancel action — a **user-visible status, not a lock expiry** (no timer ever releases or steals a lock).
- **Failure while waiting:** an abort or a rejected request means the operation did not start; nothing is written; the in-memory block (if already applied) stays.
- **Failure while holding:** the callback's error propagates; the browser releases the lock when the callback settles; partially completed transitions are resolved by the next state evaluation (each step is ordered so that every intermediate durable state is blocking, see sign-out ordering).
- **Termination:** the browser releases a terminated or closed tab's locks. **Suspended tabs:** a frozen tab holds a lock only if frozen mid-callback (milliseconds for `tnle-offline-security`); a transition then waits (with the visible status) and the in-memory block in the initiating tab is unaffected. `tnle-auth` held by a suspended tab mid-request delays other authentication operations until it resumes or is discarded — accepted and disclosed.
- **Stale operations:** every operation records the generation and `lifecycle_id` it started with; after any await it re-checks both and aborts if they changed.
- **Database version change:** every connection closes on `versionchange` (3a) and increments the generation; the next access reopens under the lock and re-evaluates. **Blocked deletion:** reported ("close the app's other tabs"); never reported complete until `success` and a verification read.
- **Immediate local blocking never waits for a lock:** setting the tab's `blocked` flag, incrementing the generation, and posting the notice are synchronous and lock-free; only the durable steps wait for `tnle-offline-security`.

##### Immediate blocking and sign-out ordering

1. User initiates sign-out (the existing operation hold is taken — D-h).
2. **Synchronously:** `blocked = true`, generation++, authenticated UI and offline views hidden (OFF-OUT-1 step 1). No lock needed.
3. **Synchronously:** BroadcastChannel `lifecycle-ended` (best effort; OFF-OUT-1 step 2).
4. Acquire `tnle-auth` (exclusive) — sign-out does not overlap another authentication operation.
5. Acquire `tnle-offline-security` (exclusive). Under it: write `signout_intent` to `tnle-offline-state` (durable intent, OFF-OUT-1 step 3); on failure → OFF-FAIL-1 (D22 `set()`; if that fails, memory-only, disclosed).
6. Still under it: remove the marker and mark the lifecycle's records for cleanup in one `tnle-offline-data` readwrite tx (existing publications are already prevented by step 2's generation change; operations holding the shared lock finished before the exclusive lock was granted, and any later commit fails the marker check).
7. Still under it: best-effort cleanup of the lifecycle's records (logical deletion + verification read); outcome recorded (`failure: cleanup` on failure). Release `tnle-offline-security`.
8. Server sign-out request (under `tnle-auth` only). Confirmed → clear the intent under a brief exclusive `tnle-offline-security` (only when cleanup is also complete or recorded separately; the intent is cleared only on confirmed server sign-out — OFF-OUT-5). Unconfirmed → the intent remains; no retry.
9. Report three outcomes separately: **signed out on this device**; **server sign-out** confirmed / not confirmed; **cleanup** complete / incomplete / failed.

- *Guarantees:* **initiating tab** — immediate (synchronous) hiding and blocking. **Other active tabs** — prompt on the notice, and in every case before any further offline read (the shared lock sees the durable state). **Suspended tabs** — only on resume; rendered content may remain on screen until then (accepted). **After termination or restart** — whatever is durable: the intent (or D22) and marker state.
- *Interval between step 2 and step 5:* if the tab terminates there, **no durable evidence exists yet** — the marker and server session remain, and after restart the app would treat the lifecycle as active unless the server session was meanwhile ended elsewhere. This cannot be prevented; it is minimised (steps 2–5 contain no network wait; the lock wait is the only delay) and disclosed as a limitation. Termination after step 5 leaves the intent, so restart stays signed out on the device.

##### Capability and failure matrix (grouped)

| Situation | Read offline | Create lifecycle | Save/refresh | Remove one | Delete all | Normal sign-in | Local sign-out | Server sign-out | Finish signing out | Sign in again |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A.** All capabilities; no intent, failure, or D22; verified session matches marker (or no marker) | ✓ | ✓ (if no marker) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — | — |
| **B.** Intent present (any marker state) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ (intent preserved) | ✗ | — (already) | ✓ (as Finish) | ✓ | ✓ |
| **C.** D22 present with no explaining IndexedDB record (lock is the only evidence) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ (conservative) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| **D.** D22 present with an explaining failure/intent record | as B or E | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | as B or E | ✓ | ✓ | as B | as B |
| **E.** Durable failure record (cleanup/invalidation/migration), no intent | ✗ (locked) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | — | — |
| **F.** Session check confirms a **different** account than the marker | ✗ until cleanup | after cleanup | ✗ until cleanup | ✗ | ✓ | (already signed in) | ✓ | ✓ | — | — |
| **G.** Web Locks **unavailable** | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | **decision required** (see below) | ✓ (memory block; durable steps refused) | **decision required** | ✗ | ✗ |
| **H.** BroadcastChannel unavailable (others available) | ✓ (revalidation on focus/visibility/access) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | as B | as B |
| **I.** IndexedDB unavailable or denied | ✗ ("offline storage unavailable", never empty) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ (if D22 absent) | ✓ (D22 attempted as durable evidence; else memory-only, disclosed) | ✓ | ✓ (if D22 set) | ✓ (if D22 set) |
| **J.** `localStorage` unavailable (D22 unreadable) | ✗ (cannot evaluate D22) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ (intent preservation must then be confirmed in IndexedDB, else blocked) | ✓ if IndexedDB shows no intent/failure | ✓ | ✓ | as B | as B |
| **K.** Server unreachable / session unverifiable | ✓ for the existing marker (marker selects the library; not authentication) | ✗ (needs verified identity) | ✗ (online-only) | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ (online-only) | ✓ | ✗ (reported unconfirmed) | ✗ until reachable | ✗ until reachable |

- **Ordinary online authentication and missing capabilities:** today sign-in and sign-out work in every browser. OFF-OUT-7 requires authentication operations never to overlap, coordinated across tabs, and refusal when safe coordination cannot be established. Without Web Locks (Safari before 15.4, Firefox before 96, Chromium before 69) no reliable cross-tab mutual exclusion exists without new storage (only D22 is approved in `localStorage`). **Decision required (DR-1):** (a) **strict** — refuse sign-in, sign-out's server step, Finish signing out, and Sign in again when Web Locks is unavailable, with an explanation (local sign-out's in-memory block still applies); (b) **scoped** — keep today's ordinary sign-in/sign-out in such browsers, serialized within the tab only, with **all offline features disabled** there (no lifecycle, so no offline security state can exist), which would need a Specification 6 clarification of OFF-OUT-7. *Recommendation:* (b), because it does not weaken the existing application and no offline state can conflict, but it requires the clarification; (a) satisfies the current text literally.
- **Conflicts prevented:** in every row where an intent, D22, or a failure exists, normal sign-in is replaced by Sign in again (or refused) so no authentication operation can conflict with unresolved offline security state.

##### Lifecycle state machine

- **States:** `none` (no lifecycle); `active(account, lifecycle)`; `blocked-local` (in-memory, transient, before durable steps complete); `intent-pending` (durable intent; server sign-out unresolved) with cleanup status complete/incomplete/failed; `cleanup-incomplete` (no intent; residual records or a cleanup failure; library locked); `safety-lock` (D22 present; conservative); `recovered` (transient: verified recovery completed → `none`); `storage-unavailable` (IndexedDB or `localStorage` unusable; offline features off).
- **Transitions:**

  | From → To | Trigger | Preconditions | Durable changes | Memory | Notify | Lock | Then permitted | On failure |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | none → active | verified session after sign-in or session check | no intent, failure, D22, marker, residual records | marker + sequence | generation++ | `lifecycle-changed` | exclusive | read/save/remove | stay `none` |
  | active → active | session check confirms the same account | — | `verified_at` only | — | — | exclusive (brief) | unchanged | unchanged (reload, connectivity, and rechecks never create a lifecycle) |
  | active → blocked-local | sign-out pressed | — | none yet | blocked, generation++ | `lifecycle-ended` | none | — | — |
  | blocked-local → intent-pending | intent durable | — | intent; marker removed; cleanup | — | after commit | auth + exclusive | Finish signing out, Sign in again, Delete all | → safety-lock (D22) or memory-only |
  | intent-pending → none | server sign-out confirmed **and** cleanup verified | — | intent cleared | generation++ | `recovered` | auth, then exclusive | sign in | intent kept |
  | intent-pending → cleanup-incomplete | server confirmed, cleanup failed | — | intent cleared; `failure: cleanup` kept | — | yes | exclusive | Retry cleanup, Delete all | stay |
  | active → cleanup-incomplete | confirmed absence of session (OFF-OUT-8) or account switch | — | marker removed; cleanup; failure on failure | blocked, generation++ | yes | exclusive | Retry cleanup, Delete all, sign in (online) | → safety-lock |
  | cleanup-incomplete → none | cleanup verified | no residual records | `failure` cleared | generation++ | `recovered` | exclusive | create lifecycle | stay |
  | any → safety-lock | durable IndexedDB recording failed | — | D22 set | blocked | `lock-set` | exclusive | Finish signing out, Sign in again, Delete all | memory-only (disclosed) |
  | safety-lock → none | verified recovery (D22 protocol) | all clearing conditions | D22 cleared last | generation++ | `recovered` | auth (if a sign-out may be unresolved) + exclusive | normal | stay locked |
  | any → storage-unavailable | open/read failure | — | none | blocked | — | — | online features only | — |

  A valid server cookie never overrides `intent-pending` or `safety-lock` (OFF-OUT-4).

##### D22 recovery protocol

- **Relationships:** the **intent** (state DB) records an unresolved sign-out; the **failure record** (state DB) records unresolved invalidation, cleanup, or migration; the **marker** (data DB) selects the active lifecycle; **D22** stands in for any of these when IndexedDB could not record them; the **in-memory block** stands in for everything when nothing durable could be written.
- **Escalation (OFF-FAIL-1):** immediate in-memory block → attempt the durable IndexedDB step → on failure, attempt logical deletion of the affected records (or another durable record) → on failure, D22 `set()` → if `durable: false`, memory-only (disclose OFF-FAIL-4) → notify → disclose and offer Retry / Delete all. Cases: *invalidation write fails* → delete the affected snapshots; else D22. *Cleanup fails* → `failure: cleanup` in state DB; else D22. *State DB write fails* (intent/failure) → D22. *Data DB write fails* → state DB failure record; else D22. *Lock persistence fails* → memory-only. *Lock clearing fails* → stays locked (no state change). *All storage fails* → memory-only; the risk is disclosed.
- **Reported states (never conflated):** durable invalidation (recorded and read back); logical deletion (deleted and verified by a read); safety-lock protection (D22 read back); memory-only protection; unconfirmed cleanup. Physical erasure is never claimed.
- **Only authorized clearing of D22:** inside the exclusive lock (and `tnle-auth` when a sign-out may be unresolved), after re-verifying that (1) every required invalidation is durably recorded or the affected records are logically deleted and verified; (2) no residual record of an invalidated lifecycle is readable (verification scan); (3) where a sign-out may be unresolved (an intent exists, or D22 is the only evidence), the server sign-out is confirmed or a Sign in again has completed. Then `clearAfterVerifiedRecovery()` runs **last**. Never on sign-in, reload, reopening, or database deletion alone; a missing lock is not evidence of recovery.

##### Delete all offline data

1. Operation hold; confirmation (OFF-LIFE-9 text).
2. Synchronous block, generation++, `lifecycle-ended` notice.
3. Exclusive `tnle-offline-security`. Read the state DB: if an intent exists it stays (it is in the other database); if the state DB **cannot be read**, set D22 first — if D22 is not durable either, **block the action** and disclose (OFF-LIFE-9).
4. Delete `tnle-offline-data` (other tabs' connections close on `versionchange`). `blocked` → report "close the app's other tabs", record `failure: cleanup`, stay locked. Error → record `failure: cleanup` (or D22).
5. Verification: reopen and confirm the stores are empty. Then clear `failure: cleanup` (if it was recorded for this) — **never** the intent; D22 only under the D22 protocol.
6. Release; notify `recovered` or the remaining locked state.
- *Deletion succeeded but a later security-state step failed:* the data is gone but the failure record or D22 remains → still locked until a retry clears it under the protocol (safe direction). *Blocked or partial:* the failure record keeps the library locked on every startup (OFF-FAIL-3). Database deletion is never evidence of a confirmed server sign-out; a new lifecycle needs a verified session with no intent, failure, or D22.

##### D-d — ordering model, concurrency table, and metadata retention

- **Concepts:** *lifecycle identity* — `lifecycle_id` in the marker; every commit requires marker = the operation's lifecycle. *Operation-start sequence* (`start_seq`) — the lifecycle `sequence.value` read under the shared lock when the operation starts (before its request). *Snapshot revision* — per record; a commit requires the stored revision to equal the one read at start (`base_revision`, or "absent"). *Authoritative invalidation sequence* — `invalidations[landmark].seq`, assigned by incrementing `sequence` when unavailability is applied. *Deletion record* — `deletions[kind,item].seq`, assigned by incrementing `sequence` on user removal. Sequences increase only on invalidation and deletion; an available commit never increments it. An operation's protected fields for landmark L may be written only if `invalidations[L].seq ≤ start_seq`; an item may be (re)created only if `deletions[item].seq ≤ start_seq`.

  | Case | May commit | Metadata consulted | Records changed | Removed | Restoration later |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Two overlapping available responses (same item) | the first commit; the second fails its revision check (or, for two first saves, finds the record and is a duplicate no-op — OFF-STORE-3) | revision | one record | — | — |
  | Available, then authoritative unavailable (non-overlapping) | both, in order | invalidation (new) | snapshot → marker; trips propagated | protected fields everywhere | yes, by a refresh started after the invalidation |
  | Unavailable, then a stale available (started before the invalidation) | unavailable only | `start_seq` vs invalidation seq | — | — | yes, by a new refresh |
  | Late unavailable after an overlapping available committed | both; unavailability applied last and prevails (OFF-EV-5(d), (h)) | invalidation | marker; trips propagated | protected fields | yes, by a later refresh |
  | Later non-overlapping successful refresh after invalidation | yes (`start_seq ≥ inv.seq`) | invalidation, revision | that landmark snapshot only (not trips — OFF-EV-8) | — | — |
  | Snapshot removed while a save/refresh is in flight | no (`deletion.seq > start_seq`) | deletion | — | — | yes, by a new explicit save |
  | Removed, then explicitly saved again | the new save (`start_seq ≥ deletion.seq`) | deletion, revision | new record (revision 1) | — | — |
  | Lifecycle terminated during an operation | no (marker mismatch or absent) | marker | — | (cleanup handles the old lifecycle) | in a new lifecycle only |
  | Account switched during an operation | no (marker mismatch) | marker | — | — | — |
  | Landmark invalidated while an affected **trip save** is in flight | yes, with that stop stored as the unavailable placeholder and adjacent legs null (OFF-EV-5(c)) | invalidation per stop landmark | trip snapshot | the stop's protected fields | by a later trip refresh |
  | Same, **trip refresh** in flight | yes, same rule; revision must still match | invalidation, revision | trip snapshot | as above | as above |
  | Concurrent landmark and trip invalidation | both apply; each increments `sequence` | invalidation | marker(s); trips propagated | protected fields | per item |
  | Authoritative trip unavailability (`404`) | yes; trip marker (revision++), no landmark change (OFF-EV-7) | revision | trip → marker | trip content | yes, by a later trip refresh |
  | Transient failure (network, `429`, `5xx`) | no change | — | — | — | the snapshot is kept, labelled stale |
  | Invalid payload | no change ("unexpected server response") | — | — | — | — |
  | Storage failure during authoritative invalidation | — | — | attempt deletion of the affected snapshots → D22 → memory-only | in memory: never displayed again in this instance | after recovery, by refresh |

- **Retention:** invalidation and deletion records are kept for the **whole lifecycle** and removed only with it (cleanup or Delete all). No time-based expiry. *Growth:* both stores are keyed per item (re-invalidation or re-deletion overwrites the same key), so they are bounded by the distinct items ever saved or contained in saved trips during the lifecycle — at most a few thousand small records in practice (200 landmarks; 25 trips × 25 stops). Compaction within a lifecycle is **not** proposed: it is unsafe without knowing every in-flight operation's `start_seq` across tabs.

##### D-h — update-safety coordination matrix

- **Principles:** an operation that must not be interrupted by an application-controlled update takes an existing **operation hold** (`acquireHold()`) **before its first step** — before any network request — and releases it after its last required durable step and its user-visible outcome. If `acquireHold()` returns `null` (an update holds the gate), the operation is **refused before starting**, with "Unavailable while the app updates." (Q2 for sign-out). Once a hold is held, the gate cannot be acquired, so the update waits. Browser termination and externally initiated reloads cannot be prevented: correctness then relies on the durable ordering (every intermediate durable state is a blocking one) and on IndexedDB transaction atomicity. No change to `updateSafety` or the update controller.

  | Operation | Hold | Acquired | Gate check | If an update is in progress | Network | Durable commits | Follow-up | Released | Error / interruption | Unfinished intent protected |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Lifecycle creation | yes | before the session check | via `acquireHold` | deferred (retried at the next session check, not automatically on a timer) | session check | marker, sequence | — | after commit | nothing created | — |
  | Sign-out initiation | yes | on press, before step 2 | yes | refused with the updating reason | server sign-out | intent, marker removal, cleanup | server request, reporting | after step 9 | intermediate states block | the intent (durable) |
  | Intent persistence | (within sign-out) | — | — | — | — | intent | — | — | D22 escalation | yes |
  | Lifecycle invalidation (confirmed absence, account switch) | yes | when the session result is processed | yes | the in-memory block applies at once; if the gate is already held (no hold obtainable), the durable steps are deferred to the next startup evaluation and the deferral is disclosed (DR-5) | — | marker removal, cleanup | — | after commit | blocking states | — |
  | Cleanup | yes | before deletion | yes | refused (retry offered) | — | deletions, failure record | verification read | after verification | failure recorded | — |
  | Finish signing out | yes | on press | yes | refused | server sign-out | intent cleared on confirmation | — | after reporting | intent kept | yes |
  | Sign in again | yes | on press | yes | refused | sign-out, then sign-in | intent cleared; lifecycle created | — | after the outcome | credentials not sent if sign-out fails | yes |
  | Account switch | (as invalidation) | | | | | | | | | |
  | Delete all | yes | on confirm | yes | refused | — | deletion, verification, failure record | — | after verification | locked state recorded | intent preserved |
  | Save / refresh landmark or trip | yes | **before the request** | yes | refused | GET | snapshot; on authoritative unavailable: invalidation + propagation | propagation in the same commit | after commit and outcome | on interruption after the response but before commit: nothing stored — **an authoritative unavailable response not yet recorded is lost**; the next refresh re-learns it, and no protected content was written | — |
  | Remove saved landmark or trip | yes (brief) | on press | yes | refused | — | deletion record + removal (one tx) | — | after commit | atomic | — |
  | Authoritative invalidation propagation | within the save/refresh hold | — | — | — | — | one tx | — | — | escalation (OFF-FAIL-1) | — |

  *Note on the "refresh received unavailable before durable invalidation" case:* the hold prevents an application-controlled reload between the response and the commit. If the browser terminates in that window, no available content was written by that operation (the old snapshot remains, still eligible by the last recorded evidence); this is the accepted limit of OFF-EV-4 under termination and is disclosed.

##### Proposed Increment 3b subdivisions (each separately authorized; nothing user-visible; no application wiring)

- **3b-i — coordination and capability primitives.** *Purpose:* capability detection, the two locks with ordering/reentrancy guards, the notice channel, the tab security generation. *New production files:* `frontend/src/offline/capabilities.ts`, `frontend/src/offline/locks.ts`, `frontend/src/offline/notices.ts`, `frontend/src/offline/securityGeneration.ts`. *Existing file change (approval needed):* `frontend/src/offline/db.ts` — export `openWith` (Q13). *Tests:* `capabilities.test.ts`, `locks.test.ts` (with a deterministic in-memory Web Locks stand-in implementing shared/exclusive semantics, plus a guard test that the real API is used when present), `notices.test.ts` (BroadcastChannel stand-in; messages carry no identifiers), `securityGeneration.test.ts`, and a blocked-upgrade test in `db.test.ts`. *Invariants:* exclusive excludes shared; nested/reverse acquisition throws; no lock across awaits of network (structural: lock helpers accept storage callbacks only — documented); notices carry no identifiers; stale results are not publishable. *NCs:* exclusive granted while shared held; reverse order allowed; nested acquisition allowed; notice with an identifier accepted; publication after a generation change.
- **3b-ii — durable lifecycle and intent state.** *Purpose:* state evaluation (startup/focus/access), lifecycle create/continue/terminate, intent record/clear, marker removal, account-switch detection — as pure modules taking injected session results (no `AuthProvider` change). *Files:* `frontend/src/offline/lifecycle.ts`, `frontend/src/offline/lifecycle.test.ts`. *Invariants:* no lifecycle while intent/failure/D22/residual records; continuity on recheck; intent before marker removal; a matching cookie never clears an intent. *NCs:* lifecycle created with an intent present; new lifecycle on recheck; marker removed before the intent; intent cleared without confirmation.
- **3b-iii — cleanup, failure escalation, verified recovery.** *Purpose:* lifecycle cleanup with verification, Delete all, the OFF-FAIL-1 escalation, failure records, D22 escalation and verified clearing. *Files:* `frontend/src/offline/cleanup.ts`, `frontend/src/offline/recovery.ts`, tests `cleanup.test.ts`, `recovery.test.ts`. *Invariants:* Delete all never removes the intent; D22 set before removing the only intent evidence; D22 cleared only under the protocol and last; deletion never reported complete before success and verification. *NCs:* intent deleted by Delete all; D22 cleared on sign-in; cleanup reported complete without verification; failure not recorded; absence of D22 treated as recovery.
- **3b-iv — integrated security-boundary verification.** *Purpose:* cross-module deterministic race tests over `fake-indexeddb` with the lock stand-in and controlled ordering (deferred promises): authorization-to-read and authorization-to-commit races against transitions; stale publication; interrupted transitions resumed at the next evaluation; capability rows A–K; D22 escalation end to end; blocked deletion. *Files:* `frontend/src/offline/securityBoundary.test.ts` only. *NCs:* drop the shared lock from reads; drop the in-tx marker check; skip the generation check before publication; acquire the exclusive lock after (not before) writing the intent; treat an unreadable D22 as absent in the evaluator.
- 3c (authentication integration) and 3d (snapshot operations) are unchanged in scope.

##### Verification strategy

- *Deterministic (3b):* `fake-indexeddb` (fresh factory per test) for both databases; a **test-only in-memory Web Locks implementation** (shared/exclusive, `ifAvailable`, `AbortSignal`, release on callback settle) and a BroadcastChannel stand-in injected through the capability module (no production test hooks: injection is by constructor/parameter, as in 3a's `createSafetyLock`); a `Storage` stand-in for D22; deferred promises for every interleaving.
- *What `fake-indexeddb` and stand-ins cannot establish:* real Web Locks semantics across real tabs, BroadcastChannel delivery timing, real `blocked`/`versionchange` timing, quota and private-mode behavior, termination and freezing of tabs, `localStorage` behavior under storage pressure.
- *Real browser (at the 3c integration boundary, when the app is wired):* two pages in one context — real Web Locks exclusion, notices, focus revalidation, sign-out during another tab's read, blocked deletion with another tab open, D22 across reload, capability removal by test-only init scripts (Web Locks or BroadcastChannel deleted). Not before wiring: the running app is not connected to offline storage for testing.
- *Negative controls:* listed per subdivision above; each security-critical invariant has one direct, non-echoing assertion.

##### Risks, limitations, and decisions requiring approval

- **DR-1** — authentication without Web Locks (strict refusal vs. scoped offline-disable with a Specification 6 clarification). *This is the one potential conflict with an approved specification (OFF-OUT-7) and requires a disposition.*
- **DR-2** — the two-lock architecture (`tnle-auth` exclusive spanning requests; `tnle-offline-security` shared/exclusive, storage-only) and the ordering rule.
- **DR-3** — the tab security generation as the publication guard.
- **DR-4** — sign-out refused (not queued) while an update holds the gate, with the updating reason (Q2).
- **DR-5** — lifecycle invalidation from a session result when the gate is already held: in-memory block now, durable steps at the next startup evaluation (disclosed).
- **DR-6** — exporting `openWith` from `db.ts` for the Q13 blocked-upgrade test.
- **DR-7** — the D-d ordering model and lifecycle-long metadata retention.
- **DR-8** — the 3b-i to 3b-iv subdivision.
- *Limitations:* the window between the synchronous block and the durable intent (no durable evidence if the tab dies there); suspended tabs; `tnle-auth` held by a suspended tab delays other authentication operations; a refresh's unrecorded authoritative unavailability is lost on browser termination (no protected content written); real-browser verification of coordination only after 3c wiring.
- **Recommended first subdivision:** **3b-i** (coordination and capability primitives), after DR-2, DR-3, DR-6, and DR-8 — DR-1 can be decided before 3c, where authentication is integrated.

##### Increment 3b architecture dispositions and 3b-i preimplementation confirmation (2026-11-26) — confirmation PENDING REVIEW; nothing implemented

- **Accepted direction:** the 3b architecture, with the refinements below. **3b-i is authorized in principle**, subject to review of this confirmation; implementation has not begun.
- **DR-1 — conditional scoped fallback (approved in principle; specification wording pending approval):** ordinary online authentication without Web Locks is permitted **only** when the absence of any conflicting offline security state can be reliably established; otherwise the strict refusal applies.
  - *States distinguished by inspection:* offline functionality never established (neither database exists, D22 absent); an existing lifecycle (marker or residual records present); unresolved intent; durable failure record; D22 present; D22 unreadable; security state not inspectable (IndexedDB or `localStorage` error, inspection unsupported).
  - *Inspection without creating storage:* D22 via `safetyLock.read()`; each database via a **probe open without a version** whose `upgradeneeded` (meaning "does not exist") is answered by **aborting** the version-change transaction, so no database is created; an existing database is opened, its `marker`/`state` records read and validated, and closed. No deletion, no clearing.
  - *Permitted (absence established):* ordinary online sign-in, sign-out, and session checks with **in-tab serialization only** (no cross-tab serialization is claimed); offline lifecycle creation, snapshot access, and persistence disabled; the user is told offline copies are unavailable in this browser.
  - *Refused (conflicting state, or absence not established):* offline access blocked; authentication transitions that cannot be safely coordinated (sign-in, server sign-out, Finish signing out, Sign in again) refused with truthful capability/recovery feedback; intent and failure evidence preserved; no session restoration over unresolved local state; D22 never cleared; nothing deleted to enable authentication. Local in-memory blocking still applies.
  - *Cross-context analysis:* the fallback is used **only when `navigator.locks` is absent** (the API does not exist), not when it exists but a request fails — "present but failing" is treated as *coordination not established* (strict refusal), because another context of the same browser could still have working locks. Absence of the API is a property of the browser engine and version, so **every context sharing this profile's storage lacks it at the same time**; since offline state can be created only under a Web Lock, **no context can establish conflicting offline state while the fallback is in use**, and a point-in-time inspection is therefore sufficient *under this capability model*. The model's assumption (one engine version per profile at a time) is recorded; if it does not hold, the inspection is not claimed sufficient. *Between sessions:* a browser upgrade that adds Web Locks simply enables offline features; a downgrade that removes them finds any existing state through inspection and refuses. Each authentication operation in fallback mode re-inspects immediately before its server request.
  - **Proposed OFF-OUT-7 clarification (exact wording; the specification is not edited until approved).** Append to OFF-OUT-7:
    > *Clarification (M06-T03, approved <date>):* Where the browser does not provide the preferred cross-tab coordination facility at all, ordinary online sign-in, sign-out, and session checks remain available, serialized within the tab only, if and only if the application has reliably established — without creating or modifying offline storage — that no offline security state exists on this device: no account marker or records of any lifecycle, no sign-out intent, no durable failure record, and no safety lock (OFF-FAIL-5), with every one of these inspected successfully. In that case offline lifecycle creation and all offline-library access and persistence are disabled, and cross-tab serialization is not claimed. Where any such state exists, cannot be inspected, or the facility exists but cannot be used, the operations above that cannot be safely coordinated are not started (fail closed) and the reason is disclosed; existing offline security state is never deleted or cleared to enable authentication.
  - Authentication implementation remains in 3c.
- **DR-2 — lock architecture (approved):** `tnle-auth` (exclusive) and `tnle-offline-security` (shared for authorized reads and ordinary commits; exclusive for transitions, cleanup, and security-state changes); order `tnle-auth` before `tnle-offline-security` when nested; no security lock across network requests; cancellable waiting with truthful waiting feedback; no timeout-based release or stealing.
  - *Authentication-lock release boundary:* **sign-out** — `tnle-auth` is taken for the server step and held until the server outcome is processed (on confirmation: the intent is cleared under a brief nested exclusive security lock; on failure: the failure is recorded and reported) — then released. **Finish signing out** — same boundary. **Sign in again** — held across the sign-out request, its confirmation, the sign-in request, and the resulting lifecycle evaluation (nested brief security locks), released at the defined success or failure boundary. **Ordinary sign-in** — held across the sign-in request and the following session verification. The security lock is always released before any server request.
  - *Sign-out durable steps do not wait for `tnle-auth`:* the synchronous local block, the notice, and then the **exclusive security lock** (intent, marker removal, applicable cleanup) are performed **before** `tnle-auth` is requested — sequential, never nested, so the order rule holds. An in-flight sign-in elsewhere cannot defeat this: its completion must pass OFF-OUT-4 (an intent blocks restoration). This keeps the pre-durability interval independent of another tab's network request.
  - *Operation-scoped nesting detection:* every operation carries an explicit `LockScope` object (created per operation and passed to the lock helper); the scope records which locks **that operation** holds. Acquiring a lock already held by the same scope, or `tnle-auth` while the scope holds `tnle-offline-security`, throws a programming error. There is **no module-global held flag**: independent operations in the same tab have separate scopes and simply queue through Web Locks (for example two shared reads proceed together; a shared read and a transition queue in request order).
- **Immediate-blocking qualifications:** the initiating tab blocks synchronously, without any lock. Other tabs fall into three cases: (1) tabs that **receive the notice** block in memory when they process it (not guaranteed to precede their next read); (2) tabs that **acquire the shared lock before** the initiating tab's exclusive request is granted — including shared requests already queued ahead of it — can still read the pre-intent state and publish it (the notice may then remove it); (3) tabs whose shared request is granted **after** the exclusive transition see the durable intent and are refused. Web Locks grants requests in order, so once the exclusive request is queued, later shared requests wait behind it. The interval is minimised by requesting the exclusive lock in the same synchronous turn as the local block, with no network wait before it. *Not claimed:* that every other tab is blocked before its next read during the pre-durability interval. Termination before the intent is durable loses the sign-out initiation. No additional mechanism is proposed now; D22 is not repurposed as an intent flag.
- **DR-3 — publication boundary (generation primitive accepted; not the complete guarantee):** the identified interleaving (A reads under shared lock → releases → B terminates under exclusive → A has no notice yet → A publishes) is closed by moving the **final authorization check and the synchronous publication inside the shared-lock callback**: after the read transaction completes and while the shared lock is still held, A re-checks its generation and not-blocked status and **synchronously writes the result into the tab's offline view store** (an external store; React renders later from it). B's exclusive transition cannot start until that callback returns, so A's publication precedes B's termination; B's notice (or A's next revalidation) then removes it. *Distinctions:* reading (inside a transaction), returning a result (inside the callback), publishing (synchronous store write inside the callback), deferred React rendering (after the store write, outside the lock), already-displayed content in another tab (removed only when that tab processes a notice or revalidates; not instantaneous). The interleaving is added to the 3b-iv race tests; complete publication enforcement is accepted only with 3b-iv/3d.
- **DR-4 — update-gate refusal (approved):** a **new** sign-out is refused while the update gate is held, with truthful updating feedback; **nothing** is initiated (no local block, server request, or intent) when the refusal is reported. The Q2 control-level reason is implemented in 3c.
- **DR-5 — invalidation and interruption (approved, revised):** operation holds span the whole operation, from before the network request through required durable follow-up work. *New-operation refusal vs existing obligation:* the gate check refuses only **starting** an operation; once authoritative unavailable evidence has been received, the required invalidation is a security obligation and is **never deferred because of the update gate** — the operation's hold already prevents the gate from being acquired. *Unexpected conflict (fail closed):* if the hold is found missing or the gate held while an obligation is pending (a defect), the affected content is blocked in memory at once, the durable invalidation is still attempted, and failures escalate per OFF-FAIL-1 (including D22). *Termination limitation:* if the browser terminates after the response arrives but before the durable invalidation commits, the newly received authoritative evidence is lost and **an existing saved copy of the now-unavailable item may remain stored and readable after restart** until a later explicit refresh learns the evidence again. No automatic background refresh or retry is introduced. No `updateSafety` or update-controller change in 3b-i.
- **DR-6 — `openWith` export and tests (approved):** see 3b-i scope.
- **DR-7 — ordering and retention follow-ups (direction accepted; to be refined before 3d approval):**
  - *Available snapshot commit:* requires marker = the operation's lifecycle; the stored revision equal to the **base revision read at operation start** (or still absent if it was absent) — so of two overlapping available responses the first commit wins and the second is rejected and never overwrites the newer accepted copy; `invalidations[L].seq ≤ start_seq` for every landmark whose protected fields it writes (otherwise a trip stores that stop as unavailable and a landmark commit writes nothing); `deletions[item].seq ≤ start_seq`.
  - *Authoritative unavailable commit:* requires only marker = the operation's lifecycle — **no revision match** (unavailability wins over overlapping available responses); it increments the sequence, records the invalidation, replaces the landmark snapshot (if present) with a marker (revision + 1), and propagates to every trip containing the landmark (each trip's revision + 1, so an earlier-started trip commit then fails its revision check). If the landmark's own snapshot was deleted after the operation started, the invalidation and trip propagation still apply but no landmark marker is recreated.
  - *Explicit deletion:* no revision requirement (the user's intent); increments the sequence and records the deletion with the removal in one transaction.
  - *Subsequent explicit save:* requires the record to be absent at start and at commit, and `deletions[item].seq ≤ start_seq` (an operation started after the removal).
  - *Subsequent non-overlapping refresh:* `start_seq ≥ invalidations[L].seq` and the revision match; restores only the refreshed snapshot (OFF-EV-8).
  - *Trip-stop propagation:* part of the authoritative-unavailable transaction above.
  - *Retention reassessment:* invalidation records are keyed per landmark and therefore bounded by the size of the landmark dataset (hundreds to low thousands). **Deletion records for trips are not bounded by the 25-trip limit**: trip IDs accumulate across repeated create/save/remove cycles over a long lifecycle (each removal leaves one ~150-byte record; for example 10,000 removals ≈ 1.5 MB). Records are retained for the whole lifecycle (no compaction without a demonstrated-safe rule; no time-based expiry). *Resource failure:* a quota error while writing a deletion record aborts the removal transaction as a whole (nothing partially removed) and is reported as a storage error; cleanup of the lifecycle removes all metadata.
- **DR-8 — subdivisions (approved):** 3b-i to 3b-iv, each separately approved and accepted; authentication in 3c; snapshot operations in 3d; nothing user-facing in 3b.

###### 3b-i — exact proposed inventory

- **New production files (none imported by the application; nothing created on import):**
  - `frontend/src/offline/capabilities.ts` — capability detection distinguishing *API present* from *successful use*: Web Locks (presence; a probe `request` with `ifAvailable` on a private probe name, performed only when called), BroadcastChannel (presence; construct-and-close probe), IndexedDB (presence only; opening is `db.ts`), `localStorage` (via `safetyLock.read()`). Returns explicit results; injected environment for tests.

  - *Capabilities (`capabilities.ts`).* Five outcomes are kept distinct: `absent`, `present`, `operational` (an explicit probe used the API successfully), `use-failed`, and `denied` (access refused). `detectPresence` reads properties only. The explicit probes are: Web Locks, at most one `ifAvailable` exclusive request on the private name `tnle-capability-probe` with an immediately returning callback (a `null` grant still counts as operational; never queued; never touches `tnle-auth` or `tnle-offline-security`); BroadcastChannel, which constructs one probe channel and closes it at once without sending; and `localStorage`, a read-only `safetyLock.read()` where unreadable means `denied`. IndexedDB is presence-only, because a non-creating inspection is a DR-1 obligation for 3c. Nothing runs on import, and there is no startup integration.
  - *Locks (`locks.ts`).* `AUTH_LOCK = "tnle-auth"` is exclusive only. `SECURITY_LOCK = "tnle-offline-security"` is shared for authorized reads and commits and exclusive for transitions. `createLockScope()` gives one operation its held set, with no module-global state. `withLock(scope, name, mode, callback, options)` returns `done`, `unavailable` (no Web Locks, or access refused; the callback does not run), `not-acquired` (`ifAvailable`), `aborted` (cancelled while waiting), or `failed` (the request failed before entry). A callback error is rethrown after release. `LockOrderError` is thrown, before anything is requested, for `already-held`, `reverse-order` (`tnle-auth` while the scope holds the security lock), `auth-not-exclusive`, and `invalid-options` (`signal` together with `ifAvailable`).
  - *Lock ownership and cancellation.* Release belongs to the browser: the protected work is awaited inside the Web Locks callback, so the lock is held until that work settles, whether it succeeds, throws, or rejects. There is no custom release, timeout, or stealing. An abort while waiting removes the request, and the callback never runs. An abort after acquisition is ignored by Web Locks: it does not release; the callback receives the signal to stop cooperatively. `onState` reports `waiting`, then `acquired`, then `released`, and "waiting" never implies acquisition. `onLongWait` is a one-shot timer observation that never acquires, releases, or cancels, and throwing observers are contained.
  - *Notices (`notices.ts`).* The channel is `tnle-offline-notices`. The types are `lifecycle-ended`, `lifecycle-changed`, `lock-set`, `failure-changed`, `recovered`, and `state-changed`. `isValidNotice` accepts only an object with a plain or null prototype, exactly one own data property `type` (no getter, no symbol keys), and a known value. `open` returns `open`, `unavailable`, or `failed`; `post` constructs `{ type }` fresh and returns `sent`, `not-open`, `invalid`, or `failed`; `close` is idempotent. Notices are advisory only: never authorization, recovery, or permission to clear state. There is no persistence-based fallback.
  - *Security generation (`securityGeneration.ts`).* `block()` is synchronous: it sets the block and advances the generation, returning a token. `advance()` invalidates earlier snapshots. `isCurrent(snapshot)` is true only when not blocked and at the same generation. `unblockFor(token)` succeeds only for the current generation, so a stale operation cannot clear a newer block, and an earlier generation never authorizes a result after a newer block, even after unblocking. It is tab-local and in-memory, with no durable authorization, no cross-tab claim, no UI, and no connection to the application.

#### M06-T03 Increment 3b-ii — preimplementation plan (2026-11-26) — **approved 2026-11-26** (approvals 1–6 with qualifications; implementation record below)

The scope is the durable lifecycle and sign-out-intent mechanisms only. No implementation, tests, record-contract, specification, or ADR change was made during this planning.

##### DR-2 sign-out ordering — comparison

**Option A** acquires `tnle-auth` first, then records durable intent. **Option B** records durable intent under an exclusive `tnle-offline-security` lock, releases it, and then acquires `tnle-auth` for the server step.

| Concern | Option A: `tnle-auth`, then durable intent | Option B: intent under exclusive security lock, release, then `tnle-auth` |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-durability interruption window | The whole wait for `tnle-auth`, which is unbounded: it may sit behind a sign-in or session check waiting for a network timeout. If the tab closes in that window, nothing durable records the sign-out. A still-valid cookie then restores the session on the next load: a silent reversal of a user sign-out (contrary to the intent of OFF-OUT-1 "immediately" and OFF-OUT-4). | Only the wait for the exclusive security lock plus one state-database transaction. The security lock is never held across a network request, so the wait is bounded by local storage work. |
| Authentication serialization | Trivial: intent creation is ordered with every authentication operation. | Every server authentication step (sign-in, session check, server sign-out, Finish signing out, Sign in again) is still serialized under exclusive `tnle-auth`. Intent creation is **not** serialized with authentication, so every authentication operation needs a durable-state pre-check before sending and a post-check before publishing (below). |
| Existing authentication operations | Complete and may publish before the sign-out starts; the sign-out then invalidates them. | An operation already in flight cannot publish if the intent committed before its post-check (Case 1). If the post-check ran first, it is an ordinary "signed in, then signed out" sequence. |
| Server-session changes | The sign-out runs after the change and terminates the new session. | The same: the intent is device-wide, and the queued server sign-out terminates whatever session the browser cookie holds (Case 3). |
| Lifecycle creation and termination | An earlier sign-in may create a lifecycle that is terminated at once (churn, but safe). | No lifecycle can be created after the intent commits: creation re-reads the intent inside its own exclusive security-lock callback. |
| Durable intent preservation | Compare-and-clear under `tnle-auth` plus the security lock. | The same, and concurrent initiators **join** the existing intent rather than replacing it. |
| Cross-tab behavior | Other tabs learn nothing durable until `tnle-auth` is obtained. | Durable state changes within a bounded local wait, and the notice is posted while the exclusive lock is held, so readers re-reading under a shared lock queue behind the write. |
| Recovery | OFF-OUT-5 and OFF-OUT-6, unchanged. | The same. |
| Remaining limitations | The long reversal window. | Termination before the intent commits still loses the sign-out (bounded window; inherent, disclosed). The completion checks run only in this application's code, and their correctness in `AuthProvider` is verified in 3c. |

**Recommendation: Option B.** It shrinks the only window in which a user's sign-out can be silently reversed from "unbounded network wait" to "one local transaction." OFF-OUT-7 serialization of server operations is fully preserved: every server request still runs under exclusive `tnle-auth`. The added obligations (an authentication pre-check and post-check, join semantics, compare-and-clear) are local, deterministic, and testable in 3b-ii through the isolated interface.

The lock usage is **sequential, not nested**. Option B holds `tnle-offline-security` (exclusive), **releases it**, and only then requests `tnle-auth`. It never requests `tnle-auth` while holding the security lock: the prohibited reverse nesting, which `LockOrderError("reverse-order")` rejects, does not occur. Nested acquisition happens only in the permitted order: security inside `tnle-auth`.

##### Recommended sign-out sequence (Option B), mapped to OFF-OUT-1

1. `generation.block()`, synchronously: in-memory blocking of offline data and authenticated publication in this tab (OFF-OUT-1 step 1).
2. Acquire `tnle-offline-security` **exclusive**. Inside the callback:
   - post the `lifecycle-ended` notice (step 2; receivers re-reading under a shared lock queue behind this write);
   - read the intent:
     - absent → write `{ key: "signout_intent", schema_version: 1, pending: true, created_at }` and verify by read-back;
     - pending → **join** it (never overwrite);
     - invalid or unreadable → escalate;
   - remove the marker in a separate `tnle-offline-data` transaction, verified by read (step 3: two databases, so two transactions; the intent always comes first);
   - post `state-changed`;
   - release.

   If intent persistence fails, see Case 7.
3. Best-effort cleanup (step 4) — **3b-iii**.
4. Acquire `tnle-auth` **exclusive**. Inside it:
   - re-read under a nested **shared** security lock;
   - intent absent, or present with a different `created_at` from the token → the joined intent was already resolved: send no request;
   - otherwise send the server sign-out (step 5), with no security lock held during the request;
   - on confirmation, take a nested **exclusive** security lock and compare-and-clear the intent;
   - release.

   The server step is wired into `AuthProvider` in **3c**.

##### Authentication interleavings (Option B)

**Every authentication operation follows two rules:**
- **Pre-check:** after acquiring `tnle-auth`, and before sending credentials or a session check, read durable state under a nested shared security lock. An ordinary sign-in is refused while an intent, a failure record, D22, or an unreadable state exists; only Sign in again (OFF-OUT-6) may proceed.
- **Post-check:** before publishing any result or creating a lifecycle, re-read durable state **inside** the security-lock callback, and check that the operation's generation snapshot is still current (DR-3). Publication happens synchronously within that callback.

**Case 1 — existing sign-in.** Tab A holds `tnle-auth` and its sign-in request is in flight; Tab B commits the intent; A's response arrives.
- A's post-check sees the pending intent (or A's own generation is blocked by the notice). The response is **not published**.
- No session verification result is published, and no authenticated state is restored (OFF-OUT-4).
- **No lifecycle is created**: `confirmIdentity` refuses with `intent-pending`.
- The server session that A's sign-in may have created **remains** until B's server sign-out. The intent is device-wide, and the sign-out terminates the browser's cookie session whatever account it holds.
- A releases `tnle-auth`. B then acquires it, sees its own token still pending, sends the server sign-out, and on confirmation compare-and-clears the intent.
- A reports that the sign-in was superseded by a sign-out (wording in 3c).

**Case 2 — existing session verification.** A check that started before the intent returns afterwards. Its post-check sees the intent, so the result is discarded:
- no `verified_at` update, no lifecycle, no restored access;
- a **stale "no session" result does not confirm the intent either**.

Only a server operation sent **after** the intent was observed under `tnle-auth` may confirm it. This is a conservative reading of OFF-OUT-8 (see "Approvals required"); its cost is at most one redundant sign-out request.

**Case 3 — account change.** An earlier sign-in switches the server session from account A to account B before the queued sign-out runs.
- The pending intent is a **device-wide obligation to terminate this browser's server session**. This follows from §12.1 ("no session remains for this browser") and OFF-OUT-2 (the record has no account field).
- The intent is not discarded because the account changed, and **no lifecycle is created for B**.
- If the sign-in's post-check ran before the intent committed, B's sign-in was legitimately published. The account-switch rule (OFF-LIFE-8) then invalidated A's lifecycle, and the later intent terminates B's session and B's lifecycle, if one was created.
- *Ambiguity requiring approval:* the specification implies but does not state the device-wide reading. Interface wording that names the right account is a 3c matter.

**Case 4 — concurrent sign-out initiations.**
- The tabs **share one intent**: the second initiator joins and keeps the first `created_at` as its token. Neither can replace the other's evidence, because writes happen only when the intent is absent, under the exclusive lock.
- Duplicate server requests are avoided: whichever tab acquires `tnle-auth` first sends the request and compare-and-clears. The second, on acquiring `tnle-auth`, **must recheck** durable state. Absent, or a different `created_at`, means its intent was resolved: it sends nothing and reports the earlier confirmation.
- The resolution is sound because the intent is cleared only by a confirmed server sign-out (OFF-OUT-5, OFF-OUT-8) or by verified recovery (which itself requires confirmation or Sign in again, OFF-FAIL-5). "Delete all" never clears it (OFF-LIFE-9). Throughout, `tnle-auth` excludes any intervening sign-in.
- A newer initiation that arrives after an earlier confirmation creates a **new** intent. The obsolete completion cannot clear it: compare-and-clear requires an equal `created_at`, inside the exclusive lock, under `tnle-auth`.

**Case 5 — Sign in again during another tab's sign-out.**
- Sign in again holds `tnle-auth` throughout. Step 1 (finish sign-out) compare-and-clears the intent token it read under `tnle-auth`.
- If another tab initiates sign-out **before** step 1's clear, it joins that intent. Step 1's confirmation satisfies it (no session exists, and nothing can sign in meanwhile).
- If it initiates **after** step 1's clear, it creates a new intent. Sign in again's step-2 credential completion fails its post-check (`intent-pending`): no publication, no lifecycle. The new session is terminated by the queued sign-out.
- A credential success never bypasses a pending intent. D22 also stays in force: after Sign in again, online authentication may be published, but no lifecycle is created until verified recovery clears D22 (3b-iii).

**Case 6 — interrupted authentication (termination at each boundary).**

| Boundary | Durable evidence | Next startup | Required recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before durable intent | None (marker and cookie intact) | The session check can restore the session: **the sign-out is lost** | None possible. An inherent, disclosed limitation (bounded window under Option B) |
| After intent, before marker removal | Intent and marker | Pending intent ⇒ no session restoration; the marker's lifecycle is treated as invalid | Marker removal is re-run (idempotent `beginSignOut` continuation); then cleanup (3b-iii); then Finish signing out or Sign in again |
| After marker removal, before cleanup | Intent and residual records | Residual records are unreadable (no matching marker, OFF-LIFE-6); the library is locked | Cleanup (3b-iii); then Finish signing out |
| After cleanup, before the server request | Intent only | Blocked as above | Finish signing out (no automatic retry, OFF-OUT-3) |
| During the server request | Intent only; the outcome is **unknown** | Neither success nor failure is claimed | Finish signing out; or a startup session check started after the intent was observed under `tnle-auth` that confirms "no session" (OFF-OUT-8) |
| After server confirmation, before the intent clears | Intent only; the server session is in fact gone | The same as above | The same; the confirming operation then compare-and-clears |

**Case 7 — failure to persist intent.**
- The in-memory block (generation) is already in force. If the intent write or its read-back fails, or the security lock is unavailable or fails, the operation **escalates** to D22 (`safetyLock.set()`, a monotonic write that needs no coordination) and posts `lock-set` (OFF-FAIL-1 step 4).
- It then still attempts marker removal (protective: the lifecycle becomes durably unreadable) and proceeds to the server sign-out, the strongest remaining protection.
- **Blocked:** all offline-library access and lifecycle creation (D22, plus in memory), and authenticated publication in this tab (generation).
- **Guaranteed?**
  - D22 durable → conservative recovery after restart (OFF-FAIL-5). Clearing and recovery belong to 3b-iii.
  - D22 write fails as well → nothing survives termination (OFF-FAIL-4). The risk is disclosed, and a valid cookie may restore the session after reload.
- No failure record is written, because the state database that just failed is the same store. No new failure kind is proposed.

##### State distinctions (never conflated)

- **Verified server identity:** a validated server response naming an account, obtained under `tnle-auth`. It is an input to `confirmIdentity`, not a stored state.
- **Authenticated application state:** in-memory `AuthProvider` state (3c). It is published only after a successful post-check.
- **Offline lifecycle ownership:** a valid marker whose lifecycle matches. It is an offline-library selector, never proof of a session (§12.1).
- **Local blocking:** the generation block in this tab. It is in memory only and is not durable authorization (Q18).
- **Durable sign-out intent:** the `signout_intent` record. It is device-wide.
- **Confirmed server sign-out:** a successful server sign-out response, or a "no session" check sent after the intent was observed under `tnle-auth`. It is never inferred from cleanup or from an interrupted request.
- **Verified recovery:** 3b-iii only. It clears failure records and D22 after verified cleanup and confirmation. 3b-ii implements none of it.

##### Proposed 3b-ii contracts (accepted 3a records only; no field changes)

**`securityState.ts`**

`readSecurityState(deps)` runs under a **shared** security lock. It reads, in order:
1. D22 (`safetyLock.read()`);
2. state database: `signout_intent` and `failure`, validated;
3. data database: `marker` validated, plus a residual check — any record in `landmarks`, `trips`, `invalidations`, `deletions`, or a `meta` `sequence` that does not belong to the marker's lifecycle (any record at all when there is no marker), using counts and the `by_lifecycle` index in one read-only transaction.

It returns exactly one classification, in this precedence: `unreadable` (any read or validation failure, or an IndexedDB open failure) → `safety-lock` → `failure` (kind) → `intent-pending` (token = `created_at`) → `residual` → `lifecycle` (marker) → `none`. It never creates a database it did not find; in 3b-ii, opening uses the existing `open*` functions inside tests only, and the non-creating inspection is DR-1 (3c). It never writes.

**`lifecycle.ts`**

`confirmIdentity({ scope, accountId, snapshot }, deps)`:
- **Precondition:** `scope` holds `tnle-auth`. Otherwise it throws `LockOrderError`-style `requires-auth`.
- Takes an **exclusive** security lock (lifecycle transitions are exclusive). Inside the callback it:
  - re-reads the security state **inside** the lock (never a cached read);
  - checks `generation.isCurrent(snapshot)`;
  - re-reads D22 immediately before committing.
- Outcomes:
  - `refused` (`stale` | `unreadable` | `safety-lock` | `failure` | `intent-pending` | `residual`);
  - `reused` (same account: `verified_at` updated in the marker transaction; same `lifecycle_id`, OFF-LIFE-3);
  - `created` (state `none`: new `crypto.randomUUID()` lifecycle, marker written and verified by read);
  - `account-switch` (a different account: the old marker is removed and verified; the result is `cleanup-required`, and no new lifecycle is created while residual records remain, OFF-LIFE-8 and OFF-LIFE-9).
- Posts `lifecycle-changed` after a creation or switch commits.

`releaseLocalBlock({ token }, deps)`:
- Takes a **shared** security lock, re-reads the state, and calls `generation.unblockFor(token)` **only** when the state is `none` or a `lifecycle` consistent with the caller's verified identity, **and** the token is current (Q18).
- It is never called on generation possession alone.

**`signOutIntent.ts`**

`beginSignOut(deps)`:
- No `tnle-auth`; the precondition is that the scope holds **no** coordination lock.
- Runs steps 1–2 of the sequence above.
- Returns:
  - `{ intent: "recorded" | "joined", token, marker: "removed" | "absent" | "remove-failed" }`, or
  - `{ intent: "failed", escalation: SafetyLockWrite, marker: … }`.

`readIntentUnderAuth({ scope }, deps)`:
- **Precondition:** `tnle-auth` held.
- Takes a nested **shared** security lock and returns `{ pending: token } | { none } | { blocked: classification }` for the server step.

`completeServerSignOut({ scope, token }, deps)`:
- **Precondition:** `tnle-auth` held; called only after a confirmation obtained from a request sent after `readIntentUnderAuth`.
- Takes a nested **exclusive** security lock.
- If the stored `created_at === token`: delete, verify the absence by read, and return `cleared`. If absent: `already-resolved`. If different: `newer-intent-preserved` (never cleared). If unreadable: `unreadable` (nothing cleared).
- Posts `state-changed` after a clear.

`escalate(deps)`:
- The narrow failure-escalation boundary: `safetyLock.set()`, then post `lock-set`, and return the `SafetyLockWrite` result.
- It does **not** clear, retry, or record recovery. Full OFF-FAIL handling belongs to 3b-iii.

**Common to all three modules:**
- Dependencies are injected (coordinator, safety lock, generation, notices, opened databases or openers, clock, UUID source).
- Nothing runs on import.
- Results carry reason codes only, never record contents.
- No `AuthProvider`, UI, or startup integration.

##### Intent ownership and stale completion

The accepted fields (`pending: true`, `created_at`) are **sufficient**, and no new persisted identifier is proposed. `created_at`, read under `tnle-auth`, acts as the compare-and-clear token. It is safe given the lock discipline:
- a new intent is written only when none exists (join otherwise), under the exclusive lock;
- an intent is cleared only under `tnle-auth` plus the exclusive lock, after a confirmation obtained while holding `tnle-auth`;
- so while any `tnle-auth` holder runs its server step, the intent it read cannot be cleared and replaced by anyone else.

A millisecond `created_at` collision (an intent cleared and a new one created with the same timestamp) is **benign**. A holder that mistakes the new intent for its own sends a sign-out **after** that intent was created, which is exactly what the new intent requires. The new initiator then finds it resolved, which is correct for the same reason.

No contract amendment is requested. Validators unchanged: `validateStoredSignOutIntent`, `validateStoredMarker`, `validateStoredFailureRecord`.

##### Lifecycle creation rules (`confirmIdentity` outcomes)

| State at commit (read inside the exclusive lock) | Outcome |
|---|---|
| First verified authentication (`none`; no residual records) | `created` |
| Existing matching lifecycle | `reused`: `verified_at` updated; no new lifecycle (reloads, connectivity changes, and rechecks never create one) |
| Verified **different** account | `account-switch`: old marker removed; cleanup required (3b-iii); no creation while residual records exist |
| No verified session | `confirmIdentity` is not called. Invalidation by confirmed absence (OFF-OUT-8) is a 3c caller decision using `beginSignOut`-equivalent termination (to be confirmed in 3c planning) |
| Unresolved intent | `refused: intent-pending` |
| Durable failure record | `refused: failure` |
| D22 present or unreadable | `refused: safety-lock` / `refused: unreadable` |
| Explicit recovery | Creation is possible only after 3b-iii's verified recovery removes the blocking state; then the rules above apply |
| Verified account after "Delete all offline data" | The data database is gone, and the intent, failure record, and D22 are preserved (OFF-LIFE-9). `created` only if none of them exist; otherwise `refused` |
| Generation snapshot not current | `refused: stale` |

A server session existing is **never** by itself sufficient while any unresolved security state remains.

##### Lock and publication boundaries (3b-ii operations)

| Operation | Locks, in order | Durable checks / transactions | Generation | Notice | Failure behavior | Release |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `readSecurityState` | security **shared** (may be nested under `tnle-auth`) | D22, then a state read transaction, then a data read transaction | — | — | `unreadable` (fail closed) | Callback settles |
| `beginSignOut` | security **exclusive**, then **release**; never `tnle-auth` | Intent write and read-back (state transaction), then marker removal and read-back (data transaction) | `block()` **before** the lock request | `lifecycle-ended` after acquisition; `state-changed` after commit; `lock-set` on escalation | Escalate to D22; in-memory block kept | After the marker step |
| `readIntentUnderAuth` | `tnle-auth` held, then security **shared** | Intent read | — | — | `blocked` | Inner callback settles |
| `completeServerSignOut` | `tnle-auth` held, then security **exclusive** | Compare and delete, then verify by read (state transaction) | — | `state-changed` after a clear | Nothing cleared | Inner callback settles |
| `confirmIdentity` | `tnle-auth` held, then security **exclusive** | Full state read, `isCurrent`, D22 re-read, then the marker write or removal transaction | `isCurrent(snapshot)` inside the callback | `lifecycle-changed` after commit | `refused` | Inner callback settles |
| `releaseLocalBlock` | security **shared** | Full state read | `unblockFor(token)` inside the callback | — | Remains blocked | Callback settles |

The security lock is never held across a server request. 3b-ii performs no server request: the "server step" in tests is a deferred promise run under `tnle-auth` with no security lock held. The synchronous publication boundary for authenticated state is the post-check callback. In 3b-ii it is represented by the `confirmIdentity` and `releaseLocalBlock` results; publishing `AuthProvider` state there is 3c.

##### Approvals required (no change made)

1. **Option B** as the DR-2 sign-out ordering, including the pre-check and post-check rule for every authentication operation.
2. **Device-wide reading of the sign-out intent** (Case 3): an interpretation of §12.1 and OFF-OUT-2, not a specification change. The developer may instead require a specification clarification.
3. **Conservative confirmation rule:** only a server operation sent after the intent was observed under `tnle-auth` confirms it. A stale "no session" result does not (a narrower reading of OFF-OUT-8).
4. **OFF-OUT-1 step 3:** the intent and marker removal happen in two transactions (separate databases, accepted in 3a), with the intent always first. "Where possible" is taken to permit this.
5. **Case 7:** no failure record is written when the state database fails; escalation goes directly to D22, with no new failure kind.
6. **Account switch** removes the old marker in 3b-ii but defers record cleanup to 3b-iii.

No record-contract, specification, or ADR changes are requested.

  - `frontend/src/offline/lifecycle.ts` — `confirmIdentity` (create, reuse, account switch, refuse) and `releaseLocalBlock`.
  - `frontend/src/offline/signOutIntent.ts` — `beginSignOut`, `readIntentUnderAuth`, `completeServerSignOut`, and the narrow `escalate`.
- **New test files:** `frontend/src/offline/securityState.test.ts`, `lifecycle.test.ts`, `signOutIntent.test.ts`.
- **Modified file:** `frontend/src/offline/testSupport.ts` (test-only). It gains a fake-IndexedDB installation helper (the 3a pattern, without editing `db.test.ts`) and a storage failure-injection wrapper that fails a named transaction or read-back.
- **Not modified:** `records.ts`, `db.ts`, `locks.ts`, `notices.ts`, `securityGeneration.ts`, `safetyLock.ts`, `capabilities.ts`, `AuthProvider`, the startup path, the specification, and ADRs. Documentation: `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.
