##### Verification plan

Tests are deterministic, run on `fake-indexeddb` and `FakeLockManager`, and use synthetic UUIDs and non-echoing assertions.

| Area | Planned test |
|---|---|
| Verified lifecycle creation | Created and verified by read; a lifecycle UUID; `verified_at` |
| Existing lifecycle reuse | Same `lifecycle_id`; `verified_at` advanced; no new ID across repeated rechecks |
| Account mismatch | Old marker removed; `account-switch` / `cleanup-required`; no new marker while residual records exist |
| Unresolved intent prevents creation | `refused: intent-pending`; no marker written |
| D22 prevents creation | `refused: safety-lock` |
| Unreadable security state | D22 unreadable; an invalid intent or marker; an IndexedDB open failure → `unreadable` |
| Intent-first durable ordering | Failure injected at the marker step → the intent persists and the marker remains; failure injected at the intent step → D22 escalation, the marker is not removed first |
| Marker removal | Verified by read; idempotent when absent |
| Stale lifecycle rejection | Snapshot, then `block()`, then confirm → `refused: stale` |
| Concurrent lifecycle transitions | Two `confirmIdentity` calls under separate `tnle-auth` holders → one `created`, one `reused` (exactly one lifecycle) |
| Concurrent sign-out initiation | Two `beginSignOut` calls → one record, both tokens equal (join), never overwritten |
| Obsolete authentication completion | A synthetic sign-in holds `tnle-auth` with a deferred "response"; `beginSignOut` commits meanwhile; then `confirmIdentity` → `refused`, and no marker |
| Newer intent preservation | `completeServerSignOut` with an old token, after clear and recreate → `newer-intent-preserved` |
| Failure between durable steps | Each injected failure leaves exactly the Case 6 evidence |
| Local generation protection | `releaseLocalBlock` refuses while an intent, failure record, or D22 exists, even with the current token |
| Notification boundaries | Notices are posted only at the defined points, with `{type}` only, and never before the exclusive lock is acquired |
| Lock ownership and release | `requires-auth` preconditions; no security lock held while the synthetic server step runs; no reverse nesting; locks released on throw |

**Testable in 3b-ii** (through the isolated interface): Cases 1, 2, 4, and 5 as synthetic operations holding `tnle-auth` with deferred responses; Case 6 by failure injection; Case 7 by intent-write failure and D22-write failure; Case 3 only as "a different account under a pending intent → refused".

**3c only:** the real `AuthProvider` pre-check and post-check, Better Auth cookie behavior, server responses, interface wording and publication, startup checks, and real-browser cross-tab behavior. Synthetic tests are not claimed as authentication integration.

##### Negative-control plan

Each control will be confirmed applied, restored byte-identically, and followed by a build comparison, with non-echoing diagnostics.

- **N1** — `confirmIdentity` skips the intent check → lifecycle creation despite an unresolved intent.
- **N2** — `beginSignOut` removes the marker before writing the intent (order swapped) → the failure-injection test finds the marker removed without durable intent.
- **N3** — the generation `isCurrent` check is omitted in `confirmIdentity` → stale authorization.
- **N4** — `completeServerSignOut` clears without comparing the token → the newer intent is lost.
- **N5** — `confirmIdentity` uses a state read taken before awaiting the lock instead of re-reading inside it → missing revalidation (intent committed while waiting).
- **N6** — `confirmIdentity` takes the security lock **shared** instead of exclusive, or the `requires-auth` precondition is removed → incorrect lock ownership (the concurrent-creation test produces two lifecycles, or no precondition error).
- **N7** — `beginSignOut` overwrites an existing intent → join violated (the concurrent sign-out test).
- **N8** — `releaseLocalBlock` unblocks on token alone → Q18 violation.

##### Remaining risks and integration obligations

- **Accepted limitations carried forward:** the bounded pre-durability window (Case 6, first row); OFF-FAIL-4 when D22 also fails; device-wide termination of a session the user may not have known changed account (Case 3, wording in 3c).
- **Synthetic-test limits:** every 3b-ii test uses stand-ins. Real cross-tab grant order, IndexedDB durability, and termination behavior remain unverified, as do the authentication races until 3c.
- **Preserved, unchanged:**
  - the DR-1 obligations before 3c;
  - the DR-3 integrated publication verification in 3b-iv;
  - the DR-5 termination limitation (unresolved);
  - the DR-7 items before 3d;
  - all earlier release blockers (§9.8 sensitive-site policy);
  - the dependency findings (Q11);
  - the manual assistive-technology review (A2, M07-T03);
  - the outstanding CI verification (A3, at M06 closure);
  - M06-T04 **Deferred**.
- **Readiness:** the 3b-ii plan is ready for review. Implementation awaits explicit authorization and decisions on approvals 1–6.

#### M06-T03 Increment 3b-ii — durable lifecycle and sign-out intent: implemented and verified 2026-11-26; **accepted 2026-11-26** (Q19–Q23; see the acceptance record below)

Authorized 2026-11-26 ("Authorize M06-T03 Increment 3b-ii — Durable Lifecycle and Sign-out Intent only. Do not begin 3b-iii."). The 3b-ii preimplementation report and the 3b-i acceptance record were accepted. Nothing is connected to the application, and 3b-iii is not begun.

- **Decision dispositions (approved 2026-11-26):**
  1. **Option B** (intent first). The exclusive security lock establishes or joins the durable intent and invalidates the lifecycle, then is released before `tnle-auth` is requested. Nested acquisitions stay auth → security. Pre-checks and post-checks are approved. *Qualification:* the pre-durability window includes the security-lock wait, database access, and transaction completion. It is **not** claimed to be bounded or necessarily short.
  2. **Browser-session-wide termination obligation.** An unresolved intent applies to the application's current browser-associated server session, even if an earlier authentication operation changed the account. It implies nothing about other devices or browser profiles. The intent is never discarded because the account differs, and no replacement lifecycle is created while it exists. Truthful user-facing explanation is a 3c obligation.
  3. **Stricter OFF-OUT-8.** A no-session response initiated before the intent was observed under `tnle-auth` cannot confirm it. Clearing requires current intent ownership and a server confirmation.
  4. **Two databases, two transactions**, with the intent persisted or joined before ordinary marker removal. No cross-database atomicity is claimed. A remaining marker never overrides an unresolved intent. The intent survives a marker-removal failure, incomplete cleanup, an interrupted request, and an unconfirmed outcome.
  5. **Direct D22 escalation** when the intent cannot be established. The remaining durable invalidation steps are still attempted, and the obligation to attempt the server sign-out when safely coordinated is preserved. Durable intent is never reported when only D22 was established, and the server sign-out is never reported as confirmed before confirmation. *Qualification:* a set-only D22 write is **not** inherently safe against a concurrent D22 clearing; this is preserved as a 3b-iii requirement (below).
  6. **Account switch** invalidates and removes the previous marker in 3b-ii; full residual cleanup is 3b-iii. No replacement while residual records, an intent, failure evidence, D22, or an unreadable state remain. The absence of a marker is not proof of clean storage.
  - **Intent ownership:** `created_at` is provisionally accepted as the compare-and-clear token. Uniqueness is **not** assumed; correctness rests on lock ownership and the intent-transition rules, demonstrated with same-millisecond tests (below). No persisted field was added.
- **Exact changed-file inventory:**
  - New production: `frontend/src/offline/securityState.ts`, `lifecycle.ts`, `signOutIntent.ts`.
  - New tests: `securityState.test.ts` (12), `lifecycle.test.ts` (23), `signOutIntent.test.ts` (21).
  - Modified: `frontend/src/offline/testSupport.ts` (test-only), which gains `installFakeIndexedDb`, a `MemoryStorage` D22 stand-in with failure switches, `injectTransactionFailures`, `gateOpen`, a deterministic clock and lifecycle-ID source, and the `createOfflineTestWorld`/`createOfflineTestTab` wiring of these stand-ins into per-tab dependencies. Also modified: this file.
  - Unchanged, verified by hash against their accepted versions: `records.ts`, `db.ts`, `safetyLock.ts`, `locks.ts`, `notices.ts`, `securityGeneration.ts`, `capabilities.ts`. Also unchanged: the specification, ADRs, and `LandmarkSearch.tsx` (`C4511E4666E3DC4D`).
- **Implemented contracts:**
  - *`securityState.ts`:*
    - `inspectSecurityState(scope, deps)` must run inside a `tnle-offline-security` callback; it throws `OwnershipError("requires-security-lock")` otherwise. It reads D22, then the state database (intent and failure record, one read-only transaction), then the data database (marker and residual check, one read-only transaction). It returns the full `evidence` and a `primary` classification with the priority unreadable → safety-lock → failure → intent-pending → residual → lifecycle → none.
    - Malformed records (validated with the accepted 3a validators) and storage errors (open failure, a thrown transaction) are `unreadable`, never absent. Lower-priority evidence is always returned, and nothing is removed.
    - *Residual records:* any record in `landmarks`, `trips`, `invalidations`, or `deletions` not belonging to the marker's lifecycle (counts against the `by_lifecycle` index), a foreign or invalid `sequence`, or any unknown `meta` key; any record at all when there is no marker.
    - `runAuthOperation` holds exclusive `tnle-auth` and issues an `AuthTicket` (scope plus the generation snapshot at operation start), registered in a private `WeakSet` and revoked when the callback settles. `assertLiveTicket` rejects forged, structurally identical, or expired tickets. No caller-supplied boolean is accepted as proof of ownership.
    - `readSecurityState` reads under a shared lock, nested under a live ticket when one is given. `removeMarkerWithin` and `writeMarkerWithin` require a held security lock and verify by a separate read.
    - In 3b-ii the injected openers are the 3a `open*` functions, which create a v1 database when absent. Non-creating inspection remains a DR-1 obligation for 3c.
  - *`lifecycle.ts`:*
    - `confirmIdentity(ticket, accountId, deps)`: the post-check, with the following steps.
      1. Require a live ticket.
      2. Validate the isolated `accountId` input.
      3. Take an exclusive security lock nested under `tnle-auth`.
      4. Inspect freshly inside the lock.
      5. Check `isCurrent(snapshot)`.
      6. Run the account switch if the valid marker names another account: remove the marker, advance the generation, post `lifecycle-ended`, and return `account-switch` with `replacement: "blocked"`.
      7. If the state is `none`: re-read D22, then create a validated marker with a new lifecycle ID and verify it by read (`created`, `lifecycle-changed`).
      8. If the state is `lifecycle` (same account): re-read D22, then write the same marker with only `verified_at` changed (`reused`).
      9. Otherwise, `refused` with the primary classification. `stale`, `invalid-identity`, `coordination-unavailable`, and `write-failed` are also reported.
    - `releaseLocalBlock(token, deps)` takes a shared lock and inspects freshly. It calls `unblockFor(token)` only when the state is `none` or `lifecycle`; otherwise it returns `blocked` (Q18).
  - *`signOutIntent.ts`:*
    - `beginSignOut(deps)`, in order:
      1. `generation.block()` (synchronous).
      2. Take an exclusive security lock in a fresh scope (never `tnle-auth`).
      3. Post `lifecycle-ended`.
      4. Record the intent and verify it by read, or **join** a valid pending intent. A malformed stored intent is `unreadable` and is never overwritten.
      5. If the intent was not established, escalate inside the lock.
      6. Remove the marker.
      7. Post `state-changed` and release.

      The result reports `path` (ordinary or exceptional), `coordination`, `intent`, `escalation`, `marker`, and `durable { intent, safetyLock, markerInvalidated }`.
    - `readIntentUnderAuth(ticket)` takes a nested shared lock and returns an `IntentObservation` bound to the ticket and token.
    - `planQueuedSignOut(token, read)` returns `send` only for the same token, `resolved` for an absent or different token, and `blocked` for an unreadable or unavailable state.
    - `beginConfirmingRequest(observation)` must precede the server request, and only one is allowed per observation.
    - `completeServerSignOut(request, outcome)` requires an unconsumed request and a live ticket. A `not-confirmed` outcome preserves the intent. A `server-confirmed` outcome takes a nested exclusive lock and re-reads the intent: absent gives `already-resolved`; invalid gives `unreadable`; a different `created_at` gives `newer-intent-preserved`; an equal one is deleted and verified absent (`cleared`, `state-changed`). Only the intent is cleared: never D22, failure evidence, or residual records.
    - `escalate(deps)` sets D22 and posts `lock-set`. There is no clearing or recovery.
- **Intent ownership and compare-and-clear:**
  - A second sign-out joins; it never replaces the intent's identity or erases evidence.
  - Clearing requires a live `tnle-auth` ticket, an observation made under it, a confirming request begun under it, and a fresh re-read of the intent under the exclusive security lock.
  - A queued sign-out rechecks durable state under `tnle-auth` before sending, and an already-resolved intent causes no duplicate request.
  - Within a ticket's lifetime no other path can clear the intent, because clearing requires `tnle-auth`. Creation happens only when the intent is absent, so the observed intent cannot be cleared and replaced while a completion relies on it.
  - *Same-millisecond evidence (fixed clock):*
    - concurrent initiations record one intent and join it, with equal tokens;
    - after a clear and a same-millisecond re-creation, the obsolete request handle cannot be replayed (rejected);
    - a queued sign-out holding the colliding token sends a request that begins after the replacement was created (exactly what the replacement requires), and the replacement's own initiator then finds it resolved;
    - exactly 2 server requests for the 2 intents.

    Collisions do not undermine the protocol.
- **D22 set-versus-clear (3b-iii architecture requirement):**
  - In 3b-ii escalation happens inside the exclusive security-lock callback whenever the lock was acquired.
  - **Emergency escalation outside any lock** occurs only when the security lock is unavailable or fails. Then only D22 is set: no IndexedDB write is attempted, and the marker is `not-attempted`.
  - Because 3b-ii implements no D22 clearing, no set/clear race exists in the code yet. **Before 3b-iii approval** the design must establish that verified recovery cannot clear protection established by a newer security failure, including an emergency set made outside the lock. The fixed boolean D22 representation must not gain fields.
- **Lock and transaction boundaries (verified by lock-manager snapshots):**
  - `beginSignOut`: security **exclusive** only (no `tnle-auth`), released before any auth request.
  - `readIntentUnderAuth`: auth exclusive, then security **shared**.
  - The synthetic server step: auth exclusive only, with **no** security lock held.
  - `completeServerSignOut` and `confirmIdentity`: auth exclusive, then security **exclusive**.
  - `releaseLocalBlock` and `readSecurityState`: security **shared**.

  There is no reverse nesting. Protected work is awaited inside every callback, and locks are released on success and failure. Each database access is a separate transaction, with no cross-database atomicity claim.
- **Negative controls** (all mutations confirmed applied by hash; all three 3b-ii test files run for each; every file restored byte-identically and its hash verified; no sensitive values were planted, only synthetic UUIDs and timestamps):

  | Control | What was broken | Failed tests (of 56) | Designated detector |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | N1 | Creation despite an unresolved intent | 7 | Unresolved-intent refusal; remaining marker vs intent; revalidation while waiting; Cases 1, 3, 5 |

#### M06-T03 Increment 3b-iii — cleanup and recovery: preimplementation plan (2026-11-26) — **accepted 2026-11-26** (decisions 1–7 dispositioned; only 4 and 5 implemented, in 3b-iii-a below)

Planning only: no implementation, tests, record contracts, specification, or ADR changes.

##### Q21 — notification timing (analysis and proposed correction)

- **Delay:** yes. Because the notice is posted only after acquiring the exclusive security lock, other tabs' advisory blocking is delayed by any security-lock holder: a long cleanup, a blocked "Delete all" deletion (below), or queued readers. The in-tab block is unaffected (synchronous).
- **Is an immediate pre-durability notice needed?** It is desirable, not a durable guarantee. OFF-OUT-1 orders block → notify → durable record, and OFF-LIFE-7 asks for prompt cross-tab invalidation where supported. Delivery is advisory either way.
- **Does `lifecycle-ended` imply durable termination?** Its name could be read that way, and it is currently posted **before** the durable write. Nothing may infer durability from any notice: receivers always re-read durable state under a shared lock.
- **Proposed correction (smallest):**
  - Post `lifecycle-ended` **synchronously immediately after `generation.block()`, before requesting the lock**, then request the exclusive lock in the same synchronous turn.
  - Keep `state-changed` after the durable steps.
  - Document the semantics: `lifecycle-ended` = "a tab has begun ending the lifecycle: block locally and re-validate"; it never states that termination is durable. `state-changed` = "durable security state may have changed: re-validate".
  - Receiver rule (for 3b-iv and 3c): on any notice, block locally and re-validate under a shared lock. If a re-validation still sees a valid lifecycle, the cause is either (a) the initiating tab's exclusive request is still queued, or (b) the initiator terminated before persisting. Per the Web Locks specification's FIFO queue, the initiator's exclusive request, made in the same turn as the post, precedes any receiver's later shared request, so case (a) resolves to the committed state. Case (b) is the approved pre-durability limitation.
- **Alternative:** add a distinct `termination-started` notice type. This would change the accepted `notices.ts` contract and is not recommended unless the developer prefers explicit naming.
- **Notification failure:** `post` returning `not-open` or `failed` does not change the sequence. The durable steps proceed, and the outcome may be reported, but it is never treated as protection.
- **Verification boundary:** in `signOutIntent.test.ts`, the 3b-ii test "posts no notice and writes nothing until the exclusive lock is acquired" changes to "delivers `lifecycle-ended` while another tab holds the security lock, and writes nothing until acquisition". A new test asserts that the exclusive request is queued before any receiver's re-read (stand-in FIFO; the real-browser ordering is a 3c and real-browser obligation). Negative control: post moved back after acquisition → the delivery-while-held test fails.

##### Q22 — local unblocking and identity (proposed tightening)

- **Proposal:** `releaseLocalBlock` unblocks **only** when the fresh primary state is `none` (no marker, no residual records, no intent, no failure record, no D22). It no longer unblocks on `lifecycle`.
  - After sign-out and recovery the state is `none`, so a released tab can read **no** offline data: there is no marker, and OFF-LIFE-6 requires a matching marker.
  - A lifecycle can then exist only through `confirmIdentity` (verified identity, with the post-check).
  - Authenticated publication remains gated by the `confirmIdentity` post-check (3c).
  - So unblocking is necessary but never sufficient for any access.
- **Tests:**
  - *3b-iii-a:* `releaseLocalBlock` refuses while a valid marker exists.
  - *3b-iv:* a snapshot read or commit immediately after a release, without `confirmIdentity`, is refused; a view-store publication after a release without a current lifecycle is refused.
  - *3c:* `AuthProvider` never publishes authenticated state after a release unless `confirmIdentity` returned `created` or `reused` for the verified account.
- **Negative control:** `lifecycle` re-admitted to the permitted states → the marker-present refusal test fails.

##### D22 set-versus-clear — analysis and recommended protocol

- **The problem.** D22 is a fixed boolean in `localStorage`, which has no compare-and-set operation. A set while D22 is already present leaves no trace. So no recovery can distinguish "the lock it verified" from "a newer lock set afterwards", whether by re-reading, notices, or generations.
- **The 3b-ii hazard.** The emergency out-of-lock set (security lock unusable) is not ordered against a clear. Even coordinated sets have the same hazard if a recovery's evidence (for example, a server confirmation) predates a newer failure.
- **Conclusion.** Evidence-based clearing ("I verified the failure that caused this lock") **cannot be made safe** with the available primitives. That would need lock identity, a revision, or another persisted mechanism, none of which is approved.
- **Recommended protocol: predicate-based clearing.** D22 is cleared only when the system is in a state that discharges the obligations of **every** possible security failure, whatever its timing. This "fully discharged" state is checked at the moment of clearing.
  - **D-1 (server obligation):** the recovery runs inside one live `tnle-auth` ticket. A confirming server request (sign-out, or a session check returning "no session"), **begun under that ticket after the durable state was observed**, has been confirmed, and **no other authentication request has been made under the ticket since**. Because `tnle-auth` is held continuously from the confirmation to the clear, no session can exist for this browser at the moment of clearing, whenever a newer failure occurred.
  - **D-2 (local obligation):** inside one **exclusive** security-lock callback nested in that ticket:
    - the offline data database is verified to contain **no records at all**: no marker, sequence, or other `meta` key, and no `landmarks`, `trips`, `invalidations`, or `deletions` record;
    - the intent is absent or was just compare-and-cleared using this ticket's observation;
    - the failure record is absent or was just cleared under the same predicate.

    Every IndexedDB writer uses the exclusive or shared security lock: snapshot commits are shared, and the emergency path performs **no** IndexedDB write. So no record can appear between verification and the clear.
  - **D-3 (order inside the callback):** verify data emptiness (performing a full cleanup first if needed, then verifying by a separate read) → clear the intent → clear the failure record → **clear D22 last** with `clearAfterVerifiedRecovery()`, which removes it and verifies by reading.
  - **Why a newer set cannot lose protection:**
    - a newer failure **before** the clear has obligations (server session ended; no readable offline data) that D-1 and D-2 already discharge at the clearing instant;
    - a set **after** the clear makes D22 present again;
    - an out-of-lock set landing **between** the removal and its verifying read makes the read see "present", so the recovery reports `clear-failed` (truthful) and D22 stays.
  - **Ordinary coordinated setting:** inside the exclusive callback (3b-ii).
  - **Emergency uncoordinated setting:** unchanged from 3b-ii (D22 only, no IndexedDB write). It is safe under this protocol because clearing never relies on evidence that the emergency set could invalidate.
  - **Recovery ownership and concurrent recoveries:** a recovery is defined by its ticket. Two recoveries are serialized by `tnle-auth`. The second re-observes the state and finds it already clean, or newly dirty, and acts on that.
  - **Failed lock acquisition or storage access:** no clear. D22 remains, and recovery reports `unavailable` or `unreadable`.
  - **Suspension or termination:**
    - before the clear: D22 remains (restart protection);
    - after the clear, before the local unblock: the state is clean, and on restart the tab starts with an empty in-memory block — offline is empty and lifecycle creation still requires `confirmIdentity`;
    - after the unblock: as above.
  - **After a browser restart:** startup sees D22 and requires Finish signing out or Sign in again. Recovery repeats D-1 to D-3. Automatic or startup retry of the server request is never performed (OFF-OUT-3).
- **Costs and conflicts requiring approval:**
  - **(i)** D-2 requires **an empty data database**, which deletes every saved offline copy on the device. This is stricter than OFF-FAIL-5's "residual offline data is cleaned up". It is unavoidable with a content-free boolean that may stand for any failure, including an authoritative redaction (3d).
  - **(ii)** D-1 clears at the server-confirmation point, **before** any deliberate new sign-in. Of OFF-FAIL-5's two branches ("server sign-out confirmed **or** a deliberate new sign-in has completed"), only the first is used. Sign in again therefore runs its recovery between step 1 and step 2, within one ticket.
  - **(iii)** "No other authentication request under the ticket after the confirmation" is a **caller obligation** (3c). The module can enforce single use of the confirmation handle, but cannot observe network calls.
- **Conservative alternative:** refuse D22 clearing whenever the emergency path could have been active. This cannot be established (it is another context's private state), so it would make D22 permanent until the user clears site data. Not recommended.

##### Cleanup architecture

Common rules:
- Cleanup is local only and never confirms a server sign-out.
- It takes `tnle-offline-security` **exclusive** (no `tnle-auth`; never across a network request).
- Each data-database removal is **one readwrite transaction over all five data stores**, so it is all-or-nothing within that database.
- Every removal is verified by a separate read-only inspection.
- These are logical deletions: physical erasure is never claimed (OFF-FAIL-2).
- The **state database is never modified by cleanup**: the intent and failure records are preserved.
- D22 is never cleared by cleanup.
- Notices are posted after commit (`state-changed`), and on escalation (`failure-changed` or `lock-set`).

Two modes:
- **Residual cleanup (CL-R):** removes every record **not** owned by the current **valid** marker's lifecycle, judged by primary-key components (`[account_id, lifecycle_id, …]`), not by content. It also removes a foreign or invalid `sequence` and unknown `meta` keys. It keeps the marker and its own records. It applies only when the primary state is `residual` and there is no intent, failure record, or D22.
- **Full cleanup (CL-F):** removes **every** record in the data database, including the marker. It applies whenever the lifecycle is invalidated or any security condition exists (intent, failure record, D22), and in recovery (D-2).

| Operation | Lock | Local block | Durable precondition | Removed | Preserved | Verification | Failure escalation | Then permitted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| After sign-out (`beginSignOut`) | Security exclusive (separate acquisition after `beginSignOut`) | Already blocked | Intent pending (or D22 escalated) | CL-F | Intent, failure record, D22 | Fresh inspection: no data records | A failure record `{kind:"cleanup"}` if none exists (join otherwise); if that write fails, D22 inside the lock | Server step (3b-ii); Retry |
| Verified account switch | Security exclusive (after `confirmIdentity` returned `account-switch`) | Generation advanced (3b-ii) | Marker removed | CL-F (no valid marker remains) | State database, D22 | Emptiness check | As above | `confirmIdentity` (creation once `none`) |
| Residual records, no marker | Security exclusive | Caller blocks offline views | Primary `residual`; no security records | CL-F (no marker: everything is residual) | State database, D22 | Emptiness check | As above | Creation |
| Marker present with foreign records | Security exclusive | Library blocked (OFF-LIFE-9) | Primary `residual`, valid marker, no security records | CL-R | Marker and its own records | Residual check returns none | As above | Reuse |
| Interrupted termination (intent pending, marker survived) | Security exclusive | Blocked | Intent pending | CL-F (the marker never overrides the intent) | Intent | Emptiness check | As above | Server step or recovery |
| Failed authoritative invalidation (3d) | — | — | A failure record `{kind:"invalidation"}` or D22 | Only by recovery D-2 (CL-F) | — | — | — | Recovery |
| Explicit Retry cleanup | Security exclusive | Blocked | Any | CL-F if any security condition, else CL-R | As above | As above | As above | As above |
| Delete all offline data | See below | | | | | | | |

**Malformed or unreadable stores:**
- Malformed records in the data stores are removed by key like any other non-owned record. A malformed **marker** makes the state `unreadable`: normal cleanup refuses, and only explicit destructive recovery (Delete all, or CL-F inside recovery) removes it.
- Malformed **intent or failure records** (state database) are never touched by cleanup and never silently discarded (see "Verified recovery").
- An unreadable data database (open or transaction failure) means cleanup fails: escalate.

**Replacement authorization:** a replacement lifecycle is created only by `confirmIdentity` when the fresh state is `none`. An absent marker is never treated as clean: residual records block creation (3b-ii).

##### Durable failure records

- **When required:** a local security operation (cleanup, and in 3d invalidation) fails in a way that leaves residual or unknown state **and** the state database is writable. The record is written in the same exclusive callback.
- **Direct D22 instead:** when the state database cannot be written (the record cannot persist), or the intent itself failed (3b-ii, approval 5).
- **Existing record:** **preserved (joined)** — never replaced and never downgraded. The single `failure` key holds the first unresolved kind. This is sufficient because clearing (below) is predicate-based and does not depend on the kind; the kind is used only for disclosure.
- **Multiple failures:** they join the existing record. A failure-record persistence failure escalates to D22.
- **Survival of data-database deletion:** the record lives in `tnle-offline-state`, which Delete all does not touch (3a design).
- **Obsolete recovery cannot erase newer evidence:** all failure-record writes and clears happen under the exclusive security lock, so a clear's fresh predicate (an empty data database) is evaluated after any earlier write. The obligation of a newer failure that happened before the clear (residual local data) is discharged by that predicate.
- **When it may be cleared:** only inside a recovery (D-2), when the data database is verified empty. That holds for every kind; the `migration` kind is not produced before 3d or later. Failure-record clearing does **not** require D-1 (it is a local obligation only), but in the recovery sequence it precedes the D22 clear.
- **Record fields:** the accepted `{ key, schema_version, kind, recorded_at }` is **sufficient**, and no amendment is requested.

##### Delete all offline data (separate from sign-out)

1. `generation.block()` and post `lifecycle-ended` (per the Q21 correction). The lifecycle is terminated by deleting the database.
2. Take the security lock exclusive (no `tnle-auth` needed: it is local only).
3. Inspect the state database:
   - a pending intent, failure record, and D22 are **preserved, never read as permission**. The intent lives in `tnle-offline-state`, so deletion never removes "the only durable record of a pending intent", and OFF-LIFE-9's pre-deletion D22 set does not arise;
   - if the state database is unreadable, deletion may still proceed (it does not touch the state database). Recovery is then blocked as `unreadable`.
4. Request `deleteDatabase("tnle-offline-data")`. This module's connections are per operation and closed. Other tabs' 3a connections close on `versionchange` (`blocking` handler).
   - If `blocked` fires, report **deletion blocked** ("close the app's other tabs"). The request stays pending, and the lock is held until the request settles (proposal; see the limitation below).
5. Outcomes are reported separately:
   - **deletion requested**;
   - **deletion blocked**;
   - **deletion completed** (`success` event; `indexedDB.databases()` is used as corroboration only where supported);
   - **logical cleanup verified** (the next inspection finds zero records);
   - **security-state recovery verified** (only through recovery D-1 to D-3).
6. **No database is recreated to prove deletion.** Completion rests on the platform's `success` event. A later inspection opens the database, which with the 3a openers recreates an empty v1 database. That is permitted because inspection must read it, and a DR-1 non-creating inspection in 3c will see "absent" (equivalent to empty).
7. **Failure or interruption:**
   - `error` → report deletion failed, and record failure `{kind:"cleanup"}` (state database) or set D22;
   - termination after the request → the outcome is unknown, and the next inspection shows the actual state.
8. **Afterwards:** deletion never confirms a server sign-out and never authorizes clearing D22 or failure records alone. Lifecycle creation still requires `none` (an intent, failure record, or D22 blocks it), which means recovery.
- **Limitation (decision requested):** holding the exclusive lock while deletion is blocked delays every other security operation, including other tabs' `beginSignOut` durable steps; their in-memory block and notice are unaffected. The alternative — releasing the lock while the deletion stays pending — is safe for the data database (later opens queue behind the pending delete), but it lets `beginSignOut`'s marker removal wait inside its own lock hold. Recommendation: hold the lock, with disclosure.

##### Verified recovery: prerequisites and ordering

| Condition | Established by | Verified by |
|---|---|---|
| Cleanup completed | CL-R or CL-F commit | — |
| Residual records removed | — | Fresh inspection (residual check or emptiness) |
| Server sign-out confirmed | A confirming request begun under the ticket after observation (3b-ii approval 3) | Caller-supplied outcome bound to the handle (3c obtains it from the server) |
| Unresolved intent cleared | `completeServerSignOut` compare-and-clear | Read-back |
| Durable failure evidence resolved | Recovery D-2, with an empty data database | Read-back |
| D22 cleared | Recovery D-1 to D-3, last | `clearAfterVerifiedRecovery` read-back |
| Local block released | `releaseLocalBlock` (fresh state `none`, per Q22) | Generation token |
| Verified account identity | 3c (server response) through `confirmIdentity` | Post-check |
| Replacement lifecycle established | `confirmIdentity` → `created` | Marker read-back |

Recovery paths:
- **Finish signing out (intent pending, no failure record or D22):** a ticket, then observation, then a confirming request. Confirmed → the intent is compare-and-cleared (3b-ii) → CL-F is required before creation only if residual records exist.
- **D22 or failure record present (with or without an intent):** a ticket, then observation (a new recovery observation, including the intent's token or its absence, and a malformed intent captured as unreadable), then a confirming request. Confirmed → one exclusive callback runs D-2/D-3: CL-F and an emptiness check, the intent clear, the failure-record clear, then the D22 clear. Release the local block afterwards (shared, state `none`).
- **Sign in again:** the same as the D22 path for step 1, run inside the same ticket **before** the credentials are sent. Step 2 creates a lifecycle only through `confirmIdentity`.
- **Malformed intent record (decision requested):** OFF-OUT semantics make any intent a browser-session termination obligation. A server confirmation begun after the malformed record was observed under the ticket therefore discharges it. Propose deleting it only if its raw stored value still **deep-equals** the value captured (in memory) at observation. This is an explicit, server-confirmed recovery, not a silent discard. Without approval, a malformed intent stays and blocks indefinitely, with Delete all unable to clear it.
- **Preserved:**
  - no restoration over an unresolved intent;
  - no automatic retry;
  - nothing cleared because of a valid cookie (recovery requires a **no-session** or sign-out confirmation), because of database deletion, or because of generation possession;
  - ordinary sign-in is refused by the pre-check while any intent, failure record, D22, or unreadable state exists.

##### Joined intents and recovery interleavings

- **Two sign-outs joined:** cleanup may run from either tab (both exclusive, serialized); the second finds the database already empty. One server request (3b-ii).
- **Cleanup finishes before the server request:** the state is "intent pending, data empty". The server step then clears the intent, giving `none`.
- **Server confirmation before cleanup completes:** the intent is cleared (the server obligation is discharged). Residual records remain as durable evidence, so creation stays blocked until CL-F. Confirmation never erases cleanup obligations.
- **Cleanup failure after server confirmation:** a failure record `{cleanup}` (or D22). Recovery D-2 is required later, and D-1 needs a **new** confirmation under the recovery ticket. Cleanup success never implies server confirmation, and vice versa.
- **Queued sign-out finds its intent resolved:** `planQueuedSignOut` → `resolved` (3b-ii). Cleanup is still verified independently.
- **New sign-out during recovery:** its `beginSignOut` joins the observed intent (same token) or creates a **new** one after a clear. A new intent appearing inside the recovery's exclusive callback is impossible, because it is serialized behind it. A new intent after the callback blocks creation and needs its own server step. A recovery that observed "no intent" and finds one at D-2 **refuses** to clear D22 (strict approval 3).
- **New failure during recovery:**
  - coordinated → serialized before or after the D-2 callback: before means it is subsumed; after means it is present again;
  - emergency → subsumed (see the D22 analysis).
- **Sign in again with incomplete cleanup:** recovery D-2 performs CL-F; if CL-F fails → the failure record is preserved or written, D22 is not cleared, step 2 is not authorized to create a lifecycle, and online authentication publication is a 3c decision (lifecycle creation is refused regardless).
- **Account switch with residual records:** `account-switch`, then CL-F, then `created` on the next confirmation.
- **Delete all with an intent pending:** the data is deleted, the intent is preserved, and the state is "intent pending, empty". The server step is still required. Deletion does not confirm it.
- **Same-millisecond correctness:** unchanged. Recovery's intent clear uses the 3b-ii compare-and-clear bound to the ticket's observation.

##### Failure and interruption matrix

| Failure during | Remains blocked | Durable evidence | Restart protection | Explicit retry | Recovery permitted | Truthful report |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Security-lock acquisition | This tab (in memory) | Whatever existed | Only if it existed already (or the emergency D22 succeeded) | Yes | No | "Could not coordinate; nothing changed durably" |
| Auth-lock acquisition | Server step not started | Intent or D22 unchanged | As before | Yes (Finish signing out) | No | "Sign-out not sent" |
| Security-state inspection | The operation refuses | Unchanged | As before | Yes | No (`unreadable`) | "Security state unreadable" |
| Marker removal | Library (intent precedes) | Intent and marker | Yes (intent) | Yes (cleanup) | — | "Signed out on this device; cleanup incomplete" |
| Record deletion (CL) | Library | Residual plus failure record (or D22) | Yes, if a failure record or D22 persisted, or if residual is visible | Yes | No until fixed | "Cleanup failed" |
| Failure-record persistence | Library | D22 attempted | Only if D22 persisted | Yes | No | "Cleanup failed; protection recorded / not recorded" |
| D22 persistence | In-memory only (this tab) | Whatever IndexedDB holds | **No**, unless other evidence persisted (OFF-FAIL-4 disclosure) | Yes | No | "Could not record protection; closing may expose data" |
| Database deletion (error or blocked) | Library | Data database (partially) unknown; state database intact | Yes, if a failure record or D22 persisted | Yes | No | "Deletion blocked / failed" |
| Post-deletion verification | Library | Unknown emptiness | As before | Yes | No | "Deletion not verified" |
| Server-confirmation processing | Intent pending | Intent | Yes | Yes | No | "Server sign-out not confirmed" |
| Intent clearing | Intent present (clear-failed) | Intent | Yes | Yes | No | "Confirmed, but local record not cleared" |
| Failure-record clearing | Library | Failure record | Yes | Yes | No D22 clear (ordering) | "Recovery incomplete" |
| D22 clearing | All offline access | D22 (still present) | Yes | Yes | No | "Recovery incomplete" |
| Local unblocking | This tab blocked | State clean | n/a (state is `none`) | Yes | — | "Recovered; reload or retry" |

Termination at any point leaves only what was durably committed. Browser-termination limitations (OFF-FAIL-4, DR-5, the pre-durability window) are unchanged.

##### Specification or contract conflicts requiring approval

1. **Empty-database requirement for clearing D22 and failure records** (stricter than OFF-FAIL-5's "residual cleaned up"; it deletes all saved copies).
2. **D22 cleared at the server-confirmation point, before any new sign-in** (only OFF-FAIL-5's "server sign-out confirmed" branch is used).
3. **Server-confirmation recovery of a malformed intent** (deep-equal guard).
4. **Q21 notice move** (semantics defined; no type change), or alternatively a new notice type (a `notices.ts` contract change).
5. **Q22 tightening of `releaseLocalBlock`** to `none` only (changes accepted `lifecycle.ts` behavior).
6. **Delete all holds the exclusive lock while deletion is blocked.**
7. **Failure records are joined (the first kind is kept), never replaced.**

No persisted record contract, specification, or ADR change is requested.

##### Proposed implementation inventory and subdivision (recommended: three increments)

- **3b-iii-a — corrections (Q21, Q22):**
  - modify `frontend/src/offline/signOutIntent.ts` (move the notice post; document semantics) and `frontend/src/offline/lifecycle.ts` (`releaseLocalBlock` permits only `none`);
  - modify `signOutIntent.test.ts` and `lifecycle.test.ts` (updated timing test, FIFO-order test, marker-present refusal).

  Small and independently reviewable. It must precede 3c.
- **3b-iii-b — cleanup and Delete all:**
  - new `frontend/src/offline/cleanup.ts`: `cleanupResidual` (CL-R), `cleanupAll` (CL-F), `deleteAllOfflineData`, and `recordFailure` (join, or D22 on failure);
  - new `frontend/src/offline/cleanup.test.ts`;
  - modify `securityState.ts`, adding an in-memory `dataEmpty` evidence field (a code type, not a persisted contract);
  - modify `testSupport.ts`, adding a retained-connection helper for blocked deletion.

  It depends on `locks`, `notices`, `securityGeneration`, `safetyLock` (`set` only), `db`, and `records`.
- **3b-iii-c — verified recovery:**
  - new `frontend/src/offline/recovery.ts`: a recovery observation (intent token, absence, or malformed raw value), a confirming request, and `completeRecovery`, which runs D-2/D-3 in one exclusive callback and uses `safetyLock.clearAfterVerifiedRecovery()` for the first time;
  - new `recovery.test.ts`;
  - modify `signOutIntent.ts` to export its compare-and-clear helper for reuse (no behavior change).
- **Boundaries:**
  - **3b-iv:** snapshot reads and commits, the view store, and the DR-3 integrated publication test, including the Q22 read-after-release tests.
  - **3c:** `AuthProvider`, real server confirmations, the "no other request after confirmation" caller obligation, user-facing disclosure, startup, and DR-1.
- **Rationale for splitting:** the D22 protocol is self-contained, but it is the highest-risk change, and it is the first use of a D22 clear. Keeping it separate from cleanup lets each be reviewed and mutated independently.

##### Verification and negative-control plan

- **Deterministic tests (stand-ins):**
  - CL-R keeps the owner's records and removes foreign ones, including malformed content, an invalid sequence, and unknown meta keys;
  - CL-F empties the database, verified by read;
  - the intent and failure record are preserved through every cleanup and through Delete all;
  - a failing cleanup transaction writes a failure record (joined if one exists) or sets D22 when that write fails;
  - interrupted cleanup (an aborted transaction) is all-or-nothing;
  - blocked deletion with a retained raw connection reports "blocked" and completes after close;
  - successful deletion followed by verification;
  - D22 clearing refused when data remains, an intent is newer than the observation, the ticket is not live, or the confirmation is missing or not confirmed;
  - newer failure during recovery: a coordinated set before the D-2 callback, then cleared only with the predicate satisfied; an emergency out-of-lock set between the removal and the verifying read gives `clear-failed` with D22 present;
  - obsolete recovery completion (an expired ticket or a reused handle) is rejected;
  - a joined intent is preserved;
  - "server-confirmed, cleanup-incomplete" and "cleanup-complete, server-unconfirmed" are distinct states;
  - local unblocking only after recovery reaches `none`.
- **Requires real-browser verification:** Web Locks FIFO across real tabs (the Q21 ordering), real `deleteDatabase` blocking and `versionchange` timing, `localStorage` cross-context visibility, and termination behavior.
- **Proposed production negative controls:**
  - **R1** — D22 cleared without the emptiness check;
  - **R2** — D22 cleared before the failure record or intent (order);
  - **R3** — recovery not bound to a live ticket or confirmation;
  - **R4** — cleanup deletes the intent or failure record (state-database scope);
  - **R5** — a failure record is replaced instead of joined;
  - **R6** — CL-R removes owned records (wrong ownership predicate);
  - **R7** — Delete all reports completion on `blocked`;
  - **R8** — `clearAfterVerifiedRecovery`'s read-back is ignored (a recovery report of "cleared" while D22 is present);
  - **Q21-N** — the notice is posted after acquisition;
  - **Q22-N** — `lifecycle` is permitted for unblocking.

  Every control is a production mutation with byte-identical restoration and build comparison. No stand-in-only mutation is claimed as production detection.

##### Remaining risks and integration obligations

- **The D22 protocol's server leg depends on 3c honoring "no other authentication request after confirmation within the ticket".**
- **Emptying the database for D22 recovery deletes every account's saved copies (disclosure needed in 3c).**
- **A tokenless exceptional sign-out** (intent failed, lock usable) has no durable token for duplicate suppression. Whether its 3c server step sends unconditionally is a 3c decision. It could terminate a session established by a sign-in that started later (OFF-OUT-7 ignores the late result for interface purposes, but the request still terminates the session).
- **Blocked deletion holds the security lock.**
- **All 3b-iii evidence will come from stand-ins.**
- **Preserved:** DR-1 (before 3c), DR-3 (3b-iv), DR-5, DR-7 (before 3d), Q11–Q23, the §9.8 release blockers, the dependency findings, A2 and A3, the M07 follow-ups, and M06-T04 Deferred.

#### M06-T03 Increment 3b-iii-b — cleanup and Delete all: preimplementation refinement (2026-11-26) — **accepted 2026-11-26** (items 1–6 approved; implementation record below)

Planning only: no implementation, tests, record contracts, specification, or ADR changes. IndexedDB facts below come from the W3C IndexedDB 3.0 Editor's Draft (§2.1.1, §2.8.2, §4.3, §5.3) and MDN `deleteDatabase`, read 2026-11-26.

##### Q25 — surviving-marker correction

- **Defect:** `completeServerSignOut` (3b-ii) compare-and-clears the intent without examining the data database. If `beginSignOut`'s marker removal failed, the terminated lifecycle's marker survives the clearing. The state is then classified `lifecycle`, and the next `confirmIdentity` for that account **reuses** the terminated lifecycle (OFF-LIFE-2/5 violated).
- **Invariant:** clearing the sign-out intent must never make a terminated lifecycle eligible for reuse.
- **Recommended correction (the preferred ordering).** In `completeServerSignOut`, after the existing handle, ticket, and `server-confirmed` checks, inside the existing nested **exclusive** security callback (under the same live `tnle-auth` ticket; no network inside):
  1. Read the intent (read-only state transaction). If it is absent → `already-resolved`; malformed → `unreadable`; a different `created_at` → `newer-intent-preserved`. In each of these cases **nothing** is removed.
  2. `removeMarkerWithin` (data database), which verifies absence by a separate read. If removal or verification fails, return **`marker-remove-failed`**: the intent is **retained** and the server confirmation is reported separately ("server sign-out confirmed; local termination incomplete").
  3. Clear the intent: a readwrite state transaction re-reads it, compares the token again (defense in depth), and deletes it; then a read-back. A failure returns `clear-failed`, with the marker already absent (safe: intent pending, no marker).
  4. Post `state-changed`. Residual records, failure records, and D22 are **not** touched. Residual records keep blocking creation and release (`residual` classification).
- **Alternative considered:** refuse to clear while a marker remains, and require a separate cleanup. Rejected: the single-use confirming request would be consumed without effect, forcing a **second server request** for a purely local defect, and leaving one more interleaving window. The recommended fix is the smallest change (one helper call plus one result kind) and keeps the server confirmation useful.
- **Case outcomes:**

  | Case | Outcome |
  |---|---|
  | Server-confirmed with a surviving marker | Marker removed and verified, then intent cleared → state `none` or `residual` |
  | Marker removal fails during completion | Intent retained; `marker-remove-failed`; retry with Finish signing out (a new confirmation) or cleanup (CL-F removes the marker under an intent), then Finish signing out |
  | Verification fails after removal | As above (removal is reported only once verified) |
  | Intent clearing fails after marker removal | `clear-failed`; intent pending, no marker; retry |
  | Residual records after marker removal | Remain as durable evidence; creation and release refused until cleanup |
  | Failure-record or D22 persistence failure | Not involved: the retained intent is the durable protection. No escalation is needed on the completion path |
  | Concurrent joined sign-outs | Unchanged: one completion removes the marker and clears; the other's plan gives `resolved` |
  | Obsolete authentication completion | Unchanged: rejected before step 1 (ticket or handle) |
  | Same-millisecond ownership | Unchanged: the steps 1 and 3 comparisons run under the live ticket and exclusive lock |
  | Interruption between marker removal and intent clearing | Restart shows intent pending with no marker → Finish signing out (a new confirmation) → `cleared` |
  | Restart with a surviving marker and unresolved intent | `intent-pending` (the marker never overrides it); `confirmIdentity` refused; completion or cleanup removes the marker |
  | Explicit recovery after an earlier confirmation | The intent is still pending (it is never cleared without marker removal), so a new confirming request is required. Approval 3 is unchanged |
- **Files:** `signOutIntent.ts` (`completeServerSignOut` steps 1–3; `CompletionResult` gains `marker-remove-failed`) and `signOutIntent.test.ts`. No persisted field is added.

##### Revised cleanup contracts

- **Terms:**
  - **Ordinary cleanup:** removes only data whose lifecycle is not current or is already terminated.
  - **Explicit destructive cleanup:** removes a valid, non-terminated lifecycle. It requires an explicit `destructive: true` input; the user-facing authorization and disclosure (saved offline landmarks and trips in this browser's storage will be removed) are a 3c obligation.
  - **Delete all:** database deletion.
  - **Verified recovery (3b-iii-c):** the only operation that clears an intent, failure record, or D22 apart from the 3b-ii intent completion.
- **Common rules:**
  - The **exclusive** security lock is required, with no `tnle-auth`.
  - The operation fails closed if the lock is unusable; no uncoordinated IndexedDB write.
  - A data-database removal is **one readwrite transaction over all five data stores**, verified by a **separate** read-only inspection.
  - The state database is **never written by cleanup** except to record a failure (see "Failure-record ownership").
  - D22 is never cleared.
  - Deletion is logical; physical erasure is never claimed.
  - Notices go through the advisory guard: `state-changed` after commit, `failure-changed` or `lock-set` on escalation.
- **Residual cleanup (ordinary; `cleanupResidual`).** Preconditions:
  - the fresh state must be **fully readable** (state database included), with no intent, failure record, or D22;
  - the primary state must be `residual`.

  Otherwise it is refused, with the reason. Within the five data stores it **preserves**:
  - the valid marker;
  - every record whose primary key has the current owner's `[account_id, lifecycle_id]` prefix, *including malformed values*. Matching key ownership does not prove validity: such records stay unreadable copies, which reads must validate and list (OFF-SNAP-8, 3b-iv);
  - a valid sequence for the current lifecycle.

  It **removes**:
  - every record with a foreign `[account_id, lifecycle_id]` key prefix (valid or malformed);
  - a valid sequence for another lifecycle;
  - unknown `meta` keys.

  With **no marker**, every data record is residual, so residual cleanup removes everything. This is ordinary, because nothing is readable without a marker.
- **Refused for ordinary cleanup (explicit destructive cleanup only):**
  - **a malformed marker** (`unreadable`). Removing it is never ordinary cleanup, so cleanup never turns a malformed state into an apparently valid lifecycle;
  - **an invalid sequence while a valid marker exists.** Proposed classification change: `unreadable` instead of the current `residual`. Ownership of an invalid sequence cannot be established, and deleting the current lifecycle's ordering metadata could weaken OFF-EV-5 ordering in 3d;
  - **an unreadable state database:** whether the marker's lifecycle is terminated cannot be known, so ordinary cleanup refuses.
- **Full cleanup (`cleanupAll`).**
  1. Block locally where applicable (the caller's generation), then post the advisory notice.
  2. Take the security lock exclusive.
  3. Inspect fresh.
  4. One readwrite transaction clears all five data stores.
  5. A separate inspection verifies `dataEmpty` (new in-memory evidence: zero records in every data store and no `meta` key).
  6. Post `state-changed`.

  It is **ordinary** when there is no valid marker, or when the marker's lifecycle is terminated (an intent is pending, after sign-out). It is **destructive** (requires `destructive: true`) when a valid marker exists without a pending intent, including with D22 or a failure record present: D22 may stand for a redaction failure rather than a sign-out. Full cleanup proceeds even if the state database is unreadable, because removing data is always protective. The intent, failure record, and D22 are preserved.
- **Operation mapping:**
  - after sign-out (intent pending): ordinary full cleanup;
  - verified account switch (marker already removed): ordinary full cleanup;
  - residual records without a marker: residual cleanup (equivalent to full);
  - marker plus foreign records: residual cleanup;
  - interrupted termination (intent plus surviving marker): ordinary full cleanup;
  - failed invalidation (3d): destructive or recovery path only;
  - explicit Retry: the same selection rules, re-evaluated freshly.

##### Blocked database deletion (facts and design)

- **Spec facts:**
  - open and delete requests for one database are processed **strictly in order** (connection queue), and an `open()` after a pending deletion **waits until the deletion completes**;
  - the deletion sends `versionchange` to open connections, fires `blocked` if any remain, and **waits until all close**, with no timeout or abort;
  - there is **no way to cancel** an issued `deleteDatabase`;
  - when an execution context is destroyed its **connections are closed**, but what happens to a **pending delete request** whose requesting document is destroyed is **not specified** (the queue is processed "outside any specific browsing context");
  - `open()` with no version on a missing database creates an empty v1 database;
  - `databases()` returns only a "snapshot", with "no guarantees about the sequencing".
- **States reported:**
  - `requested` (the call was made);
  - `pending` (no result yet);
  - `blocked` (the `blocked` event: another connection is still open);
  - `completed` (**only** on the browser's `success` event);
  - `failed` (`error` event, or a thrown call);
  - `outcome-unknown` (the initiating context ended before an event; it is visible only on the next inspection).
- **`versionchange`:** every application connection is opened by the 3a `openWith`, which closes on `versionchange` and reports `onVersionChange`, so the operation using it drops in-memory data and fails or re-validates. The 3b modules open per operation and close.
- **A connection that never closes:**
  - the deletion stays pending;
  - the initiating tab **keeps the exclusive security lock** for as long as it lives and the request is outstanding. No timer releases it: the long-wait notice only reports;
  - every other security operation waits, with its own long-wait reporting;
  - the user is told to close the app's other tabs.

  This is fail-closed availability loss, accepted with disclosure.
- **User cancels the wait:** the user may dismiss the waiting UI. That cancels **only the wait**, never the deletion or the lock, and the operation keeps its lock until the request settles.
- **Initiating tab suspended:** the lock stays held (Web Locks) and the request stays queued. Other tabs wait. Behavior under bfcache or freezing is not specified by Web Locks and is a real-browser item.
- **Initiating tab terminated:** the browser releases its Web Lock independently. Whether the pending deletion then proceeds or is dropped is **not specified**. Conservative handling:
  - no application state assumes either outcome;
  - every later data-database access goes through `open()`, which the connection queue orders **after** any still-pending deletion. Later operations therefore cannot interleave with it: a write either precedes the deletion (and is deleted with the database) or follows it (on a fresh database);
  - deletion is atomic per database: the database exists or it does not, and there is no partially deleted state;
  - the next inspection classifies whatever actually exists (records remain → `residual` and others; deleted → empty);
  - nothing is ever reported as completed without the `success` event.
- **Subsequent inspection or opening:** it may wait behind a pending deletion. That wait happens inside a security-lock callback, so a pending deletion with a never-closing blocker stalls security operations until it resolves. This is fail-closed and reported through long-wait.
- **Deterministic (fake-indexeddb, needs confirmation by test):** `blocked` with a retained raw connection; completion after close; the security lock held throughout; `open()` queued behind the pending deletion; error and thrown-call paths through an injected deleter; completion never reported on `blocked`.
- **Real-browser only:** termination and suspension behavior of a pending deletion, eviction of frozen or bfcache pages holding connections, `databases()` accuracy, and cross-tab lock release on termination.

##### Delete all offline data (`deleteAllOfflineData`)

1. `generation.block()` (synchronous), then post `lifecycle-ended` (advisory, before any wait).
2. Take `tnle-offline-security` exclusive (a fresh scope; no `tnle-auth`). If unusable, refuse: nothing is deleted, the in-memory block stays, and the reason is reported.
3. Inspect the **state database** read-only. The intent, failure record, and D22 are recorded for reporting and **preserved**; they are never treated as permission. If the state database is unreadable, proceed (deletion never touches it) and report that recovery remains unavailable.
4. Hold no data connection, then call `deleteDatabase("tnle-offline-data")` through an injected deleter (the default resolves `indexedDB` at call time), with progress callbacks for `blocked`.
5. Await `success` (→ `completed`), `error` or a throw (→ `failed`, then the failure-record join or D22 escalation). Keep the lock until it settles.
6. Post `state-changed` and release.
7. The result reports separately: deletion (`completed`, `failed`, or `not-attempted`); whether `blocked` was observed; the preserved evidence (intent pending, failure present, D22 present, or unreadable); `serverSignOut: "not-implied"`; and `recovery: "not-authorized"`.

- No lifecycle is recreated and the local block is not lifted. `releaseLocalBlock` succeeds later only if the fresh state is completely clean (no intent, failure record, or D22).
- **Verification:** completion rests on the `success` event, and Delete all does **not** open or recreate the data database to prove it. "Logical cleanup verified" belongs to the next inspection. That inspection, with the 3a openers, recreates an empty v1 database, which is permitted because inspection must read it. The DR-1 non-creating inspection (before 3c) will instead report "absent", which is equivalent to empty.
- No persistent deletion marker or other coordination record is introduced.

##### Failure-record ownership and escalation

- **Required:** when a cleanup or deletion fails (transaction error, failed verification, or deletion `error`) and the state database is readable and writable. Written `{ key: "failure", schema_version: 1, kind: "cleanup", recorded_at }` inside the same exclusive callback, verified by read-back, followed by `failure-changed`.
- **An existing valid record is preserved (joined):** no write, and its kind is kept. The first reason is never treated as an exhaustive account; recovery must satisfy all unresolved obligations (3b-iii-c).
- **An existing malformed record:** preserved and never overwritten, with a D22 escalation, because the failure cannot be confirmed as recorded.
- **Direct D22** (`safetyLock.set()` inside the lock, `lock-set`): when the state database cannot be inspected or written, or when the read-back fails.
- **D22 also fails:** memory-only protection in this tab (generation block), with an OFF-FAIL-4 disclosure.
- **Durable evidence after partial cleanup or termination:**
  - any remaining residual records (they keep blocking: `residual`);
  - an unreadable data database (blocks: `unreadable`);
  - the failure record or D22 when written.

  The only memory-only outcome is: the cleanup failed, the failure record and D22 both failed, **and** the data database later reads as clean although the obligation was not met. That cannot occur for cleanup, whose obligation is exactly "no residual data", which the inspection measures. It remains possible only for obligations that are not measurable from storage (3d invalidation).
- No failure-record clearing in this increment. The D22 set-versus-clear questions remain for 3b-iii-c.

##### Verification and negative-control plan

- **Q25 tests:**
  - the intent persists when marker removal fails during completion (`marker-remove-failed`);
  - server confirmation does not make the old lifecycle current (the state after completion is `none` or `residual`, never `lifecycle`);
  - another tab cannot reuse the surviving marker: its `confirmIdentity` creates a **new** lifecycle ID, never the old one;
  - marker removal precedes intent clearing (gate: while the intent clear is paused, the marker is already absent);
  - a marker verification failure preserves the intent;
  - residual records keep blocking creation after completion;
  - an obsolete completion cannot remove newer evidence (an expired ticket or reused handle is rejected before any data-database access; the newer intent and the marker are untouched);
  - explicit later cleanup remains possible (CL-F after `marker-remove-failed`).
- **Cleanup and deletion tests:**
  - residual preservation of the current owner (including malformed values under owner keys) and removal of foreign records (valid and malformed);
  - a foreign sequence and unknown meta keys are removed;
  - refusal for a malformed marker, an invalid current-lifecycle sequence, an unreadable state database, or any security record;
  - full cleanup empties the database in one transaction, with verification by a separate read;
  - destructive gating (a valid non-terminated marker without `destructive` is refused);
  - the intent, failure record, and D22 are preserved by every operation;
  - a failed transaction joins an existing failure record, or writes one, or escalates to D22 (state database failing), or is memory-only (D22 also failing), each reported separately;
  - a verification failure (a store ignoring `clear()`) is reported as failed;
  - Delete all: `blocked` reported, then completion after the blocker closes; the lock held throughout; a never-settling deleter keeps the lock (with a long-wait report, no release); `error` and throw give `failed` plus escalation; no database is recreated by Delete all; a later `open()` waits behind a pending deletion; no lifecycle recreation; `serverSignOut: "not-implied"`.
- **Production negative controls:**
  - **Q25-N:** remove the marker-removal step from completion. Detected by the reuse test: the old lifecycle ID becomes eligible and is reused, and the marker is present after the intent was cleared.
  - **C1:** cleanup deletes the state-database intent or failure record. Detected by the preservation tests.
  - **C2:** a failure record is written unconditionally, replacing an existing one. Detected by the join test.
  - **C3:** the residual ownership predicate also removes current-owner records. Detected by the owner-preservation test.
  - **C4:** Delete all resolves `completed` on `blocked`. Detected by the blocked test.
  - **C5:** post-cleanup verification is omitted. Detected by the ignored-`clear()` test.

  Each control is a production mutation with byte-identical restoration, hash evidence, and a build comparison.

- **Q25 correction (`completeServerSignOut`):** after the live-ticket, single-use request, and `server-confirmed` checks, inside the nested **exclusive** security callback (no network):
  1. **Read and compare ownership** read-only. An absent, malformed, or unreadable intent, or a mismatched token, returns before the data database is touched.
  2. **Remove the surviving marker** with `removeMarkerWithin`, which never assumes validity, so a malformed marker is removed too, and verifies absence by a separate read. Failure → `{ kind: "marker-remove-failed", serverConfirmed: true }`, with the **intent retained**.
  3. **Re-read, compare again, clear, and verify** the intent. Failure → `{ kind: "clear-failed", marker }`, with the marker absent and the intent kept.
  4. **Post `state-changed`.** Residual records, failure records, and D22 are untouched.

  Success → `{ kind: "cleared", marker: "removed" | "absent" }`. The confirmed server sign-out is reported separately from incomplete local termination. **Invariant: clearing the intent never makes a terminated lifecycle eligible for reuse.**
- **Residual cleanup (`cleanupResidual`, ordinary):**
  - Exclusive security lock; only when the fresh primary state is `residual`. It is otherwise refused with the classification, removing nothing.
  - **Preserved:** the valid marker; every data-store record whose primary key has the current owner's `[account_id, lifecycle_id]` prefix, including **malformed** values (preserved does not mean valid; reads must validate, and a test confirms the preserved malformed copy still fails validation); the current lifecycle's valid sequence; current-lifecycle invalidation and deletion records.
  - **Removed:** foreign-owner records (valid or malformed) and a foreign sequence. With **no marker**, everything is removed, including an invalid sequence.
  - One transaction, then verification by a separate inspection (expected `lifecycle` with the same marker, or `none`).
  - **Refused (fail closed):** a malformed marker, an invalid sequence beside a valid marker, an unknown `meta` key, an unreadable state database, an intent, a failure record, D22, and nothing residual.
- **Unknown `meta` keys (clarified):** never removed by ordinary cleanup. They are now classified `unreadable` (metadata `invalid`) with or without a marker, because unrecognized keys are not provably disposable under the v1 schema. Only full cleanup removes them: ordinary full cleanup when no valid marker exists or the lifecycle is terminated, destructive otherwise. *This classification change goes beyond approved item 2 and is disclosed here for acceptance.*
- **Full cleanup (`cleanupAll`):** one readwrite transaction clears all five data stores (verified as a single readwrite transaction by the transaction log), followed by a separate inspection requiring the in-memory `dataEmpty`.
  - **Ordinary:** no valid marker, or a pending intent (the lifecycle is terminated).
  - **Destructive (`{ destructive: true }`):** a valid non-terminated lifecycle, or a malformed or unreadable marker. It blocks locally (synchronously) and posts `lifecycle-ended` before the lock request.
  - The intent, failure record, and D22 are preserved. Deletion is logical; physical erasure is never claimed.
  - Nothing performs destructive cleanup implicitly; nothing calls these modules from the application.
- **Security-state classification:** `SecurityEvidence` gains `metadata` (`valid`, `invalid`, or `unreadable`) and the in-memory `dataEmpty` (true only for a readable, record-free data database; never on a storage error). `inspectStateEvidence` reads D22 and the state database only, used by Delete all, which must not open the data database. `isOwnedKey` and `openDataDatabase` are exported helpers. No persisted field changed.
- **Delete all (`deleteAllOfflineData`):**
  1. Synchronous `generation.block()`.
  2. Advisory `lifecycle-ended`.
  3. Exclusive security lock (refusal → `not-attempted`, `coordination-unavailable`, and no deletion request).
  4. Inspection of D22 and the state database.
  5. **Unreadable-state safeguard:** if D22, the intent, or the failure record cannot be reliably read, D22 must be set and verified first (`path: "unreadable-state"`). If that fails → `not-attempted` (`protection-not-established`), with no deletion request.
  6. The data-database deletion request, through an injectable deleter (default `indexedDB.deleteDatabase`).
  7. Await the actual browser outcome while holding the lock.
  8. Report.
  9. `state-changed`.

  The result separates `deletion` (`completed` only on `success`, `failed`, or `not-attempted`), `blockedObserved`, the preserved evidence (D22, intent, failure), `serverSignOut: "not-implied"`, and `recovery: "not-authorized"`. The state database is never deleted; no lifecycle is created; the block is not lifted. The data database is **not** reopened or recreated to report success (only the state database remains listed after completion). Later verified storage state and verified security recovery are separate later outcomes.
- **Blocked deletion and termination:**
  - Progress is reported as `requested`, then `pending`, then `blocked`. None is completion, and `onProgress` observers cannot affect the operation.
  - The lock is held until the browser answers: no timer, cancellation, or forced release. A user cancelling a wait (an integration concern) would cancel only the wait.
  - A connection that never closes blocks indefinitely: a preserved limitation, with later guidance to close the app's other tabs.
  - **Termination:** the browser may release the Web Lock. That neither cancels nor proves the outcome of the pending deletion; the IndexedDB specification does not say what happens to it. Conservative handling relies on the specified connection-queue ordering (later opens wait behind a pending deletion). This does **not** by itself prove that existing connections, suspended contexts, or outstanding transactions are coordinated.
  - "Unknown" is a next-inspection outcome, not something the initiating context reports.
- **Failure-record ownership:**
  - On a cleanup or deletion failure, the local block is preserved and a `cleanup` failure record is written and verified by read-back (`failure-changed`).
  - An existing valid record is **joined** (preserved; it is not an exhaustive account).
  - A malformed existing record is preserved, with D22 escalation.
  - An unreadable or unwritable state database, or a failed read-back, leads to D22 escalation inside the lock.
  - The result reports `remaining` from a fresh inspection: `observed`; `durableBlocking` (true only for a readable D22, failure, intent, or residual state, never for an `unreadable` observation); and `failureRecordDurable` and `safetyLockDurable` separately. When the failure record and D22 both fail but residual records remain, the outcome is reported as durably blocked, not memory-only; an unreadable observation is never claimed as protection.
  - No failure-record clearing.
- **Deterministic verification:**
  - *Q25 (8):*
    - a surviving marker is removed and a **new** lifecycle is created, never a reuse of the terminated ID;
    - ordering (gate: marker absent while the intent clear is pending);
    - marker-removal failure retains the intent (the other tab refused `intent-pending`);
    - a verification failure (stale read-back) retains the intent;
    - an intent-clear failure is reported with the marker removed;
    - residual records block replacement until cleanup;
    - ordinary cleanup after `marker-remove-failed`, then completion;
    - an obsolete completion is rejected before any data-database open.

    The same-millisecond and ownership tests are unchanged and pass.
  - *Cleanup (19):* preservation and removal rules, refusals (7 cases plus an unreadable state database), failure recording (written, joined, preserved-malformed with D22, state-and-D22 failure reported separately, unreadable observation not durable), the single-transaction log, destructive gating, malformed-marker gating, separate verification, and lock unavailability.
  - *Delete all (8):*
